seeker: Hello

supporter: Hi how are you?
seeker: Im not doing very well at all. 

supporter: What's going on?
seeker: I am very stressed out with my work. 

seeker: I feel like I am being over worked but I also feel stuck at this job. 

supporter: I know the feeling. what do you do for work?
seeker: I am a lab assistant. 

supporter: how long have you been in your role? and do you have any coworkers that feel similar to you that you know about?
seeker: I have been in this role for about a year. I am the only one at this level. I take care of a lot of the productivity and logistical work. Im just really stressed recently

supporter: Somewhat similarly I'm in a supply chain role, for a year now, and the only one at my level too. I often feel like I'm alone in my job and that I manage my boss... It's pretty frustrating.
supporter: is there anything that makes your job less stressful?
seeker: I think that being able to have a better work life balance would help but I have a hard time talking to my boss. 

supporter: do you think your boss would be receptive if you did talk to them? or would they dismiss your concerns?
seeker: I am unsure. They are very much all about work. I am afraid they wont see my point and understand my want for a better work life balance. 

supporter: This has been a pretty hard year for everyone. however you ultimately gotta do whats best for you. 
supporter: Have you considered searching for a new job?
seeker: I have but it is hard to find a job at this time. I also really like what I do but wish I could have more balance. Do you have any advice for how to balance stress at work and your life outside of work?

supporter: I'm in the same boat. I would say, the things that work best for me, are to take breaks during my work day and go for walks or as soon as I'm done with work I force myself to go for a walk. I find moving helps me feel better. I also use that time to think about how I can look for a new job or rethink the things that are bothering me
supporter: maybe you can try something similar?
seeker: I think I could try that. I have a hard time detaching from work especially working from home. I feel like I never really 'leave' the office. I am always working even when I normally wouldnt be. 
supporter: Change the scenery, it'll help! plus movement releases endorphins which make you feel better. 
seeker: Thank you! I will try that. 

supporter: no problem!

seeker: I just don't know about that.  It's so much pressure to succeed.  The classes are so expensive and I can't fail.
supporter: It sounds like you are overwhelmed and want to come up with a plan to move forward.

supporter: I see that COVID-19 really changes the way we do things.  Is it possible to do a zoom study group or Facetime with friends?

supporter: Do you have other concerns?

seeker: I do worry still about the financial consequences of possible failure.  If I fail, then I have to retake the class and it is so expensive.  
supporter: I can see from chatting with you that this is a major stressor for anyone to undertake. 
seeker: Yes, I'm so concerned about having to pass but also how I will pay my bills if I don't pass and don't have a degree. I will have all this college debt and nothing to show for it.
supporter: I can see where that is a stressor.  I had to repeat a class once and pay for the housing, classes, and financial aspects. seeker: Wow that was very well said. I appreciate that.
supporter: Keep pressing forward and work toward your dreams because you can do it.  Just the way you contemplate things so much, I can tell that you really care and will make a difference to the world.
seeker: Thanks for the help. I feel much better.
supporter: You are very welcome.  
seeker: I think I'm going to go right now and set up a zoom meet with my friends to study.  You have given some inspiration to me.

seeker: I feel a bit lighter emotionally. Mending the rift with her feels like a burden lifted.
supporter: That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
seeker: It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.
supporter: That’s a positive step forward. You've been through a lot, and it’s important to take care of yourself too.
seeker: Trying my best. It’s a work in progress, you know? Balancing everything is tough.
supporter: Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.

seeker: Hello

supporter: Hello how are you doing today?
seeker: Somewhat stressed but otherwise ok. How about you?

supporter: I am great, it snowed and looks like Christmas here.  Why are you so stressed?
seeker: I'm developing romantic feelings for a friend but she doesn't share those feelings with me in return.
supporter: That is very hard to have feelings for someone who does not feel the same way.  I have been there myself.  
supporter: Have you tried to put distance between yourself and this friend?
seeker: Yes, I had received that advice from someone and tried it but it didn't help. We have been friends for a long time and I think it would be tough to smother these romantic feelings.
supporter: Have you thought about talking with this friend about these feelings?
seeker: I have but I'm sure she wouldn't react very well and it could damage our relationship. 

seeker: I'm also pretty sure she's already aware. She's pretty sharp.
supporter: Well maybe you should address these feelings with her in a very relaxed public atmosphere.  Just let her know that you really like her and you have realized that she has many of the qualities that you look for in a person to get serious with.  However, you treasure your friendship more than anything and you do not want anything to come in between your friendship....this way you have addressed your feelings, she knows how you feel and then should she decide to every take the friendship to the next step, she wouldn't feel awkward. 
seeker: That sounds like a good plan. I do like having things out in the open instead of holding them in. My other thought was to maybe try to seek out a romantic partner that isn't her so then maybe the feelings would go to another focus and it wouldn't damage our relatinship.

supporter: That sounds like a great idea.
supporter: Have you been dating other people much?
seeker: No, it has been difficult with the whole Corona virus thing. I have taken a large income hit and also I'm having trouble finding someone who wants to actually go do something.
supporter: Yes the Corona virus has really put a damper on all kinds of normal activities.  Have you thought about joining like a group with similar interests as yourself?  Maybe look for a local group that has a Facebook page and you can  start with building friendships just by chatting online or even on the public page itself.  Some of the best lasting relationships start out as friends with similar interests and then they blossom. 
seeker: I think I'll give that a try. I could use a new hobby anyways.

supporter: Sounds like a great plan, how are you feeling now?
seeker: I feel a lot better nwo that I have some options.
supporter: That's great, sometimes just being able to talk through things with someone else, really helps to get things in perspective and brainstorm some new ideas.  I am glad you are feeling better and hope that you have a great rest of your day.
seeker: Yes, thank you. And you also have a great day.
supporter: Good Bye

reading_text:

supporter: Hi. How are you doing today?

seeker: I can't believe it I just got layed off.

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It is a tough time right now for people working. Do you want to talk about it more?

seeker: I know. It's going to be nearly impossible to find something good now.

supporter: I understand that it is frustrating and scary to lose a job. But depending on what field you work in, there are actually quite a few places hiring right now because of the holidays. 
supporter: My boyfriend was laid off from his job and was able to get interviews with a handful of places in his area. Granted, they are not dream jobs, but at least it is a paycheck. 
seeker: I live in a small town. The mill is pretty much all we have that pays good.
supporter: Do you have access to any areas outside your town that are in driving distance or a bus can reach? 
seeker: I have my car. No bus's go through here.

supporter: Well if you have a car, maybe you would be able to find something a little outside your area that would pay more. Try taking a look on indeed.com or even craigslist for open positions. You may be surprised by what you find and a change in career can sometimes be a positive thing
seeker: I just got out of the Air Force. I really need a steady paycheck right now.
supporter: The only way you are going to be able to get a job is by looking what is out there. If you can work retail, it is a great time for that because of the holidays. Even if it is a temp position, at least it is something. 
seeker: And the holidays are just about here. This is going to suck.

supporter: It is a difficult time in general for a lot of people. I think most people are going to be understanding this year when it comes to gift giving. I wouldn't worry too much about that and instead focus on what you are able to do about the situation. 
seeker: This is the first time in 3 years i will be home for Christmas I was hoping to make for not being here.

supporter: Perhaps think of you just being home as the gift. Having time to spend with your family and friends is likely to mean more than something you can buy. 
seeker: My luck we won't be able to leave the house.

supporter: Then make it a great experience in the house. Make decorations and do holiday things. There is a lot people can do this time of year without going outside that is fun and meaningful. Try to be optimistic even in tough times. Sometimes it is all we can do to get by. 
seeker: I was thinking about learning how to make my own beer. Two birds one stone.

supporter: Yeah! That is a great idea. I know people that started doing that and ended up opening their own local brewery. You never know what could happen when you try new things!
seeker: That is true.

supporter: I hope I have been a little helpful for you today. It is tough right now but we can get through it. 
seeker: Thank you and have a great weekend.
supporter: You as well.

supporter: Hi! How are you doing today?

seeker: I'm ok I guess, but I'm pretty stressed out.
supporter: Can you tell me more about that?
seeker: I have a final exam tomorrow, and it has me really stressed out. If I don't get at least a B I'm not going to pass this class.
supporter: I can definitely understand why that would be stressful. Do you have anyone to help you study?
seeker: I do. There is a study group of people in my class. I am preparing really well but I've struggled with this class so much that I still get really worried.

supporter: It sounds like you are preparing well but are still worried that it won't be enough. Does that sound right?
seeker: Yes, that's right. I feel like I could literally study 24 hours a day and it won't be enough. It's hard to know if the information is really getting into my head, and if I'm actually understanding it all.

supporter: Sometimes taking a break and clearing your mind, taking a few deep breaths, can help people calm down. Is that something you can do?
seeker: I have tried that. And it does kind of help in the moment. It's when I get back to studying that all of the anxiety sets in. And it gets worse as it gets closer to the test. If I'm not studying, I feel guilty that I'm taking a break.

supporter: I understand that. I have felt the same way before. But I realized I don't have to feel guilty for taking a break. It's important for my mental health.
seeker: And I try to remember that, too. And I know that's right. But in the moment I feel guilty, so it's so hard for me to relax taking a break.

supporter: Just in the conversation I can see how stressed out you are and struggling with how to handle that.
seeker: Yes. Once my head is in this stressful mode, it's hard to break free.

supporter: Sometimes talking with a close friend can help. Have you tried that?
seeker: I have. And that does help in the moment. It's always when I get back into the actual studying that it's a problem. I think getting the test over with is the only thing that will help.

supporter: It sounds like the actual studying is what is causing you to be stressed. Does that seem to be true?
seeker: Yeah, definitely. I'm just worried about the test.

supporter: I think you have done everything you can to be prepared for the test. And know a few strategies to help you cope with your stress. I think you will feel much better once it's over!
seeker: I agree
\.
supporter: Ok! It sounds like this helped!
seeker: It did - thank you.

supporter: You're welcome.

seeker: Hello?

seeker: I do love my kids, but they are expecting some toys and stuff from Santa.

supporter: Would it be possible to look at some more home made stuff for this year that will still be fun and meaningful?
seeker: I cannot craft. If I made them something it would be so bad. 

supporter: I know it can be really hard to feel like you can't make anything worthwhile, but I'm sure theres something you could come up with that could still put a smile on your kids faces

seeker: Do you have any craft ideas?

supporter: Maybe you could look at involving your kids in the process. The feeling of doing something together as a family can make it way more fun. It could be a shared experience your family can look back on fondly later on.

supporter: I have seen some people make small ornaments filled with candies and treats and other small goodies. So even if all of the gifts feel small, they can feel like they are getting a lot of them. And you could even get them to have fun decorating and painting the ornaments!
supporter: Yeah, a box fort is really fun!
seeker: I never that about filling an ornament with small stuff. That's a great idea.
supporter: When I was a kid, I loved making box forts, and its a great way to reuse stuff you might already have around the house. The fun pretend games you can play were a blast. I'm sure your kids might love it too!
seeker: I could paint and decorate it. My daughters would like that. I can make it look like a castle. 

supporter: It can feel tough when it feels like you can't provide all the big gifts that you feel your kids deserve
supporter: But you clearly care and love your kids, and want to do something for them
seeker: I do. this has been very helpful. It's not all hopeless. 

supporter: Last Christmas when I gave gifts to my family, one of them later told me that the gift they loved the most was the box of Christmas cookies that they were able to enjoy over the course of the week afterwards, and not the keyboard I had gotten them. Sometimes it doesn't take something expensive to be meaningful and make someone happy

seeker: That sounds wonderful. I'm getting to work on my projects. Thank you.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. It still might feel tough, but truly things are not hopeless

seeker: Hey.

supporter: And he has always had cocky attitude? Have you ever told him that?

supporter: I understand your frustration, it's upsetting when they dismiss what you say even though you have been friends for so long.
seeker: Thanks.

supporter: What I would recommend in this case is, spend more time with other friends who appreciate you. You also need to tell Rick your honest thought, don't beat around the bush but let him know you're serious

supporter: I have been in the same situation myself, what I usually do is sit down with them and start the conversation in a serious mood. Explain everything I need to say and tell them that I mean every word. If they don't seem to accept and change, I keep my distance from them
seeker: Makes sense. Unfortunately we live on the same street so it's kind of hard not to run into each other. :/

supporter: That's even easier to make it clear, if you run into him, just give him a polite greetings. The point is, make it clear you have had enough

seeker: Right, so basically let him know if he continues to act like he does, we're done as friends, correct? Or should I not be that bold?

supporter: Yes. Be not too harsh at first. I would say to give him 1 more chance. If he still doesn't respect your words, it's the best for both to say it clearly.

seeker: Suggestions welcome! :)

supporter: You have the right mindset! Practice before talking will help you deliver your thoughts better.

supporter: I would start with something along the line "Look, I  know we have had this conversation many times. However, i feel as though you never take me seriously. I want to say this one last time...."

seeker: Seriously!

supporter: Getting emotional is totally fine, that's why you need practice
seeker: True it's just we've been friends for so long it would suck if we weren't anymore.

seeker: So I've got a plan and know what to do. You've been super helpful! Thanks!

supporter: I understand, it's difficult to come to this decision when you've been friends for so long. I hope he appreciates your friendship just as you do and tries his best.
seeker: We will see!

supporter: You're very welcome. is there anything I can do for you?
seeker: No, I think that's it!

seeker: Much appreciated!

supporter: I think you can end our session here. I'm glad I could help a bit
seeker: Yes, agreed, and yes you did!

seeker: Thanks again!

seeker: Hello

supporter: Hello! 

seeker: How are you?

supporter: I'm fine. How are you? Is there any issue I can help you with?
seeker: Yeah I'm really depressed. I just found out my buddy of 20 years is now posting that he believes Trump and that the election is being stolen from him. I thought I knew him but now I don't know.

supporter: That's a really tough thing to deal with. It can be hard to be confronted with a different, unexpected side from a trusted friend. 
seeker: And I had this guy as my best man for my wedding

supporter: Perhaps you can try reasoning with him. I'm certain that your judgement in friendships is not flawed and although he has made quite the yikes choice, he still has redeemable qualities. Especially if he wasn't making his political viewpoint known until recently. It leans towards the idea that with the right information, he'll understand that Trump is a big loser and he lost lmao
seeker: I tried but he says that he's sick and tired of Facebook and Twitter putting a muzzle on Trump and ever since he's been on Parler he now knows the truth

seeker: It's like he doesn't believe science anymore

supporter: Consider directing him to news sources that are not Twitter or Facebook, though I know this is hard to do. it is just a teensy bit funny he thinks that Trump is being muzzled on twitter when they are not deleting any of his tweets. 
seeker: Yeah he thinks it's wrong that Twitter is flagging his tweets and he's mad that Facebook are taking down these groups that he feels are telling the truth

supporter: This seems like a very sudden reaction from him, from what I've gathered, seeing as how it took you by surprise. Is there anything going on his life that may have put him into a negative mindset? Perhaps he's having problems in a relationship or at work that is leading him to rabbit holes on the internet.
seeker: He just got furloughed.

seeker: Maybe like 3 weeks ago

supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. He might be struggling with that and looking to shift his negative feelings onto another issue, one that has the support of many. It could be providing him comfort to be angry at the suppression of Twitter rather than coming to terms with his own turmoil. I think talking to him about his job status might be a start in reasoning his new outlook.
seeker: I dunno. How do you think I should approach him about that? He's sort of touchy about the whole subject.

supporter: Gently. It's never a good idea to press the issue, especially if it seems like he's trying to avoid it. 
seeker: Yeah, it just seems whenever I try to chat about anything it just ends up in an agrument.

supporter: Perhaps you should implore the help of somebody else in his life. I understand wanting to help your friend, especially when it's negatively impacting your own mental health, but there's only so much one person can do. You both deserve to be in a good head space and asking for help is okay. 
seeker: Yeah I guess you're right. I suppose I can talk to his wife about it but I'm not sure how to bring it up. 

supporter: I'm sure she might already be concerned as well. It might be easier than you expect. If he's consistently getting in arguments with you, it's likely that he's stuck in a negative haze and it might be affecting his other relationships. 
seeker: That's true but I don't want to make this more complicated that it should be. But I used to date his wife so I'm sure in his state of mind, how he would take it if it were the two of us bringing this up.

supporter: Try having a private conversation with her and don't ask her to talk to him, merely push her in that direction. It's less plotting and more seeing her point of view as well.
seeker: Ok I see, good point.

seeker: Anyway you gave me a lot to think about. I appreciate your help.

supporter: I'm glad to have given you some steps that may help you!

reading_text:

supporter: Hello, How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm scared about my future
supporter: Can you tell me more about why you are scared for the future?
seeker: I got fired because of Covid, and I don't know how I'll be able to find a job and have an income.
supporter: It seems that Covid has had a negative effect on your employment and financial insecurity is weighing heavily on you.
seeker: Yes that is correct, and with the job market, how am I supposed to find a secured job.
supporter: I can understand that feeling of insecurity, and how helpless you feel. I myself have been in the position of loss of income and financial insecurity in the past, and while it was hard while I was in the valley, I was able to walk out of it with some valuable lessons.
seeker: That is true, I just have to work hard for myself. I am learning valuable lessons like the idea that companies don't care about their workers, etc. Working more on myself sounds like the better option.
supporter: It sounds like you are already identifying areas of self improvement. A person with confidence in themselves and the ability to reflect and grow are promising attributes potential employers look for.
seeker: Thank you for all that you've done today, I couldn't get through it without you dude.
seeker: Thank you for your time today, hearing my concerns about the future!
supporter: You are so welcome. I know that you will succeed in your employment search as you have the skills and humility that potential employers are looking for.
seeker: I'll continue to keep on the lookout for new job opportunities, as well as improving myself for the long term. I appreciate it!
supporter: As you continue your job search, can you think of ways that you could trim your cost of living for the short term? Returning to the basics for a time could help save you money while you take the next steps with your career. Things like planning meals ahead of time, using items you already have instead of buying new, letting go of subscriptions you don't use daily or don't deem necessary.
seeker: I could definitely reduce my spending like going out less for fast food, cutting my Netflix and Hulu subscriptions, and prepare my own meals for the next week weeks, as I try to find a new job. This would definitely help with my concerns about income and financial security.
supporter: Our lifestyle seems to be all about convenience and instant gratification, I myself being guilty of wanting those as well. But I think when we strip our needs down to the basics for a while we allow ourselves to find what is really necessary, as well as what is truly important to us.
seeker: Very true, people definitely need to find their fitting for when things go wrong. Failure or bad events give us time to think about the important things in life, as well as our true needs.
supporter: And it is important to remember that everyone goes through cycles of feast or famine, and that when you are walking through a famine you yourself are not a failure. As long as you know you are doing your best to succeed under the circumstances you have been handed, you will never truly be a failure to yourself or to others.
seeker: Thank you, this has really helped me overcome my anxiety and fears of the events from the past year!
supporter: I am so glad you have been able to look within yourself to see that you have all the resources you need to handle this period of life. You have a optimistic attitude and a can do spirit, and those will take you far!
seeker: Thank you for your time, I'll have to be leaving now, this will help me for sure!
supporter: Enjoy the rest of your day!

supporter: Ok. Have you thought about a plan? When you tell your family, it may help to state your planned actions. This may help with feelings of uncertainty, both theirs and yours.

supporter: When I have been in a similar situation, I started reaching out to my network of friends and coworkers before I was let go.
seeker: Yea I just hate to do it today or tomorrow with it being Christmas. We do have a saving so that is good. But it will only last about 2 months.

supporter: I understand your feelings. The holidays are a joyous time. No place for uncertainty.
seeker: In my area yes. I can find some in bigger cities but I don't want to move.

seeker: Yes Christmas is my families favorite time for sure.

seeker: Thank you. So much for your help and kind words. You saved my Christmas spirt.

reading_text:

seeker: Hey, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?
supporter: Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?
seeker: I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?
seeker: Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.
supporter: Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?
seeker: We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.
supporter: It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?
seeker: Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.
supporter: Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.
seeker: That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?
supporter: That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?
seeker: I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.
supporter: It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.
seeker: I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.
supporter: Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.
seeker: That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.
supporter: It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?
seeker: It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.
supporter: That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?
seeker: Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.
supporter: It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.
seeker: Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.
supporter: Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.
seeker: Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out. Take care.
supporter: You too, take care.

supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?

supporter: Do you feel like you can't take any actions in the situation?
seeker: Long story short - at work, a new boss pulled all the leadership OUT of the jobs they were hired for (some more than 12 years ago - so they have lots of experience) and shuffled them all around to new jobs - all that is except the 5 oldest employees - they got moved into "non-positions". No longer supervising anyone, only doing grunt work, etc. It ticks me off and there's nothing I can do about it.

seeker: I'm working on a *possible* action - RETIREMENT from this job. Only problem is - bad time to be doing that; pressure to keep my income up until my daughter graduates college, etc.

supporter: That sounds frustrating, especially if you're one of the employees affected and when the new boss doesn't seem to know what he/she is doing with the reorganization.
supporter: That's positive, though, that you at least have a strategy in mind with retirement, even if this may not be the best time right now.
seeker: She has a "plan", I guess, but it isn't being articulated that well, and these actions are demonstrating poor "people management" and seem to be both confusing lots of folks, and professionally insulting many others. Oh, and by the way, things are running WORSE than they were before, but it's being blamed on COVID

seeker: Problem with the "retirement strategy" is that it means going out on a limb with no job with the holidays coming up, and with COVID with no end in sight. SO, just "muddling through" the days these days, hoping better times are ahead.

supporter: It sounds like you are not the only worker who is seriously questioning the changes being made. 
seeker: Oh, no. 1 person outright quit immediately. 1 other has retired already. 1 more I know is retiring by New Years. Others are more "stuck", as they just CAN'T afford to quit OR retire. So, yeah, us "old folk" are not "happy campers"

supporter: Wow! From what you've said, it sounds like your coworkers feel much as you do about the changes. 
seeker: Yep. We are sort of our own "support group", but since we are all 100% teleworking these days, we don't "see" each other, though we try to touch base through phone calls at least once a week.

supporter: That must be tough, but it must help to at least commiserate through the phone calls and be able to relate to each other.
seeker: Yep. Best I can hope for at this point. If I find another job to transition to, that would improve things. Until then, gotta just "keep on keeping on"

supporter: My former spouse works for a company that has moved him to departments he needed to retrain to work in, and he is considering looking for a different job, maybe after COVID is outta here.
supporter: It sounds like you're determined to stay as positive as possible while considering other options, such as a new job. Doing something about it like this must feel a little better.
seeker: As good as it can. Thanks for your time and commiseration. 
supporter: You're welcome! I also think that's wise to hold off on retirement until your daughter is through college. My oldest is ready for college and I don't feel ready to leave work, either. 
seeker: Yep, and she's actually a senior, so she'll graduate in May. But I gotta keep my motivation up until then. ;)

supporter: You can do it!
seeker: Thanks! I guess we'll see. Have a great evening.

supporter: You too! G'night.

supporter: Hello there!  how are you doing?

seeker: I'm doing OK.  Just stressed about work.

supporter: What's been going on lately?  Is something in particular there stressing you out?
seeker: Ever since Corona hit, my work has come to a complete stop.  I'm just so worried about where my next paycheck will come from.

supporter: Oh wow, that wounds really rough.  So you haven't been able to work in the same way since Corona?  Do you have any ideas of things you could do to make ends meet?
seeker: No, my work was through a hospital and they stopped my contract.  I've been looking but not many places are hiring.

supporter: Oh, I see.  That does sound really rough.  I would be feeling the exact same way you are in that situation and I'm sorry you're going through that.  I know this sounds cliche, but I do believe that things will work out.  I once heard, "It'll always work out in the end.  If it hasn't worked out, it's not the end."
seeker: Thank you.  I appreciate your support and words.  That's very true.  Things haven't worked out yet so I just need to hang on.  

supporter: I know there were some grants and loans and things specifically set aside for small businesses for the pandemic.  You might want to look into local resources and see if some are available to help you just to make ends meet for the time being?
seeker: Oh really?!  I didn't know that.  I'll have check that out.  It's so hard to know where to turn to or where to find that kind of information.  Is there a website or something?  Just knowing there might be something out there to help gives me so much hope.

supporter: There's so much information and disinformation out there, it can be really hard to discern help.  There's one website: sba.gov that has several different options for pandemic relief for small businesses.  I don't know what are you're in but there are some local resources available from my local government websites too, you might want to check that out too!
seeker: That is wonderful!  Thank you so much for passing along that information.  I've written the website down and I'll do some searching tonight!

seeker: Just talking to you has brought my anxiety level down so much!

supporter: Excellent, I hope you're able to find some relief through this difficult time!  I have a friend who looked into it and was able to find a small grant to help him out!
seeker: That's hopeful to hear!  Thank you!  Do you know if there's another stimulus check coming?  Those have helped me so much.  It's also amazing what a kind person, who really listens and wants to help,
 can do for your well being as well!
supporter: I have heard that another one is coming, and this one should be better than the last one.  It's all dependent on income, so anyone that makes less than 80k a year should be getting the full amount according to what I've heard.  I agree, they did help!  Would that ease your burden a little bit if the next one comes soon?
seeker: Great!  I will definitely qualify if that's the case.  I would be able to pay rent if we get this check soon.  It's been so hard making ends meet.  Sometimes I get so overwhelmed I feel like I can't breathe.  Any tips for that?
supporter: Hang in there, I'm sure help is on the way and your positive attitude will help carry you until then, you seem like a really strong person.  For me, I try taking really deep breaths and even meditating if it gets really bad.  Have you ever tried anything like that?
seeker: That's so kind of you to say.  I try to stay positive and be strong but I often feel like I'm failing.  It helps to hear words of support that I'm going to make it through this tough time.  I've never meditate before.  Do you listen to music or just silence.  I would love to give that a shot.  I try to take deep breaths.  Oftentimes it helps but only for a moment.  Maybe mediation could help me overall for longer periods of time.

supporter: You're not failing as long as you're still trying and not giving up.  All we can do sometimes is pick ourselves back up and keep plugging along.  There are a few apps available that have calming music, stories to listen to,  or even breath exercises to try.  They are all over the app stores.  It definitely helps me!  Meditation has been proven to help a lot of people in stressful situations.
seeker: That's so true!  I'm going to write that down and post it on my fridge!  Those are the words I'm going to live by for the next while.  I'll look up some apps!  Thank you for being such a great listener and supporter.  I feel so much lighter and hopeful.  I can't believe how much this has helped me.  I look forward to chatting again soon.  Thank you so much!  You have no idea how grateful I am to you right now.  I won't give up!
supporter: Of course, so happy to be of help!  Hopefully we can talk again soon and catch up on how you've been doing.  It helps me a lot to know I'm helping others too, any kind of service always feels nice.
seeker: Thanks again!  Have a great night!
supporter: Thank you, you too!

supporter: Hello my name is Sharon, how are you today? :)
seeker: Hi Sharon. Am good just concerned about my son.
supporter: Oh I see.  What's happening with your son?
seeker: I suspect my son is in bad company. His most recent behaviour is so different from what I am used to

supporter: Oh that's hard to deal with.   My daughter ran with a bad crowd for a while and I remember the deep worry.
supporter: What sort of behaviour are you noticing?  How old is he?
seeker: My son is 15. Recently he's keeping to himself and mostly stays locked in his room. He barely allows anyone in.
supporter: And when you try and talk to him about it what does he say?
seeker: He says he's studying online. But I suspect he's doing other stuff online apart from study
supporter: Oh I see.  Apart from isolating how is he doing otherwise, like at school?  Is he still seeing his friends at all?
supporter: It can be scary not knowing what our kids are up to online.
seeker: Not really. He just has this one particular friend who comes over sometimes and they lock themselves in the room.
supporter: Hmm.  So a lot of mystery.   I can understand you being worried.   Is he your only child?
seeker: I am so scared I don't want to confront him I have always tried to show him how much I trust him as away to make him feel responsible enough
seeker: Yes. He is my only child and I am single parent 
supporter: Thats good parenting!   Perhaps if you frame it as being about you, e.g. "I am getting really worried, can you please explain....it's affecting me (affecting my sleep/work/whatever" .... maybe it will inspire him to be more forthcoming
supporter: Any signs of depression?   I have been depresed before, and self-isolating can be a symptom, I've been there...
seeker: Never thought of it that way. That could be a possibility. But he always seems happy and we chat a lot onlythat he his behind closed doors in his room for a long time everyday.

seeker: Am also concerned about the friend who comes over. I don't really know his family or home just that he's from the neighborhood and they go to the same school.
supporter: Hmm.  My other thought is tell him what you just told me, that you have been trying to show him that you trust him....but be honest and tell him you are afraid.   Hopefully, he won't want you feeling that way, and will open up a bit.
supporter: Yes I can see that being concerning when you know nothing about the friend.   Yet you walk a fine line because he needs the freedom and autonomy to choose his friends without explanation required...it's such a balancing act.   I can tell you that I have raised a daughter, and that teen years were tougher than toddlerhood.   Lots of worry, but she came through it and is fine now.
supporter: I wonder if there is a teacher he is close to that you could bring your concerns to, perhaps the teacher may have some insight about yoru son to offer?
seeker: I find reassurance from your words. Its been tough for me this far we have come with my son and I want us to be close even as he growing up to become a young man. I have a good relationship with their teacher and will definitely give her a friendly call to know more from her.
supporter: Oh good.   And it may be just a normal part of his development.   Teens pull away from parents, peer group becomes far more important.  It may be as simple as that.
supporter: It took my daughter about 15 years to "come back to me" and now we have a close relationship again....so even if he seems to be drifting away know that it's normal and that will change in the future.
seeker: Good to know that from an experienced parent. I will try communicate my worries and my intensions to him. I hope he will understand and not pull away.
supporter: And in the meantime remember to take extra good care of yourself :)   Sometimes as moms we forget to do special things for ourselves.   You are doing the hardest and most imporant job in the world so it's important to recognize that and reward yourself for it.   I hope that conversation goes well for you, that you will have with him.
seeker: Thank you for your time and experienced advise.
supporter: Oh you're so welcome, it's been a pleasure speaking with you.
seeker: The pleasure was all mine. Bye.

seeker: I don't know what do with my life. 

supporter: I know sometimes it can be difficult to make decisions. What dilemma are you facing today?

supporter: I too, have been in your place. There were days I would just stare blankly without being productive. However, I tried meditating which helped me improve my focus.  
seeker: Does that really help? How do you start?

supporter: I am glad you asked. At first, it can seem a little difficult. But the key is to start small and build as you go. For example, allocating 10 minutes after lunch or borrowing some time off of social media.
seeker: What exactly do you? How can it help me make decisions without getting anxious?

supporter: It sounds as if you are low on self-confidence and are afraid about unfavourable outcomes. Please correct me if I am wrong.

supporter: I can feel your anxiety just through this chat conversation.
seeker: I tend to expect the worse or nothing at all. 

supporter: In my experience, even if we were to fail, we are bestowed with a valuable life lesson which we can use in future decisions.  Approaching the problem with positive mindset will help a lot! Is that something you'd be willing to try?
seeker: I suppose so, but it's hard to break habits and a mindset that I've cultivated. 

supporter: That's true. However, research shows that any habit can be broken or formed if you put your mind to it everyday for 5-10 minutes for 3 continuous weeks. Perhaps, replacing your negative thoughts with happy ones might help.
seeker: I guess it's a start. I can do three weeks, and hopefully move on from there. 

supporter: Awesome. I am glad I was able to get you started towards a positive mentality. Is there anything else that I can assist you with today?
seeker: That's all for now. Thanks for listening. 

supporter: You're welcome! Have a wonderful week ahead!

Complete past session (original utterances; not verified world facts):
supporter: Hey Anna, how have you been? I remember you mentioned some issues with John. Want to talk about it?
seeker: Hey! Thanks for reaching out. Things have been a bit rough to be honest.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Was it another disagreement with John?
seeker: Yeah, we argued again. It feels like he just doesn't care about how I'm feeling.
supporter: That sounds really tough, Anna. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: We were talking about our weekend plans, and I tried to explain that I'm feeling stressed, especially with everything going on. He just ... brushed it off. It hurt because I need him to understand.
supporter: It must be painful when someone you care about doesn't seem to listen to your needs. What did you expect from him?
seeker: I guess I wanted him to acknowledge my feelings and maybe offer some comfort. But he just seemed annoyed.
supporter: It's normal to need validation and empathy from a partner. Have you tried talking to him about how his reactions make you feel?
seeker: I tried, but sometimes it feels like he's dismissive. Like when I mention the stress from school or family stuff, he tells me to just 'deal with it'.
supporter: That must be frustrating. Given everything you've gone through - your friend Lily moving, your parents, and school stress - it's understandable you're seeking more support.
seeker: Exactly. I feel like there's so much pressure from all sides, and him not understanding adds to it.
supporter: Right. It’s like a house of cards sometimes, isn't it? Each stress point adds up. Have there been moments where you've felt supported or heard about your dreams or art interests?
seeker: Some moments with my parents recently, actually. They apologized for being too strict. That was unexpected but nice.
supporter: I remember you mentioned that chat going well. It's good you found some resolution there. Maybe it’s possible with John too?
seeker: I hope so. I just sometimes wonder if we want different things.
supporter: Sounds like you're grappling with a lot of uncertainty. Maybe expressing your concerns clearly could help him see your perspective.
seeker: Maybe. I think I need to figure out what I want too, with everything else that’s happening.
supporter: Finding clarity in your own needs is vital. Supporting you in this journey sounds important for him. And I am always here if you need to talk things out.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps just being able to talk and organize my thoughts.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Remember, it's okay to prioritize your well-being and take things one step at a time.
seeker: You're right. I'll try to talk to John again, but more importantly, I'll focus on understanding my own feelings and goals.
supporter: That's a solid plan. Baby steps lead to big changes. Keep me posted if you need to chat or just vent.
seeker: Will do! Thanks for listening and being there for me. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Anna. You got this. Talk soon?
seeker: Definitely. Take care!

reading_text:

seeker: I am having a deep sense of sadness after the break up with my boyfriend.
seeker: I feel like crying all the time and I feel like the sadness will never end.
seeker: I have sense of overwhelming sadness as if my heart is sinking or like I am on a sinking ship. I wake up in the middle of the night and I am gasping for air, too.

supporter: Thanks for sharing that with me. I'm so sorry you've been feeling like that. Breakups are so hard and can cause so much grief.
seeker: Yes, I feel like I will never meet anyone else and that I wasted so much time.

supporter: I know those feelings of sadness can feel like they will never end- I have felt that way too before.
seeker: Do you feel like the best part of your life was over? That is how I feel now. Its seem like all of my plans for the future are over and ruined.

supporter: But they do pass eventually and become easier to manage- with time and care. Do you have anyone in your life, a friend or family member who you can lean on when you're feeling so sad?
seeker: I have a best friend but she told me that she didn't like my boyfriend from the beginning so she is glad that we broke up. Well, that I got dumped.

supporter: It sounds like it's hard to have your best friend not be as supportive as you want during this hard time. What has been helping you to pass the time these days- do you have any activities or hobbies that you like to do to relax, have fun, or take your mind of things?
seeker: I have been wanting to buy a bike and start taking my dog out for little bike rides. I want to get one with a basket and have her sit in the front. I just hate being alone and I feel so sad about doing everything alone now.

supporter: That's a great idea. I love taking walks and bike rides outside when I feel down. I also have a little dog and she helps me whenever I'm feeling lonely- dogs are great at providing comfort and unconditional love. 
seeker: I just bought my puppy and she is super comforting. I think that because she was a recuse dog I feel a greater attachment. It is kind of nice having her.

supporter: My dog has also helped me meet other people and make friends- sometimes I'll walk my dog with others or go on bike rides with friends. If there is a dog park or local park nearby, maybe you can go and talk to other people there- talking about your dogs is a great icebreaker!
seeker: I know about a local dog park and think I will visit it today. That is a really good idea. I don't need a bike for that.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that! I hope you have a great time there! Research has also shown that spending time outside everyday is really good for our mental health.

seeker: You are giving me something to think about that isn't related to the break up. I feel like a weight is sort of lifting off of me. I think I needed to talk and get some of my feelings on the table today.
supporter: If you are still interested in getting a bike, I'd say go for it too! Biking is a great stress relief and form of exercise that often makes me feel better. 
supporter: I am so glad to hear that and am so happy you are talking to me is making you feel better. 
seeker: Yes, I really want to get one but since I don't have a lot of money right now I will waitr on that and go to the dog park instead. I also heard about yoga iin the park.

supporter: Those are both great ideas! Yoga in the park sounds awesome. Yoga is another great stress reliever and form of exercise that is often free or very inexpensive. 
seeker: I am feeling like life still goes on and things are going on all around me. I am going to start seeing whats out there and trying to join in a little bit more. My dog is opening a door for me and with your encouragement too. 
supporter: I am very glad to hear that. Is there anything else I can help you with today? I am here to listen. 
seeker: I was thinking about reading self help books or journaling but I was so down on myself.
supporter: Reading and journaling are also great tools to use. Even when you are feeling down it can be helpful to write down your feelings as a form of release. 
seeker: Thank you for all of your support and understanding today. I am going to journal and then head to the dog park and get some fresh air.

supporter: That sounds like a great plan. Good luck and I hope you continue to feel better. 
seeker: Thank you again for being a wonderful listener and better friend than my best one. 
supporter: You're very welcome.

seeker: I am having a really hard time with something that I did to my boyfriend.
supporter: Do you want to talk about it?

seeker: Yes, thank you! I was with him since childhood and we are actually still together. I slipped up one night and hate to admit what I did.

supporter: It sounds like you're holding onto a lot of guilt about this incident.
supporter: Are you comfortable talking about that night?
seeker: Yes, it is intense guilt. I can't think of anything else. I hate to tell you but I cheated on him. I am so sorry and can't look at myself in the mirror.
supporter: That can really weigh you down, beating yourself up with guilt.
supporter: Does he know about the incident?
seeker: I feel like I am worthless and I don't deserve to ever be happy or laugh again. I really do love him and I don't ever want him to find out what I did. Yes, I cant stop beating myself up. He doesn't know what I did but he is little suspicious. 
supporter: You definitely deserve to laugh and be happy. One mistake doesn't define you!
seeker: Thank you! A long time ago his sister told me that he cheated on me and I believed her and so I wanted to get him back.
supporter: It says a lot about your character that you feel badly about this, that you can see and recognize you acted in a way you don't agree with. That's something to build on.
supporter: That desire to "get even" is definitely understandable.
seeker: I appreciate that and have been thinking about character a lot lately. I do believe he cheated on me first, if that even matters now.
supporter: Do you feel like you got what you needed from the experience, as in, that you've "gotten even"?
seeker: Yes, I feel very even! I won't do it again. Can I ever give up the guilt that I feel and move on in our relationship or do I have to tell him what I did? I have known couples who don't tell each other and they are happy now.
supporter: While it may be true in general that honesty is the best policy, in this case I wouldn't suggest telling him. It is just going to cause angry feelings.
supporter: But, the fact you already believed he cheated on you and it motivated you to do the same shows a basic lack of trust in this relationship. That's something you should really look at.

seeker: Thank you for making me feel heard. I have been alone in my thoughts and needed to be understood. Yes, I agree with you and I feel like I kind of let it go now that I told you about it.
seeker: I am going to be in touch regularly of that's okay? I feel so much better now. I can take a deep breath again and I want to go take a walk with my dog now. Thank you for all of your time and understanding.
supporter: I'm glad you're feeling better now that you've gotten it out in the open. Of course, you are welcome anytime.
seeker: That sounds great because I want to keep this private and I know you won't tell anyone so I feel really safe here. 
supporter: Absolutely. This is all in complete confidence.

seeker: Well, I found some errors in the project report I submitted, and my boss called me out in front of everyone. It was humiliating.
supporter: That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since you've been dealing with a lot of pressure at work already.
seeker: Yes, exactly. It's like everything is piling on top of me, and I can't seem to catch a break.
supporter: It makes sense that you'd feel overwhelmed. Are there any parts of the project or your workload that are more manageable for you?
seeker: I guess there are some smaller tasks I can focus on, but even those feel daunting right now.
supporter: I understand. It might help to break them down into even smaller steps, to make them feel a bit more doable.
seeker: I've thought about that, but it's hard to start when I'm just so exhausted all the time.
supporter: I remember you mentioned issues with sleep in the past and how that's been affecting your energy levels.
seeker: Yeah. It’s been a persistent problem, and the stress from work only makes it harder to manage.
supporter: That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?
seeker: I tried meditation and some breathing exercises which were somewhat helpful before. But I haven't been consistent with them.
supporter: It might be worth giving those another shot when you have a moment to yourself. Even small doses of relief can add up.
seeker: You're right. I should try to make it a routine instead of just something I turn to when things get really bad.
supporter: That sounds like a great start. Making a little time every day for yourself could help ease some of that pressure.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.
supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You're doing your best under really tough circumstances, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I think I'll try setting up a time every day to meditate and maybe even talk to someone at work about easing my workload.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. Taking those steps could make a big difference. And remember, it's okay to seek help; you're not alone.
seeker: I will. Thanks again for being there and for your support.
supporter: Of course, Charlotte. I'm always here to listen and support you.

seeker: Hi there

supporter: Hello.  How's it going?
seeker: I've not been doing great to be honest. I'm finding it hard to stay positive with all these constant lockdowns and 
restrictions
supporter: I can agree.  There are so many places going back to where we were several months ago.  Which state do you live in?
seeker: I'm actually from the UK. I live in the North of the country near Manchester and things are bad here right now.

supporter: I agree it's bad!  Where I live in the US our numbers are going back up and the kids are being home schooled again.  I just keep thinking this is temporary!  
seeker: Yes I suppose it does help to think it possible not for the long term but my friends seem to be dealing with it better than I am and I'm not quite sure why it's put me in such a sad emotional state. I should just get on with it but have very low motivation

supporter: I have to say it's hard to find motivation and I was in that spot at the beginning.  With news of vaccines being introduced here shortly, that's what's keeping me afloat.  Are you able to hang out with friends?
seeker: no not really because I'm not supposed to mix with people outside of my household. I could potentially try and meet them virtually online or on a video call is this something you've had much experience with?

supporter: Oh very much so!  Zoom and Facetime are my best friends right now.  lol I think that's one of the reasons why I snapped out of my depression is because I started doing that more since we couldn't go out and do anything.
seeker: Ok that's interesting so you have also suffered with depression in the past? exactly how did you get out of it yourself?

supporter: I downloaded Zoom around the end of May.  The first two months were the worst. I had never heard of Zoom until a friend said we should have a virtual party so he organized it and there were 11 on the call.  It was so much fun despite the fact.
supporter: Maybe organizing a "zoom party" would start to lift your spirits.
seeker: that's a really good suggestion. I could also catch up with friends that haven't seen for a while. I think this would definitely work to boost my mood. The only problem is being depressed isn't something that I'm familiar with. what if it goes a little bit deeper than this?

supporter: Depression sucks I have to say!  Just don't let it win.  Since you say it's something you have never dealt with, you can fight it by staying upbeat and do something fun.
seeker: Sure, or something conversations like this help perhaps a support group would be a good idea also? 

supporter: Start off by not being hard on yourself for feeling the way you do.  Music, tv and books does it for me - and zoom
supporter: Most definitely.  Do you have Meetup over there?
seeker: I've never heard of this,
 what is it?
supporter: It's an app on mobile devices where you can (when there's no pandemic) meet up with folks who share common interests as yourself.  Nowadays instead of meeting in person, they are doing virtual meetups.  I do it with a book club.
seeker: I think something to take my mind off the current situation would be really good. I like the idea of a virtual book club. is it free?

supporter: Totally free!
seeker: I like the sound of that, thanks for your help
supporter: You are so welcome.  Just don't let that depression get the best of you.  You're stronger than it is.
seeker: thank you for the vote of confidence.

supporter: Very welcome!

seeker: I do like to read, but I haven't had enough time. I have been going on walks more frequently.

supporter: It sounds like you do a lot of activities that are solitary. Have you considered maybe partaking in a similar activity, like a book club, where there is more interaction with people?
seeker: No, I did not consider that actually. I do enjoy my alone time since I am so busy and I have a toddler, but maybe doing something more sociable would be good.

supporter: Being busy, especially with having a small child can make you feel lonely, enhancing the stress you feel from school. Participating in social events geared toward your interest might be able to connect you to people with similar feelings!
seeker: I think so too. I never thought of it like that.

supporter: I'm sure that you are trying your best to be both a good student and a great parent. It is understandable that you may not have considered those options.
seeker: Yes I constantly think of my son and family, and I didn't think involving myself in sociable activities
 would be beneficial.
seeker: I figured I really needed some alone time. I didn't realize I could be experiencing loneliness.

supporter: It is so admirable that you are acting so selfless.
supporter: Are you aware of any activities that you can participate in that can include your family? It could be the best of both worlds.
seeker: Yes, we like to go swimming at the YMCA together.
supporter: That is great! Physical activity has been shown to reduce stress levels.
supporter: My sister-in-law really benefits from having her sons in sports. She is able to connect with the other team moms and considers them some of her best friends. Depending on your YMCA your son may be able to participate in some of their programs?
seeker: Yes, and swimming is great exercise.

seeker: And if we do that more we can spend more time together.

seeker: I have been looking into putting him in soccer.

seeker: He can start at 3 years old.

supporter: Soccer would be a perfect way for both you and your son to interact with other people of similar interests.
seeker: I think so too. You gave me a lot to think about today that I didn't consider before.

supporter: I am glad to help, Hopefully, considering these options will not only reduce your stress from being busy with being a parent and with school, but it will also bring you closer to your child.
seeker: Yes, and both of those are major goals of mine. But the stress sometimes feels inevitable.

supporter: Sometimes stress is inevitable. You just have to know how to channel it. Some use physical activity, others use journaling. These seem to be outlets you can consider?
seeker: The physical activity for sure.
seeker: I do so much writing with my Master's program. Sometimes I feel like my hand will fall off.

supporter: Physical activity seems to be the option you are most interested in.
supporter: Have you considered setting daily exercise goals?
seeker: Yes, I am a pretty active and fit person.

seeker: Yes, I do try to go to the gym 3 times per week at least.

supporter: Having goals for a given day can help motivate you to do the exercises and keep your head cleared from stress.
seeker: I agree. I will definitely start to engage in more activities with peers and more swimming with my family. Thank you for your advice!

supporter: Your welcome.

seeker: Hi, how are you?

supporter: Hello there, how are you doing today?
seeker: I'm ok. To be honest, 
I'm a therapist and I'm getting burned out on the job.
supporter: I hear you .. it can be very difficult dealing with other peoples' problems all day. Would you consider retraining for something else?
seeker: Maybe. I'm not really young anymore. The thought of going through more school...well, I dunno about that.

supporter: True. So you feel you're stuck in a rut - you're not happy but you don't feel unhappy enough to move on?
seeker: I just feel like I'm in limbo. Just there. People complain all day about their problem. I have a therapist, but I think my therapist is burnt out too.

supporter: It's a vicious cycle isn't it!? What about looking for another profession that does not involve much retraining?
seeker: I'm too young to retire but I don't know how many more years I can slog on with this career. It used to be pretty good. Now, it just seems the same gray job every day.

supporter: Are you in a financial position where you could take some time off, go travelling perhaps, and renew yourself?
seeker: I've thought about that. I'd love to travel. I feel an obligation to my patients. I don't want to abandon them. I could pass them to other therapists, maybe temporarily. I don't know how they would feel about that.

supporter: Well, I would hope that they would understand that even therapists have to have a private life. And I am sure they'd prefer you at the peak of your game and not burned out. 
seeker: True. They might wonder how committed I am to them and to the profession if I go away for a while. I've thought about lightening my work load too.

supporter: Yes perhaps you could switch to part time? If you could afford it? 
seeker: Money not really the issue. I just worry that I'll keep burning out, just more slowly. Other therapists go through this as well. 

supporter: Somewhere at the top of the chain there must a very weary therapist with no-one to talk to. Though I suppose that is where these bots come in :D 
seeker: Yeah. One day I'll be replaced by a computer. Then the computers will provide therapy to other computers, who'll need a vacation when they burn out. 

seeker: seriously though, I guess I could try part-time for a while and see how it goes. 

supporter: lol. It's an interesting mental picture. I am glad you still have a sense of humour though
supporter: Yeah - try  and take up a new hobby with the extra time, maybe? 
seeker: Try to. Humor is a defense mechanism and coping mechanism. I have hobbies. They seem less fun because my job is less fun.

supporter: I am sorry to hear that. On another note, have you considered speakign to your GP? Perhaps medication might help.
seeker: My therapist recommended medication too, but I worry that it might impair my ability to do my job. 

supporter: I have tried medication and I found it surprisingly helpful but everyone is different of course. There was no impairment though. 
seeker: Ok. That's good to know. I want to be responsible to my patients, but I also have a responsibility to myself. 
supporter: Yes  you do! Thank you for talking and you take care of yourself! 
seeker: Thanks for your advice and honesty. I feel better now.

supporter: I am glad to hear it :) Goodbye!

supporter: What brings you online today?

supporter: Can I help you with anything today?  We can just chat if you don’t have anything in particular you’d like to discuss.
supporter: I’m Kim.  What’s your name?
seeker: Hi there, I'd love some help

supporter: Great! What’s going on?
seeker: I've been struggling with sleep over the last few months, and it's making me tired during the day. 
seeker: I have been finding it hard to stay asleep, and wake up tossing and turning constantly. 
supporter: Lack of sleep will definitely make you tired during the day!  Is there something bothering you that causes you to stay awake during the night?
seeker: I can't think of anything particular,  but my mood has been low generally for the last wee while which I imagine is probably the cause. I'm so tired during the day but as soon as my head hits the pillow at night I'm wide awake. 
supporter: Well it sounds like you’re tired enough for sleep, but you’re still wired and can’t get the sleep you need.  
seeker: That's exactly it. Do you have any advice on what I can do? 
supporter: Are you getting any physical activity in during the day to make body more willing to cooperate?
seeker: I'm working in a desk job so spend almost all day sitting down. That could be part of the problem. 
supporter: I’ve found that physical activity helps me to get to sleep even when I’m troubled mentally.  Another option is to slow your brain down so that your mind is relaxed.  That is much harder for me though!
seeker: That's a good idea. I could try go out for a walk either before or after work as a starting point and see if that makes a difference. 
supporter: That sounds like a good plan!  It also helps to make sure that it’s dark and very quiet.  Surprisingly enough, when they did research on sleep disorders they found that a lot of people just needed quiet and darkness.  
seeker: Have you tried lavender? I have heard pillow or room sprays can be good for sleep. 
supporter: Yep, I’ve tried a LOT of things.  I’m currently struggling with this myself.  I’m even trying out melatonin, tryptophan, and even CBD (not stoney weed oil)!  So far no success, but I’m still trying!
seeker: I've heard people mention melatonin - I might use that later if other methods dont work. It's good to know other people are in the same boat. 
supporter: It’s one of the reasons that it’s good to get outside.  Your body makes melatonin from sunshine, so going for a walk outside helps in 2 ways!
seeker: If we had a little more sunshine where I live that would be fantastic!
supporter: Getting good sleep is critical.  Supplementing with melatonin might help compensate for your lack of sunshine!
seeker: I'll look into it for sure. It's something I hadnt considered before this chat. 
supporter: Glad I could help.  
seeker: Thanks, the help was appreciated. 
supporter: Anytime.  Is there anything else you wanted to discuss?
seeker: That was all for today, thank you. 
supporter: My pleasure!  Hope your day goes well.  Sweet dreams!

supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!

supporter: I hear  you saying that they are not really effective, is that true?

seeker: so, yea

supporter: Okay .. I hope you reported him!!

supporter: Dogs are very very loyal. They never cheat on you or walk out on you! 
seeker: So trueee :) I just wish I wasn't such a freak. 

supporter: I think you are probably not anywhere near as bad as you think you are you know :). Anyway I wish you all the very best for the New Year and hope that things pick up for you soon!
seeker: Alright, bud. Thanks. You, too

supporter: take care!

supporter: That is a horrible shock to hear something like that. I  thank you for expressing yourself today it can be hard to share a disappointment.

supporter: If you are interested in religion often times they have local support groups to join as well.
seeker: I'm not religious at all.
supporter: Okay, an alternative is joining a local group that meets up for exercise in the park. Just an idea.
seeker: I have found that I have been focusing on my own health a lot more lately.
supporter: That is great news. Most of all thank you for sharing your feelings today and opening up. You are a path to healing but being so expressive and open.

supporter: Hi there!

supporter: It may be helpful to know.. my name is Ann. I am 43 years old... and I know for myself, I enjoy talking to people when I have concerns. 
supporter: What is going on? 
seeker: Thank you for your concern, I am just worried.
supporter: What has you worried? I know right now... its a hard time for so many people. I have struggled with my own anxiety the past few weeks.
seeker: Sorry about that. This is about my relationship.
supporter: Ah....relationship worries can be so draining and emotionally exhausting. I can understand that.
supporter: In your relationship, what has happened to create your worries?
seeker: I trusted my spouse but eventually disappointed.
seeker: She got a jot in another town and she utilize the opportunity to be sleeping around.
supporter: I can imagine how a break in trust has made you feel. I know a break in trust is always very difficult to process.
seeker: I am planing to get married next year but things has changed now.
supporter: Oh I am sorry to hear that. Have you had a conversation with her about her actions and how they have made you feel?
seeker: She knew pretty well how I felt.
seeker: I don't want to have anything to do with her again.
supporter: Do you feel that her actions and result can be remedied? Or is this such a fundamental break that you cannot reconcile?

supporter: Understandable. I would feel similar, in truth. 
seeker: I don't that I can love her again.
supporter: Only you know whether or not if you can look to forgiving and moving forward or if this is such a fundamental break that it is not something you can mend. 
supporter: And if you know that this is not something you wish to move forward with her that doesn’t make you a bad person. It means you are taking care of yourself first. 
seeker: Yes, I want someone that I could trust.

seeker: I will check that out, thank you very much.
supporter: I also talked to a few friends who are married and had experienced infidelity. They chose to forgive each other. I learned a lot from them. supporter: But ultimately you may experience a lot of ups and downs. That is also normal. It is your mind and heart processing everything. Please do not get discouraged.
