supporter: Hello there, how are you feeling today? 
seeker: I'm feeling pretty awful... I've been down and depressed for months now. It's hard to get through the days.

supporter: I understand. Is this related to the pandemic or is it something separate? I am sure that the pandemic has not helped, though! 
seeker: It's definitely related! I lost my dream job, went to a lower paying one, and I gained a lot of weight while working from home. 

supporter: Oh I can certainly relate to that one! I've gained a stone and a half in the last year. All this sitting around is not good for us! 
seeker: It's definitely nice to know that other people are having similar emotions as me.

supporter: Sometimes just having someone to talk to who knows how you are feeling can be really helpful I think. 
seeker: It's sad that this year has been so awful. It's hard to convince myself that it's getting better any time soon..

supporter: Can you make a list of all the  things that you hope will be better next year so you can tick them off one by one? 
seeker: 1. Better job 2. Healthier habits 3. Better financial situation

supporter: Well, the first and third one are out of your control really but you could make a start on the first one today if you liked :) 
seeker: It's hard to take the first steps. I don't even know where to begin, sadly.

supporter: I can understand that. Perhaps you could join an exercise class or similar? 
seeker: That's a pretty good idea. Have you ever done something like that?

supporter: I took an aerobics class once. It was quite fun and it was good exercise. 
seeker: That does sound like fun. Do you have any other suggestions?

supporter: Well, it's maybe not the best time to be taking on a financial commitment but have you ever considered adopting a dog? Good company and good exercise 
seeker: Actually, I have a cat! 

supporter: Ah I have two - they are wonderful company. Alas you can't really walk with them though :) 
seeker: They are great company. Sometimes when I am really feeling down, I remember that my cat needs me, so I need to stay strong. 

supporter: Pets are great like that. Do you perhaps have a neighbour whose dog you could walk if you can't get one of your own? 
seeker: That's a great idea. I just moved into a new apartment complex a couple weeks ago. Maybe I can get to know my neighbors. A lot of them have dogs. 

supporter: It's a great way to make new friends too!
supporter: Would you consider doing some voluntary work whilst you are out of work? 
seeker: That's also a good idea. I know a lot of food banks around me are in need of volunteers. 

supporter: I think it would be a really worthwhile thing to do and you would get to meet new people too
supporter: I hope I have been able to help you a little! 
seeker: I agree. I feel like I have a bunch of new ideas to start feeling better. I appreciate you talking to me. 
supporter: You are very welcome, it was my pleasure. Have a great day!

supporter: I hear how this is making you sad not feeling supported in the way that you need to be. Know that you are worthy and will find a way to connect with them. I hope this has helped.

supporter: Good morning!  What can I help you with today?
seeker: Hi, i've been feeling really depressed lately and I'd like to talk to someone about it

supporter: That is very understandable.  Depression is tough to deal with.  
supporter: Do you have specific things that are causing you sadness right now or is it an overall feeling of being sad?
seeker: It's a bit of everything. I've recently lost my job and I'm just really worried about how my bills are going to get paid. I feel so tired, you know?

supporter: I totally understand.  Losing your job is a very rough thing to go through, I'm sorry that happened to you.  Feeling constantly at red alert is taxing both mentally and physically.  
supporter: There is a concept called Maslow's hierarchy of needs, and sometimes I find it useful to think about if my needs are being met, and which is lacking.  Which is to say, obviously financial security is your primary need at the moment, but there are other needs you must attend to as well, including your physical comforts.  
supporter: In times of great stress and upheaval, there is only so much you can do.  The rest is worry, a hamster running in a wheel, a huge output of energy that does nothing at all.  
seeker: Yeah that makes sense but I've spent so much time thinking about my finances that I've sort of burned myself out

seeker: Like I have no energy even to be thankful for the other little stuff

supporter: That makes sense.  You sound emotionally exhausted.

supporter: Gratitude is one of those things, I've found, that is self-perpetuating.  Even if you begin by doing it robotically, eventually your mind and heart will want to be more sincerely grateful.  I have in the past challenged myself to find five things to be grateful for in the morning and write them down.  Whether those things are "I have hot coffee and electricity" or "I won $1000 for free", they will begin to start a small fire of joy.

supporter: You definitely have options, but your situation is still tough, and you deserve relief where you can get it.

seeker: It really helps

supporter: Of course, I am happy if I was able to help.  You have a good heart and love your kids, you stay strong, you can do this :-)
seeker: Thank you and I'll be trying! I hope you have awesome day and thanks again

supporter: You're welcome, you too!

supporter: Do u anticipate schools reopening soon
supporter: U r welcome. I hoped it helped to release stress.

supporter: I remember you mentioning that. It was a difficult situation, but you handled it well in the end. You grew from that experience.

seeker: I have always had problems with low self esteem this makes it worse. I have lost interest in everything I can barely make myself go to work.
supporter: do you think if you knew the reasons why the relationship ended it would help you deal with things a lot better?

seeker: Maybe, why would he cheat? I have seen her she is not that pretty. I thought something was going on the last few months but he kept telling me everything was fine and that it was all my imagination.
supporter: remember the fact that he cheated is not your fault. if he entered into a committed relationship with you you should not be cheating. if things aren't right you should be talking this through with you before deciding to move on and see someone else.

seeker: I thought I was a good girlfriend, I was loyal, nice to his friends, kept the house nice, cooked for him, he never said he was unhappy he just started having to work nights and weekends a lot with no overtime he said he was salary now. I must just be unlovable.
supporter: have you tried getting back out there and dating again? just because he didn't want to have an honest relationship with you, doesn't mean that nobody else does. also in my message above I have made a couple of autocorrect errors, apologies for that.

seeker: I trusted what he told me despite my gut feeling which turned out to be right. I thought we were so perfect together, I don't want him back I could never trust him again, I am not sure I could trust any guy right now, I am so hurt and confused. I don't  ever want to feel like this again.
supporter: relationship issues, especially when they and suddenly can be one of the most stressful periods in an adults life. you are not alone in that other people have been through similar experiences themselves

supporter: Do you have someone who you can talk to about this to support you? 

seeker: I have a couple acquaintances at work but I wouldn't want to discuss my personal life with, my mom said to have  a good cry but I almost couldn't stop once I started. He was my best friend and who I talked to once we got together I didn't seem to need anyone else which looks like a mistake now. That is why I am here for support.
supporter: Ok I understand. It is normal to be upset in a situation like this. When I ask if there is someone to talk to, I meant perhaps a friend or someone who has experienced a similar breakup. There are also support groups out there that can really help. Getting your emotions out and seeing that others struggle with the same issue may be a very good thing.

seeker: Have you ever had a break up of a serious relationship or know someone who has? Does the aching inside ever get better? How long will it take?

I realised that if she was capable of doing this, it's better that I found out now, rather than when we were engaged or married. I loved her but after she cheated, I couldn't stand the sight of her. I completely understand the feelings you are experiencing. The good news is that I have since met someone wonderful, we have children and I am now very happy.

seeker: I am sorry that happened to you but glad it turned out well in the end. You have a good point that it is better to know now than after we got married. I do have a nice neighbor who expressed concern when he noticed my boyfriend was gone. He said if I ever needed someone to talk to he was there. I thought he was just being nice. Maybe I should go talk to him some time maybe he was sincere.
supporter: I think that that would be a good idea! for info, In terms of how long it takes to get over it. I have read a statistic that is takes half the length of the relationship to truly get over it. Personally I think it does depend on the person and how things end in terms of the breakup.

You have made me feel hopeful and that there will be an end to these feelings and maybe things will go as well for me as they did you. Thank you again.
supporter: You are very welcome!

reading_text:

seeker: Hi there, I badly need someone to talk with! 
supporter: hi what’s on your mind today
seeker: My partner left me after fifteen years and I simply do not know what to do. 
supporter: wow. that had to come as a shock. when did you find out
seeker: Things had not been going well for a while but I had not realised just how bad it would be. 
supporter: i'm so sorry to hear that. how long ago did they leave?
seeker: About two weeks. I have barely left the house since then. I just do not feel that I can go on. 
supporter: not leaving the house is the new normal for many of us right now. are you not leaving because you have nowhere to go or because you are feeling bad
seeker: I think mostly the latter. I just do not want to face the world any more . I feel that everyone must know that I've been dumped and be laughing at me. 
supporter: you havve already made it two weeks by going one day at a time
seeker: I did not really have any choice though .  I do not see any future for myself now that we are separated. 
supporter: do you know brene brown and her work
seeker: No I do not, who is that? 
supporter: she studies vuneraility and shame. please look for her TED talk and there's a great youtube video on empathy
seeker: Thank you , I will. Right now I really need some sort of emotional support. I feel that the last fifteen years of my life have been a waste. 
supporter: i bring her up because what i sounds like is that you are feeling embarrassed because your partner made a choice that wasn't you
supporter: in reality the choice they made wasn't about you, it was about them
seeker: It is not so much that - it is that I feel that I dedicated the majority of my adult life to this relationship and now there is nothing left. 
supporter: you are left and you are enough. even if you dont feel like it right now you are enough
seeker: I really do not feel like it right now. What was the last fifteen years all about? I wanted to have children with him and he refused but now I hear he is expecting a baby with another woman. 
supporter: a relationship is part of who you are. it isn't you
seeker: But it is very difficult to try to strike out on my own again and I do not know if I even want to. 
supporter: it is hard. it sucks. but the voyage through the suck is going to be better for you than you may realize right now
seeker: But I feel that I am facing middle age on my own and I really do not want to do that. 
supporter: you have survived 14 days without a bad relationship. keep on doing that day by day and before you know it, you will be on the other side of the bad feelings
seeker: What happens if I just can't ever get over it though? Right now it's hard to see any sort of way through these feelings. 
supporter: yes, middle age is scary, but there are so many things you can do. ageism is out
seeker: I feel I might have missed out on my chance to have a family of my own though, because I waited fifteen years and my partner would not go for that. 
supporter: please watch the cartoon animals and brene brown on youtube talk about empathy. find one of your friends who has been through the suck and let them help you find your path out.
seeker: Most of my friends seem to be very happily coupled up right now. They are sympathetic but they do not really understand. 
supporter: i had an emergency ovary removal in my early 30s and didn't know if i woudl be able to have children. my doctor told me that the most important thing i could do was to be healthy becuse a healthy mother was what i could give my children even if i adopted them
seeker: That sounds like very good advice from both you and your doctor. It is a difficult thing to have to confront though. I really do appreciate the fact that you have taken the time to talk honestly with me. 
supporter: you want an empathetic friend. nobody has gone through the exact same thing you have but the emotions are common ones. you will be ok, even if you dont feel that way now
seeker: I hope that I will but am not sure. I really do feel rather better about things now though but - there's a long way to go. Thank you so much for your support! 
supporter: stay strong and stay safe

seeker: Hello there. In the past 3 years, I have gotten into 2 car accidents. Neither of them were my fault. I sustained a concussion/traumatic brain injury and am experiencing depression and PTSD.

seeker: I have nightmares of crashing at least 2x a week. I am seeing a therapist, but due to the pandemic we are not meeting in person to do EDMR for my PTSD

supporter: Hello, I'm so sorry to hear that. That sounds like an awful lot to go through in a few years time, which now can feel like the time passes so quickly. 


seeker: I have a traumatic brain injury that creates a lot of overstimulation in my life. I used to be social and now I can't be in a social setting for too long without feeling exhausted

supporter: Have you tried to talk to your therapist through video chat or is that something they offer?

seeker: Yes, I talk to my therapist every other week

supporter: That's great that they can offer that, I know it's very difficult to get regular care at the moment with the pandemic. 

supporter: Do you have any family or friends close by or something that you can talk to if you feel like you need some extra support?
seeker: I do not have supportive or understanding friends and family

seeker: I have lost a lot of them in the last few years or have created boundaries because when I got into my first car accident, legit someone said "are you not better yet?" and another said "can't you just walk it off?"

seeker: When I got into my second car accident, people said "again? are you drunk?"

seeker: Even though neither were my fault, people were not understanding or asked how scary those situations for me were

supporter: I am sorry to hear that, people are very quick to judge so it's very unfortunate that you were treated that way.  

seeker: After my first car accident, the tow truck guy was towing my car to my aunt's garage to hold for auto insurance appraisal. He said to my aunt "sorry for your loss" My aunt said "oh, she's right over there and alive"

seeker: the car accident was so bad the tow truck guy thought I had died

seeker: but even after seeing my car, friends and family acted like it was just something that happens to everyone. walk it off

supporter: Wow, I can't imagine what the car must have looked like then for such a comment to be made. I'm glad that you here and despite going through that trauma that you are still going.
 
seeker: Thanks. 

supporter: A women fell asleep at the wheel in 2013 and hit me going through an intersection and totaled by car as well, but I had only had a concussion and pain I had to go to physical therapy for a short time, so I can't imagine how you must have felt.

seeker: What are some things you do when you have depression? Have you been in a scary car accident before or know anyone? Have you offered them kindness or you just dismissed them and thought it was their own problem?

seeker: That sounds scary. And is extremely unfortunate.

supporter: I'm sorry that you didn't get the support you needed after your accidents because it's hard enough to go through the pain and trauma (mental and physical) to begin with and the support is much needed.

seeker: Absolutely! But I'm doing better now. You find out who your real friends and family are and you move on. The whole saying of "they don't deserve you at your best when they weren't there when you were at your worst"

supporter: You are 100% correct. Have you looked into any support groups at all or tried to connect with anyone with similar experiences through social media? 
seeker: I don't use social media

seeker: I quit in 2016, which is also when I started realizing how vain people are

seeker: Some of those same friends and family didn't bother to text me even though they had my number

seeker: I did find a local group that did social stuff together but they were all really old like 50 years plus

seeker: I'm in my 20s so it was hard to relate

supporter: Gotcha! Well I'm glad I was able to connect with you this evening because sometimes it helps just to chat and have someone listen :-) 
seeker: Thanks! I appreciate it. Happy Holidays and Happy New Year

supporter: I hope that for 2021 things can somewhat go back to normal so the routines can get back to what they were and that this next year is your best year yet. You have already been through so much to be in your 20's.

supporter: Hello there, how are you feeling? 

seeker: im good. how are you? just dealing with this guy

supporter: So, you are having trouble dealing with someone? 

seeker: yes and no. i agreed to work with him on the board when he asked me. he said he trusts me

supporter: If he says he trusts you I am sure that he does. He would not have asked you to work with him if he did not. 
seeker: very true. not sure if he just likes me as as friend or if he wants me back. we dated then he broke up. then he asked me out again and didn't see me cuz he was busy. now he's asking me to be on the board with him. not sure if he has other motives to try to get back with me

supporter: That must be incredibly confusing for you. How does this make you feel overall? 

seeker: confused! i'll know sooner or later what he wants. thing is i was hanging out with his friends recently who had wanted to sleep with me. he knew it and didn't like it. he liked it when i stopped talking to them

supporter: How does this relate to him asking you to be on the board with him? 
seeker: cuz the first time he asked me out i was helping him with the board. i think it might be a way for him to spend time with me and then work his way back in. not sure if he will or not though. time will tell

supporter: It is okay to feel confused and perhaps even angry about this. Have you considered talking to him and asking him straight out what his intentions are? 
seeker: yes but i'm afraid what i'll hear

supporter: I realise that this must be difficult but isn't it best to get things out into the open? 
seeker: it is but hes already hurt me before. i feel i'll find out sooner or later anyways. that way i can save face

supporter: I think it might be best for you to make a clean break. It sounds like you are being manipulated. 
seeker: possibly. i'd prob be better being away from the situation

supporter: Certainly you would be. I know that it is hard but you will feel better in the long run. 
seeker: I think I would. I tried to break away once but they asked me to come back

seeker: i feel there are benefits to it also

supporter: You need to be aware that that can and will happen. Ignore it. What sort of benefits do you feel that there are? 

seeker: it gives me an upper edge and more clout

supporter: In what way does it do that? 
seeker: being on the board gives me perks

supporter: Do you feel that perhaps you might be using him just a little bit? 
seeker: yes and i think he is using me to a degree also

supporter: Let me get this straight - you do have feelings for him but you are confused and you think that there's an element of mutual manipulation.
seeker: yes

supporter: You are definitely not the only person to feel this way! 
seeker: it's a difficult situation. i think it will become clearer the deeper i get into it. thing is he is the head of the board and holds the power. 

seeker: what it comes down to is im wondering if he has feelings for me

supporter: I feel that you are paying too much attention to your position on the board. 
seeker: i feel it gives me an advantage i want at the moment.

supporter: But that is rather manipulative of you. 
seeker: if you were me you would forget about him and the board

supporter: Yes I definitely would do that. 
seeker: thing is he is encouraging me to be like that. cuz it helps him too

seeker: okay. i'll try to lay low and walk away from it

supporter: I think it's time for a clear severance. Do you have any other people you are interested in? Any hobbies? 
seeker: yes but it's less than before cuz of Covid lockdowns. so it makes me more susceptible to this- if that makes sense

supporter: Ah I hear you. You feel that your options are rather more limited than previously because of the lockdown? 
seeker: yes

supporter: That is something I believe that most of us are feeling right now so I sympathise. 
seeker: true. i just have to be strong about it with him. even if he likes me i don't think it's a healthy relationship

seeker: i slept with one of his friends and the other one wanted to sleep with me too

supporter: I can tell that you really have deep reservations and know deep down that this is not a healthy place for you to be 
supporter: Is he aware that this happened? 
seeker: yes when it comes down to it

seeker: he suspected it happened

seeker: his friend asked the one i slept with if it was true. he denied it. so i think he suspected it

supporter: Do you feel guilty about this? 
seeker: now that im talking to him i do a little. it felt good at the time like i was getting back at him

seeker: you can tell this is a very twisted situation

supporter: Do you feel that you want to get revenge on him? 
seeker: not really. i just felt that if he stayed with me i wouldn't have slept with his friend and almost did with his other one

supporter: I am not sure what to say that will help your problem and give you closure.
seeker: thank ya for listening. i think it'll clarify itself in time

supporter: I hope so and I really do hope for the best for you. These are difficult times for all of us!

supporter: Oh I am so sorry to hear that! Are you at least getting sick pay? If not, are you getting advice about help you might be able to access? 
supporter: (sorry for duplication, not sure what happened there!)
seeker: It just keeps getting better...  I applied for the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance and was approved.  The next day, I got an email asking me to verify my identity (I am fine with that.  It actually makes good sense.)...

supporter: So you have been getting some assistance? 
seeker: So I did as instructed and got the message on the website thanking me for verification.  The following week I got a physical letter saying I was approved and the award amount per week.

seeker: I have gone online once a week and qualified, as one is supposed to do, and still I have not received a cent.

supporter: I see, so you are really financially struggling at the moment? Is there anywhere else you could apply for assistance? What about a foodbank? 
seeker: Calling the customer service line is futile.  The computer just plays a recording that the agents are on other calls and then it disconnects the call.
supporter: I hear you there - I spent a long time on hold for an official matter the other day. I guess that everyone is really desperate for help and advice right now. 
seeker: I have been very fortunate.  People in my church have been bringing me food.  I plan on trying to go to the food bank Monday, if they are open.

supporter: I hope that they can help you. My partner and I have used one before and they were very helpful. I felt a bit ashamed but there was no judgement at all. 
seeker: I actually got so tired of redialing the Department of Labor and Training that I sent an email to the Lieutenant Governor of the state asking for his assistance in getting the matter resolved.
supporter: That sounds like a very positive thing to have done. I really hope that they pay some attention to you. This situation is not your fault! 
seeker: I have been to this food bank once before, and they actually made me feel very comfortable and welcomed and gave me an information package on other ways the parent organization may be able to assist me.

supporter: Yes they are run by lovely people. Ours gave us a pamphlet for cheap and easy to make recipes too. 
seeker: I am very lucky in that the organization is only 3 miles from me.  I will be looking into their rent assistance and employment assistance programs as well.

supporter: So, at least it sounds like you have a good handle on this and are doing everything you can to help yourself, am I right? 
seeker: I have an advantage because I have a professional background in cooking, so I can take random ingredients and turn them into wonderful and nutritious meals.  I just need to have the ingredients.

supporter: That sounds very encouraging! It's amazing what you can make even with cheap food. Noodles , for instance, are very versatile :) 
seeker: You are right.  I am definitely not going to sit and pout.  I am just a bit frustrated with the system.
supporter: It's a very strange situation and I suspect that some of the authorities just feel overwhelmed and have no idea how to cope. 
seeker: I am concerned that my boss may try to not take me back at my job.  Because this is an "at will" state, he can terminate me without cause.  Although he can not legally fire me for being ill with COVID, he can take me back and simply release me the same day saying that I have become redundant.

supporter: That would be incredibly immoral of him. Do you feel that he is likely to do such a  thing? 
seeker: I would not put it past him.  Sadly.  But I have taken the attitude that if it does occur, there is nothing I can do to change the situation.  I would simply pursue a charge against him for wrongful termination, and seek a new job.

supporter: That is a very rational way to look at things. I really hope that it does not come to thank though! Thank you for talking and I wish you all the best for the coming months.
seeker: I may not win the suit, but I would definitely file one.  In 2000, I had an employer fire me without cause.  I sued and won that time.  Not only did they have to pay me back wages for the 90 days that the investigation took place, which was no minor sum, 
 
supporter: I am glad that you'd not roll over and accept ill treatment! Well done :) 
seeker: they were found to be guilty, so the judge granted me my wages based on the average of 80 hour weeks I had been working, all my vacation time, plus the overtime I would have received, holiday pay, and then to put a nice bow on that gift, he awarded me 5000 dollars in damages because the old company lied and said I had broken the law.

supporter: I am afraid I need to leave now but thank you for talking :) (can you press the quit button and take the survey?) Best wishes!
seeker: My current employer actually knows this happened, because years ago we discussed it, and I showed him the award letter from the Department of Labor and Training, itemizing the judge's findings and the awards.

seeker: Thank you for your time.  Have a great holiday.

supporter: You too!

supporter: Hello how are you doing today?

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that you are sad and anxious. Do you know what is causing you to feel that way?

supporter:  I can only imagine how sad you feel from losing your best friend. Hopefully chatting some will help. I know in the past when I lost someone it was nice to just have a conversation to help put my mind at ease.
seeker: Sure. I feel so lonely sometimes because we were very close.
supporter: I can imagine that you are feeling lonely. Did you have any mutual friends with your best friend that you can reach out to? I am sure they are feeling the same way and it could help both of you to talk to each other and share stories.
seeker: Yes we have mutual friends. I do reach out to them sometimes. But the feeling doesn't go away. It makes me have sleepless nights. I can't sleep. Every time I close my eyes I see him very close to me like we are having conversations. 
supporter: It sounds like you were really close to your best friend. It can take time to get through the grief of losing someone. Things will get better I promise.
seeker: I hope so too. And I hope he is a better place. Have you ever lost someone close to you?
supporter: I lost my father when I was 19. That was pretty tough and it took me years to be OK with it. There are still days a decade later where I think about him and miss him. 
seeker: Sorry to hear that. 

supporter: Time heals all wounds. While that doesn't sound helpful now it is true. I also found focusing on the good experiences I had with my father (or in this case your best friend) helps. Remembering the times where you both were happy. 
seeker: I will try to do that. How can I handle this sleepless nights?

supporter: That's a tough one. I personally still struggle with sleep for other reasons. Some things that can help is taking melatonin 30 minutes before bed. I have also had some luck with white noise machines or other soothing sound machines. The biggest thing is to not use your bedroom for anything but sleeping; so don't read a book or play on your phone in bed, you have to train your body that when you go to bed it is time to sleep. 
seeker: Sounds like stuff I can try out. 
seeker: I have a strong attachment to my phone. Will be a tough one to try leaving it off while I try to get some sleep.

supporter: Having a bedtime routine is also another tip. Try to do the same thing every night before bed. Have a consistent bedtime, wake up around the same time everyday, even on days that you don't have to go to work.
supporter: Yes, phone's are tough to give up but soooo many studies show how bad they are for your sleep. 
supporter: I believe in you though, you will get through this.
seeker: Good thoughts there. Will definitely try out the tips. I feel better already just talking to you.

seeker: Thank you, Bye.
supporter: You are welcome. I am sorry for your loss and I hope for the best for you.

supporter: Hope all is well


seeker: well, i'm losing my job in january so that is freaking me out

supporter: I can understand your feelings but I am sure there is a way out

seeker: I've not looked for a job in 20 years!

supporter: I was also in same situation and can fully understand how you feel but trust me you will enjoy once you start looking for job


seeker: I've got to do a new resume and then figure out how people even apply these days

supporter: Trust me it is easy these days to update resume as many templates available online and applying for job is easy as well. Many online options are available and you get a quick 
response.
seeker: I've tried to get in touch with the unemployment office but they do not answer phones lately.

supporter: Need not to worry about it. You can use search engine and just type the job matching your profile and apply online. Trust me you will be surprised to see many options.

seeker: Well it is freaking me out - I will not be able to pay my bills if I don't have a job.

supporter: I was exactly in same situations and can fully understand but trying all your options to look for job is good - apply online, call friends or family and see if they have openings where they work, look work online if you get any temporary work which can enable you to pay bills till you find better job.

seeker: I'm willing to do temp work, etc.. I just have to make enough $ to pay the main bills like mortgage, etc.. it makes me so afraid that I won't be able to do t hat

supporter: I am sure you will be able to manage all this and it is just temporary feeling you have.

seeker: 7 i'm very upset that we are even losing our jobs.  

supporter: No need to upset as it part of life. Call your best friend and discuss your feeling and I am sure you will feel good.

seeker: She's just been through this looking for a job thing so she should have some great answers and places to help me maybe 
supporter: Excellent!! - I am sure she will have very good suggestion and will be great support for you. It is always good to talk to people you are close. 

seeker: that is true!
supporter: You can always share and contact me if you need any help. I will be happy to help. Take care.
seeker: ok thank you

seeker: Hello.

seeker: I am so upset. It's ridiculous how things keep happening to people around me.
 
seeker: I suppose my supporter is not here.

supporter: hello how may I assist you today?

seeker: I am just so upset

seeker: It's like things never get better

supporter: I am sorry to hear that. I know how you feel. 
seeker: Yeah...

seeker: My mom is in Mexico right now for some ex who got deported. Like come on. It's bad enough she sent
 money to him.
supporter: What have you tried in the past to turn things around?
seeker: Hm. I tried moving on. And it just appears she gets worst

supporter: So you are missing your mom?
seeker: Not really...

seeker: She just keeps asking me for mone

seeker: I gave her like 10k for the house she bought and she hasn't done anything back. 

supporter: Oh I see my mom has also done this in the past. Sometimes I wonder who raised who?
seeker: Yeah. I get that

seeker: She rented it to some guy and left before even getting some decent money

seeker: so now she is stranded in Mexico with some guy who can't even afford to get her back

supporter: That is the worst. I ended up having to cut my mom out of my life.
seeker: I wonder if I should do the same...

seeker: My grand mother basically gave me a whole speech about how ashamed she is.

supporter: Sometimes it is for the best to set clear boundries.
seeker: But who knows. Apparently my mom said she'll put the house in my name for all these things I did for her. 

seeker: Kind of annoying to be frank.

supporter: Is Grand mother ashamed of you or her daughter? I feel it should be her ashamed of her daughter.
seeker: My grand mother is ashamed of her daughter

seeker: I am kind of left with a weird circumstance. 

supporter: At least that is a good thing to come out of a bad situation.
seeker: Only reason she has a house is because I helped. And if I leave it. Everyone in my family said I would be irresponsible
 to let my mom lose it.
supporter: I do not think that would have a reflection on you. It should only reflect on your mom.
seeker: Yeah, they said they already know my mother is irresponsible.

seeker: Instead they suggested I should provide extra financial security
 to myself or at least some future children.
seeker: Grandma already is giving a home and 2 apartments but... I guess I am the only kid. Christ.

seeker: My mom lost my om over 100k to be honest. It was crazy growing up to that

supporter: It may be nice to have a bonus house for the future. But even that comes with headaches. In the end you have to do what is best for you. 
seeker: Yeah. I guess boundaries are good.

seeker: I left her without much help to be honest but I guess just hearing it frustrates
 the crap out of me.
supporter: Or sell it now and pocket the money to recoup what was lost.
seeker: I would but it isn't even my property

seeker: And mom needs a place to stay... sometimes I wonder if she just wants to be homeless

supporter: So she is just talking circles and not accomplishing what she says?
seeker: More like she keeps talking about doing something crazy like have a police chase

seeker: and how she doesn't care for anything

supporter: Some people do choose that life to be free of responsibility.
supporter: Have you had a talk with her about seeing a mental health professional, She may be having some issues that would benefit from care. 
seeker: I tried to baker act her after she tried to call the cops on me randomly

seeker: It ended up them asking dumb questions like if she knows what day it is

seeker: letting her free

seeker: somehow ending up with her getting herself hospitalized 2 weeks later 
for low hemoglobin. 
supporter: Often police officers are not fully trained in helping mentally ill people, they only access if the person is a danger to themselves or others. 
seeker: yeah it sucks

seeker: Tried to get her on disability but they just denied her

seeker: She was brought up with bipolar depression before I was born. She said she just ran out the hospital..

seeker: I don't know how she is just getting the consequences
 of that now
supporter: A good first step is taking her to your local mental health provider. Or ask at a major emergency room where this is located as sometimes the places are hard to find. 
seeker: That was about 30 years ago

seeker: Crazy they didn't stop her

seeker: Well I do feel better. Thinking about boundaries. It has been less stressful being so involved.

supporter: Without treatment she may just be getting worse.
supporter: That is good to hear..
seeker: I've heard she has a lawyer trying to straighten up the whole disability and tr
eatment thing

seeker: My girlfriend just won't let me stay out of it

seeker: Saying my mom has no one and I would regret it if she just does something crazy

supporter: That does make it difficult when a partner encourages you to engage in unhealthy behavior.
seeker: Yeah. If it was up to me I would probably just be dead silent

supporter: I suggest talking to your girlfriend about how it makes you feel when she insists you continue a relationship that causes so much pain. 
seeker: Yeah. That's a good point. 

seeker: Well I think the point about boundaries really stuck with me

seeker: I feel so much better now

supporter: It was nice talking to you.
seeker: You too.

External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hi! How are you tonight?

seeker: Im ok - tired. Yourself. 
supporter: I'm doing fairly well, Thanks. Can I encourage you or support you in some way?
seeker: Yes - definitely. I am not sure how to proceed or what to do in my situation. I am exhausted, mentally and physically. 
supporter: You sound as if you are in a slump. I've been there. Perhaps defining the problem and some solutions can help?
seeker: Perhaps - i dont know the solution. the problem is I cannot continue to work these hours - it is just not sustainable. 
supporter: What are your hours?
seeker: like generally, or currently in these situations? usually its around 9-5 (give or take).  These days its 9 - 7 or 11pm or later. 
supporter: I have to say, when I am physically and mentally exhausted, I don't think as clearly and lose hope more easily. 
seeker: right, and that is the issue of where I am at. 
supporter: 9 to 11 would exhaust me. That is 14 hours? 
seeker: yeah - something like that. and lunches are at the desk - as i am working from home - so its pretty much no breaks either. 
supporter: I would certainly agree with you. That kind of work is unsustainable. Let me ask you this. What would happen if you told your employer you simply could not do these hours? 
seeker: hah - i dunno. im on a team of 2 people - and i guess if i dont do it, the other person has to. or it just doesnt get done, and i dont know what happens?? nothing? LOL. 
supporter: The worst that could happen is that they fire you. But that doesn't seem too likely as they seem to need you. But I have learned in life that if I don't care for myself, hardly anyone does. We need to be kind to ourselves. Set boundaries. 
seeker: agreed - i dont think they would fire me, maybe get reprimanded or more likely a guilt trip as to why I cant do it. Im just not sure what kind of boundaries I set when we have things due, and just literally no time. 
supporter: Setting boundaries can be difficult if you haven't done that a lot. When we think we don't have the ability to say NO, then we feel trapped, worn out, depressed, taken advantage of. People need to know that we reasonably can say no.
seeker: Well, I have to set boundaries, because working till 11pm most nights is not sustainable. and who on earth is going to view, let alone sign a contract at 12am 
supporter: I think that would be the first step. Determine how many hours you feel you COULD work. Then advise them that is what you will do. Find out what kind of timelines there are, and if you can't do it, don't go beyond your boundaries. It is obviously destroying your life. It really isn't healthy for you.
supporter: Exactly. It isn't working for you. Something has to change. And you sound intelligent, so you can determine what will work for you -- perhaps a range of hours, but definitely not 14 hours. Unless you are a young kid. lol Even then, that's a lot. 
seeker: yeah - ill come up with reasonable boundaries till 5:30 is reasonable, and if its a do or die situation cap it at 7:30 --- and thats only for dire situations. if that doesnt work, well then i guess either i dont have a job, or people figure out how to work in regular hours. 
supporter: That sounds reasonable to me. And if they try to make you feel guilty, reject that. Tell them, I'm sorry, but I feel this is reasonable, and truly it is.
seeker: hah i used to go out like a young kid, but still - just because most of us are working from home 24/7, doesnt mean I actually can work 24/7. even fi i were young, hell no. they dont pay me enough. 
seeker: thanks i really appreciate it. it sounds reasonable, and its what a coworker told me. if i dont set boundaries, i will crack. 
supporter: No one can work 24/7.  I think they may not even be aware you are struggling. So communication is important.  
supporter: You don't want to crack. It's not worth it.  
seeker: yeah, i think a call to not just my boss is in order, but also HR to advise them of the situation. they need to start telling managers, we are NOT front of the line workers, nor police, fire, etc. our jobs are not THAT important. 
supporter: I will say a prayer that you communicate your needs politely but firmly. And not believe false guilt. As you said, you aren't putting out fires and doing CPR.  
seeker: plus netflix, hulu, amazon keep releasing new shows. if i need a reason, it can simply be to watch tv and detox (so to speak) and get away from the BS of work (obv stating it more nicely than that). 
supporter: This has been a stressful year for many of us, you don't need to be working yourself into depression and exhaustion. 
supporter: You really do not NEED a reason not to work unreasonable hours. 
seeker: agreed 100% --- ive already hit those points, and it is not good for anyone let alone my job. 
supporter: It isn't anyone's business what you do on your off hours. 
seeker: completely agreed! and thanks for listening  :) 
supporter: I do suggest you simply stick to the facts. These are the hours, I can't work more.  You don't need to explain that to anyone. But be firm and polite. And you are very welcome. Sometimes we just need a friend! :D
seeker: its what i needed to hear from someone who is more anonymous (so to speak). who doesnt have a first hand attachment to me, so its a great assessment. 
supporter: I've been in that boat before. It isn't easy, but I learned what I had to do, and I don't get in that boat anymore. And I can see to help others get out.
seeker: :-)
firm and direct is the best approach. esp for my boss. she will appreciate that and then i will stick to what i say! 
supporter: Amen!  GREAT!  I'm glad to hear it!
seeker: cheers! take care and have a great day. if you dont do this in your day job, you should consider it. or at least i get the feeling youre there for others
supporter: Thank you! I'm retired but do community work! :D Am considering getting an office. I do love to encourage! YOu have a blessed day!

reading_text:
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hello there! How is life treating you at the moment? 
seeker: Hello, I have been concerned lately.

supporter: So you have some worries about life? Would you like to share them? 
seeker: I keep failing online classes even when I seem to have them under control. I think it might have something to do with me playing too much videogames.

supporter: Do you feel that perhaps you are playing video games as a distraction from how bad the world is at the moment? 
seeker: No, I don't think that's it. I have been playing games since I was 6.

supporter: Ah, so it's a long term hobby? I do love gaming myself I have to admit. 
supporter: Could you perhaps set yourself some strict boundaries, like you can only do a certain number of hours of gaming a day? 
seeker: I tried, but my online rank not being where I want it gives me anxiety

seeker: and I keep coming back

seeker: Just one more match, just one more, I keep telling me

supporter: It sounds like you might have a genuine addiction to gaming. Do you think you might benefit from some counselling? There are organisations that can help. 
seeker: Do you really think it's that severe?

supporter: Well, if it is affecting your grades and the rest of your real life then it might be. And it's best to catch these things before they get worse. 
seeker: The thing is, I keep telling myself I have enough time to get my school work done. But sooner than later I realize the assignments are already past their due date.

supporter: Have you been getting into trouble with your teachers about this or has no-one noticed so far? 
seeker: Yeah, I have. They say that I am either super invested on my school work or that I lack any signs of effort at times.

supporter: Does your school have a counsellor? 
seeker: Yeah, they assigned me one.

supporter: Do you feel that they have not been of any help? 
supporter: There are always external counsellors that you could speak to. How would you feel if, for instance, you were never allowed to game again? Would that significantly affect your quality of life? 
seeker: I really haven't reached out to them, so that's probably on me.

supporter: I do understand that it can be very difficult to open up about having a problem 
seeker: But I don't think I have a problem

seeker: I just wanted to get plat in League of Legends

seeker: My teammates suck sadly

seeker: so I couldn't

supporter: The trouble is that sometimes the person with a problem can be the last to actually realise it 
supporter: I hope that I've been able to give you something to think about :) It's been nice to talk! 
seeker: Thank you.

seeker: Yeah I might talk to someone.

supporter: You're welcome  -  enjoy the rest of your day! 
supporter: Remember to press the button at the bottom :)

supporter: Hey Taylor, I just wanted to check in and see how you're doing today?

supporter: That sounds tough. Conflicts like that can be really upsetting. Do you want to tell me more about what happened?
seeker: We were working on this project, and I felt like I was doing most of the work. When I brought it up, it turned into a big argument.

supporter: That makes sense. It could be helpful to think about what outcome you want from the conversation. How are you feeling about approaching it?
seeker: Nervous, but I think it’s necessary. I’ve been feeling so isolated after everything that’s happened recently, and it’s exhausting.
supporter: Isolation can definitely make everything feel a lot harder. You’re showing a lot of strength by wanting to address things and reconnect.
seeker: Thank you. I just need to get through this rough patch. Handling school and personal issues is just a lot.
supporter: It really is. Balancing everything isn’t easy, but I believe in your ability to get through it. I'm here to listen anytime you need.
seeker: That means a lot. I’ll try to focus on one thing at a time and hopefully it'll get better. Thanks for being here.
supporter: You’re doing great, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep taking it one day at a time, and reach out whenever you need support.

supporter: hi there, how are you?
seeker: I don't know how im gonna survive without my job.

supporter: can you clarify what you mean? did you lose your job?
seeker: Yes. I got laid off last week. A bunch of us were.
supporter: i see. what type of work did you do?
seeker: I was a chef in a restaurant. Since covid business went down, and now the restaraunt is closing.

supporter: oh i'm very sorry to hear that. but the great thing about having worked in a kitchen is that there are a lot of skills you can use in other jobs
seeker: All the restaurants are closing, and the ones open gotta duty to keep the employees they already had. Where else are my culinary skills gonna be used?
supporter: i understand that losing a job sucks and i can sense your frustration at the situation but there are other opportunities out there, and you don't need to be thinking only in the culinary field
seeker: All i have done is cook, my whole adult life. I dont know how to do anything else.
supporter: time management, resourcefulness, being able to think on your feet and manage multiple things at once are skills i'm sure you use and developed in the kitchen, and those are skills you can take anywhere
seeker: Wow!  Never thougt of it like that.  But still, i dont have a clue where those skills would be useful. All i know is the kitchen.
supporter: don't be so hard on yourself. I'm sure there are a lot of things you can do. of course if you want to stay in the culinary field, you might need to get creative in the short term. have you thought about finding opportunities to be a private chef? or maybe even make pre-made meals to sell for people who don't want to or dont have time to cook for themselves?
supporter: another thing you might try is an online cooking lesson or something. with more people staying home and eating in, they might be interested in learning how to cook better food for themselves
seeker: You know what, i have never thought of that.  Those are actually good suggestions.  But im not sure if i am discipline enough to run that business on my own.  I cook, and thats about it.  The business part i've always had someone else doing that.  I dont know if i know how to even set that stuff up.

supporter: that sounds like an opportunity in itself to me. i'm sure there are tons of people out there that have the business stuff but don't have the cooking skills. you could find a partner to help, and that way you won't have to do everything alone.
seeker: I dont know many people. i keep to myself. Dont know how i would find someone for the business side.

seeker: your ideas sound great, but they may be out of my league.  I dont know if i am capable of doing my own business.

supporter: i totally get it, but especially now, there are a lot of opportunities for people who like to keep to themselves, since so many businesses are being forced to go online. you could put an ad on craigslist or facebook for people who might be interested
supporter: give yourself a little more credit. you put yourself out there enough to come on here for advice. that's pretty good self-awareness and more than i can say for some other people i know
seeker: Wow! you have great suggestions.  Thank you so much for your ideas.  I think i may give it a go.  You have made me feel better about my situation, and gave me some action items to tackle.  thank you for this conversation.

supporter: you're very welcome, i'm happy to help and glad you feel better! Best of luck to you!
seeker: Have a great night wise one.
supporter: lol you too ;)

supporter: Hey Nick! How's everything going lately?

supporter: It's completely natural to feel that way. What specifically makes you nervous about getting involved?

supporter: That's a good mindset. Just take it step by step, and don't hesitate to reach out if you're feeling overwhelmed.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and for all the advice. It really helps to talk it out.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. You've got this!

supporter: Hello!

supporter: So it was almost four years ago, but you still feel depressed when you think about it?
seeker: Yes
supporter: That must be difficult for you, to still feel that way.
seeker: Initially, I was sad about being heart broken, but later I became more concerned about why I had a strange complex I never even knew I had
seeker: Which I never discovered until recently
supporter: Being upset and heartbroken is very understandable, but what do you mean by a strange complex?

seeker: When I first met my partner, she was at a low point in her life
supporter: So you really feel she was depressed or upset when you met her?
seeker: Yea
supporter: Did her being depressed have an effect on you?
seeker: Naturally, I wanted to help her, even though I felt somewhat uncomfortable at first
supporter: of course you were sympathetic towards her pain, that is totally understandable. 
seeker: So I stuck with her and saw her become better
seeker: even made some friends along the way

supporter: That sounds great, that you were able to help her out in that way.
seeker: However, I suddenly started to feel a little depressed for some reason
supporter: So as she became better, you started to feel worse?
seeker: I believe it's because I felt useless after that point
supporter: That's interesting, so you feel that you were together so long as you could help her, but then you lost interest in her?
seeker: I didn't lose interest, it was just that I had this strange complex where I needed to feel needed

supporter: or did she reject you once she felt better?
seeker: She said that she was busy with other stuff
supporter: Has that happened to you in other relationships?
seeker: Never been in another one
seeker: I've had crushes, but it never went past that for various reasons
supporter: So you have not had any successful relationships since then?  Do you think that is why you feel depressed?
seeker: I don't think so
seeker: The thing is, I'm still friends with her
supporter: So that is good, that even after the end of your romantic relationship you were still able to maintain a friendship.  
seeker: It's rather awkward, tho. We don't even talk often
supporter: Have you thought about volunteering in a position where you could be helpful to others?
supporter: So you feel that you are still friends even though you don't speak to each other often?
seeker: I've done such thing during the summer
supporter: So what you are saying is that you spoke to her this summer and that made you feel depressed about the breakup?
seeker: Oh no, I mean volunteering
supporter: That sounds like a great idea, did it give you satisfaction?
seeker: Yes, I most certainly enjoy it
supporter: That is really good to hear.  Hopefully you can continue to do that and help yourself by helping others.
supporter: Maybe we can talk more at a later time.
seeker: Okay, bye
seeker: Thanks for your time

reading_text:
Complete past session (original utterances; not verified world facts):
supporter: Hi, how are you today?
seeker: I'm doing fine. My problem is that my boss keeps hitting on a co-worker, who really doesn't like the guy. What can I do to make it stop?
supporter: Boy, that's a tough one. You've got to handle a problem like that pretty diplomatically. Have you talked to your co-worker, the one the boss hits on?
seeker: I've tried to bring it up with her indirectly, but it's an uncomfortable issue, you know? She is really upset, and I don't know whether it's my place to handle this kind of thing. It's more of an HR issue, but should I go to HR? Will that help, or just get me in trouble? I don't know.
supporter: That's a good question, and I don't know the answer. It depends on your HR department. Have you suggested that the co-worker talk to HR? Is there an anonymous system for filing complaints?
seeker: No, the company hasn't set up a system for passing along info that way. I don't know if she has talked to HR. She might not have because she's worried that it'll get back to her boss, and she'll get punished. I'd like to be supportive, even if I can't help solve the problem.
supporter: That's a good attitude. You want to be supportive and helpful. You sound like a good co-worker. Remember that the problem did not start with you, so you do not need to feel responsible for it.
seeker: Thanks for your words of encouragement? Maybe there is little I can do, but I don't want to let the problem fester. She's a great co-worker and a great worker. We need her on the team. What do you think a good first step would be?
supporter: That's a good question. I would show support for her and empathize with her and her situation. Do you have lunch with her? Can you send her a text letting her know she's valued? She might appreciate that.
seeker: Sometimes we have lunch, but usually she just eats at her desk. I could easily send her texts of encouragement.
supporter: Ok. That's a good first step. I think you have a way forward with this. Maybe after a few texts, you can sit down and talk about solutions in detail, like going to HR.
seeker: Ok. I'll try sending a couple of texts every day. Then I'll see if she wants to have lunch outside with me when the weather gets better. 
supporter: That's a good positive step. I think that you've got a pretty handle on the situation. Good for you! 
seeker: Thanks. The boss is pretty good at his job. He know how to manage projects and he's good with clients. There is just this one thing that he gets wrong and somebody needs to get him to stop.
supporter: I understand that you're frustrated and sad. I would feel the same way too. I think that anyone else in your situation would feel the same way. 
seeker: Thanks. I guess I just have to accept things as they are. I can't afford to leave this job, and it's impossible to find another job at this time. Plus I don't want to abandon my co-worker in her time of need.
supporter: Well, you have to do what is right for yourself. If you find a better job, think seriously about taking it. Your co-worker will not be there forever. You have a responsibility to yourself. 
seeker: True. I hadn't thought of it that way. I should consider my needs. Thanks!
supporter: You're welcome! I'm glad that I was able to help you!
seeker: I feel a lot better now. I start sending text messages to my co-worker on Monday. Thanks! Have a good day!
supporter: You too! Have a great day, and good luck with work!

seeker: Hey so my best friend finally stopped showing up. We're growing apart...

supporter: You are growing apart from your best friend? Is this a good thing or not a good thing? Or you aren't sure?

seeker: It's an expected thing but it's sad. We have hurt each other many times and he is a daily drug user and is very much a fair weather friend.

supporter: Ouch! That is a sad thing. As I was sitting here thinking about friends I have moved on from, sadly, most of the time it was for the best, even though it hurt at the time.

seeker: My friend stopped showing up when he said he would and I slowly stopped answering his calls and texts.

supporter: Life is a journey, and as we walk toward goals in our life, people either join us or bring us down.  Sometimes they only walk on the path we are on for a short time, sometimes longer. I have very few friends from High School, 2 to be exact. And only on FB, that was back in 1979 too. lol I'm old, but I have had to move on from destructive relationships, as you are doing now. It can be hard.

seeker: This is so strange and wonderful connecting with a stranger about this! Wow. That's true. I kept trying to get my friends clean and to work on a hobby with me but drugs destroyed my two best friends and killed one of them.

supporter: Ouch! That sounds hard. I had friends like that too. I had to walk away. Has your friend asked you why you are ignoring him? The reason I ask this is because it's good to get some closure and let them know their behavior is destructive and you need space from that.

seeker: No, he seemed to respond with pride. He deleted his facebook and never talked to me again after that.

supporter: I have learned in life that unhealthy people run from problems, healthy people stick in the mud with you and try to work out issues. 
supporter: Have you other friends?
seeker: True. It's hard to connect with people after high school. The mindset of high school is make friends and the mindset of adulthood is survival.

seeker: No, not now. I am married though.

supporter: Yes, and as you grow and mature, your life goals change, not everyone will travel with you. Right now you are starting out, I'm in the retired stage, lol Now I'm interested in helping younger people. It's amazing how our priorities change. 
seeker: Yeah some people just don't want to do anything in their lives...

supporter: I've basically figured out life only makes sense with God, and I don't worry about a thing now, very little upsets or angers me, it truly isn't worth it.  A LOT of people have no goals. I think this is actually a good time to examine the year, what you did right, what you didn't do so right, and where you want to go next year.  I think self reflection is good for us. 
seeker: This year has been a great test for us all and a call to faith.

supporter: A young neighbor just stopped by today, and he just moved out of his home, he is consumed with HOW do I pay the electric, HOW do I budget? How do I cook?  lol Like it is so interesting to see the journey in life. And my faith in Jesus Christ is really the most important thing. 
supporter: Do pray for your friend, and I will say a prayer too. Maybe he will come around some day?

seeker: Maybe I've tried to reach him but then I just wanted to be his friend. But I can't even do that.


supporter: I had two brothers die from alcohol and drugs. I had to learn not to enable them. Sadly, people choose their own life. There is opportunity to get sober, my husband is a recovered alcoholic.  When hanging with them and they do not want to change, sometimes the best thing to do is to walk away and let them hit bottom.  I have 2 brothers that DID find recover and a sister too. So my whole life was filled with people drinking and drugging. And I didn't want that life. 
seeker: Neither do I. I feel so much better. Thank you.
supporter: there's a prayer called the serenity prayer, I don't know if you are familiar with it, but it is used in AA and NA a lot, learning to let go of what we cannot change, and that is people,

seeker: Hi there, are you free to talk? 
supporter: Hello, how can i help you today?
seeker: I have been feeling terrible about the death of my dad. It would have been his birthday last week and that makes it even worse. 
supporter: Oh no... I am sorry to hear that. It must be devastating. Was it an accident, illness or natural old age?
seeker: He was only in his early sixties but he suffered a number of health problems, including early onset dementia. 
supporter: That is rough, both for you and him. I know it's meaningless to tell you not to be sad, however, you can think that he's not in a better place
seeker: I presume you mean now and not not ;). Though I simply am not a believer. It just made me think how meaningless life was. 

supporter: oh sorry, yyeah I mean now. Life is... fleeting isn't it? I sometimes think it's meaningless too
seeker: I do not really know what to do about my feelings. They are not going away. 
supporter: I feel you, coping with losing your loved ones is never easy. In fact, it's confusing when you grieve and even when you recover and move on
seeker: Do you think that people ever really recover from a significant bereavement? 
seeker: I think that what you said there was very wise. Maybe it's worse, in some ways, to feel that your grief has lessened .. there is guilt that comes with that. 
supporter: I don't think people can completely get over that, you just get used to the pain of not having them around
seeker: Whilst it hurts to think about him being dead, I think that it would hurt more if I had totally forgotten about him and did not think about him every day. 
supporter: I just need you to know that whatever your feeling is, it's completely normal and you shouldn't feel guilty for having it
seeker: It is just - very hard. I keep thinking about all the times I disagreed with him or did not appreciate him enough and I never got to tell him how much I loved him. 
supporter: Your dad wouldn't want to see you grieving everyday either. You should live the way you know he'd love to see
supporter: I believe he knew you loved him regardless how much you two argued
seeker: I know that he did :). I had just not expected to lose him at such a comparatively young age. He did not get to enjoy his retirement! 
supporter: That's sad when he spent all his time taking care of the family and yet could not enjoy his free time
seeker: Yes. I think it would have been easier to deal with had he not immediately descended into very bad health as soon as he retired and had had time to have some fun. 
supporter: have you considered seeking therapist? We almost never think of that service, but in a lot of case, people actually need help from professionals when grieving
seeker: I can't really afford to have therapy at the moment. Also I know that my dad was just have considered it to be a waste of money - he was very careful with money. 
supporter: he seemed to be a great man. Instead of regretting what happened, celebrate how great of a person he was
seeker: That is a really sensible suggestion and it cheers me up to think of it. You have been a really great help to me. 
supporter: I'm glad I could be some help for you
seeker: You really have been. I hope you have a great rest of day!

And we both said we're not 100% sure that we're ok with us being done for good. - We promised to tell each other if we start dating anyone. He said he wasn't interested in dating. Three days after that conversation, I come over unexpectedly to find him making dinner for a woman I've never seen before. Turns out it was his 3rd date with her. supporter: I'm so sorry that happened. Are you mostly hurt because he didn't tell you he was seeing somebody else?

supporter: You must feel really torn up about it. I can tell that you care about your relationship. 
seeker: Yes, that's true. The worst part is that he doesn't seem to think I have a right to be hurt. How do I even deal with someone who hurt me but doesn't care to take any responsibility whatsoever?

supporter: That would definitely add to the distress of the situation to have a weird surprise like that. It doesn't really seem like your fault that you were there but it is unfortunate nonetheless. Have you tried talking to h
im yet?

seeker: I'm also a parent, and my son is doing virtual learning, so he's just as isolated. 

supporter: I remember a time where learning crisis management that taking a deep breath and meditating in the positive work that you are doing can open up your mind to suggestions from your inner self. Have you ever thought that you superb skills can transmit in your home as well?

The reinforcement is just that I can get through this, these feelings are only temporary.

The key is transmitting your successes regardless of the situations. COVID is not going anywhere and as a person who has beaten stage 4 cancer, it is scary to be living in these times. You are doing monumental things, never forget that because your feelings and stamina for living will bind everything together. Politics, is the dirtiest and no government can solve  and will solve the problems in the world.  
seeker: thank you for listening. It helps to sometimes just get it out there. I have to go coach now (virtually). Have a great evening.

seeker: Currently I am worried to show up to work. We had a staff appreciation Thursday and we all got super drunk in front of our boss, and I am honestly scared he will judge me or fire me.
seeker: Yes, we are all laughing at the matter, but you can tell our boss is looking at us different. We all showed up to work Friday hungover, and he just made lots of comments and jokes to play the part, but you can tell he is looking at me and everyone different. I do not know how to redeem myself.
seeker: That sounds a lot easier said than done. I was the one who was the most drunk. But I do now know if he knows how drunk we all got since he left after one of us got hit in the face with a golf club and had to take her to the ER. So what if I say too much and apologize for what he does not know.
seeker: He is the doctor of the office and the 2 office managers were pretty drunk too. It was a hot mess if I have to be honest and being an office full of girls I feel like we went too far. I for one feel embarrassed, and feel like just not saying anything and it will fade away. But I know the next few weeks will be a little hard, for all of us. This one is for the books, and something I have never encountered in my 10 years of working.

supporter: Hi, how are you today?
seeker: Not doing so well today, I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm feeling super stressed about the workload I have, I just can't keep up with it all!

supporter: I’m sorry to hear that. Work can be a bad source of stress. Do you have anyone that can help with the workload?
seeker: Not really, there's only me in my role so don't really have anyone to help. I have tried talking to my line manager but she doesn't seem to understand just how busy I am.
supporter: Can the company hire any more people? Maybe they can work from home, and take some work off your plate. The line manager might also need some help with her workload. 

supporter: I understand that budgets can be tight. Maybe someone part-time?

seeker: From what I hear they aren't willing to hire anyone else, but I don't know the reasons why. I can only speak to my line manager and then she speaks to higher management.

supporter: Your manager sounds unsympathetic. That's very frustrating. A lot of people are in your situation in this pandemic: too much work, not enough help.

supporter: Do you want to leave the company? Look for greener pastures?

seeker: I have been keeping an eye out for other jobs, but like you say things are difficult just now with the pandemic, there isn't a lot out there!

supporter: Very true. Have you talked to your co-workers about this issue? What do they think?

seeker: They are all feeling stretched as well so they understand. I am trying to not talk about it too much with them, I don't want to be seen as the person who's always complaining!

supporter: Yeah, that's a good point. A little complaining is ok, but a lot can get on people's nerves. 
supporter: They want to be sympathetic, but after a while, they just get tired of you.

seeker: Yeah, I don't want them all to stop talking to me cause they find me annoying! I'm trying to stay positive, but it's hard some days! As much as I try to start the day in a positive frame of mind it quickly gets sucked out of me!

supporter: What do you do outside of work? Hobbies and such.

seeker: At the moment I'm not getting outside as much as I should, I do enjoy gaming but it's hard to find time. I've been working 14 hour days all week! My boyfriend tries to tell me to switch off but it's hard when I know there's all this work waiting to be done.
supporter: You could try setting aside an evening or two a week for time with your BF. Just walk out of the office. Try to set some boundaries. 

supporter: That might seem dangerous and risky, but sometimes it's important to set boundaries.

supporter: If you don't do that, then the managers can just keep taking advantage of you and your work ethic.
seeker: Yeah, he says the same kind of thing, that I need to be firmer and just leave when I'm due to. I guess the only way for them to truely see is for the work to just not get done as there's no time!

supporter: From what you're saying, it sounds like you think you have no power. Is that true? Are you really powerless in this situation? Do not underestimate your power over your life.
seeker: I guess I do feel powerless, I feel like they never really listen to what I'm saying, they just act as if they are but then ignore me.

supporter: It sounds like the managers are training you to be resigned to your fate. If they listen to you, it encourages you to complain. If they ignore you, you go away and leave them alone. However, if you leave work early (after 9 hours, say), then they might notice you. Are you willing to take a risk?
seeker: Maybe if I start acting more confidently they will start to listen.
seeker: I feel like something needs to happen so maybe it's time to take a risk.

supporter: That's the spirit! Taking control of your own schedule is one display of confidence.

supporter: Good evening :-)  What can I help with you with tonight?  
seeker: just graduated university and my parents are pressuring me to pursue becoming a doctor

supporter: Oof, that is a very difficult situation.  I'm sorry you're going through that.  How do you feel about it?  
seeker: I'm angry. I just want to be done school. but parents are on my butt about it.  

supporter: What do your parents say when/if you tell them you want to be done with school?  
seeker: they get mad at me and say they are dissapointed. I want to travel and see the world. not more schooling. 

supporter: That's not a fair thing for them to say to their child.  I will say that there are academic programs that combine travel and credits, but you probably know that already.  And I don't think you should have to compromise anyway. 
seeker: They won't take a compromise. parents are stubborn. What should i do? please parents or pursue my passion?

supporter: I cannot tell you what to do exactly, but I would encourage you to fulfill yourself before anyone else's dictation of your life.  
seeker: Yeah i'm leaning that. i already graduated university. i fulfilled half of their dream.  you think telling them my honest opinion will be a good idea? 

supporter: I think you need to be prepared for them to not be happy with your honest opinion, but that just because they aren't happy with it doesn't mean it's wrong.  
seeker: thanks great advise. i will definitely be prepapred. i don't care if i dissapoint them. it's my life not theres. i'll live with the consequences 
supporter: Keep in mind that from their point of view, they want the best for you because they love you, so try not to burn the bridge or salt the earth.  I had a rocky relationship with my dad after college too, but it's better now.  They will survive, and you will thrive.  
seeker: Thank you. yeah i get that. but they should be happy for me. They cant make decisions for me all the time. let me free!!! 

supporter: That feeling is totally understandable, I felt the same way.  They need to let you find your own way, it's apart of growing up.
seeker: Thank you. at least someone agrees with me.  Do i have the right to be angry at them?

supporter: The anger is understandable, but I think it is slightly misplaced as they are not trying to hurt you.  You are frustrated by their lack of understanding and their judgement of your choices, but you and they are both attempting to solve the same problem of your happiness.  
seeker: Good advice. you are great at this.

supporter: That's very kind of you to say, thank you :-)
seeker: Thank you for the great talk. im not as angry anymore. will take there feelings into consideration 

supporter: You are a great listener and have a lot of passion, I think you will be successful for sure.
seeker: Thanks have a good day. 

supporter: You too!

supporter: Hello there, how are you today? 
seeker: Hello. Better than usual. What about you?

supporter: I am good thank you. Is there anything you want to talk to me about? 
seeker: Yes. Recently, I broke up with my fiance. And no matter how much I tell myself that life continues, I still feel like there is a void inside of me ever since it happened.

supporter: So your relationship ended and you feel that you are struggling to get over it, is that correct? 
seeker: Yes, that's exactly right. 

supporter: I am very sorry. I have been through something like this myself in the past so I do understand. 
seeker: How long did it take you to get over it?

supporter: I think it was at least a year before I felt truly myself again and that I was able to enjoy life 

seeker: That gives me some perspective. 
supporter: I can tell that it's all very raw to you at the moment. You really need to step away and give yourself some time to heal 

seeker: I am not sure if I can leave my obligations behind.

supporter: What sort of obligations do you feel that you have? You need to be kind to yourself at the moment 

seeker: I have a job, and my siblings are not doing too well, so I have to make sure their stuff is taken care of, or else my parents will end up babying them, and my parents are not in their peak health. This is not something I can afford to step away from. 

supporter: It is good of you to be so caring and responsible towards your family. Do you think that perhaps you are taking too much on yourself though, especially at such a difficult time? 
seeker: It might be so, but the sad truth is that when people don't fulfill their functions, someone else is going to have to do it for them. Maybe tho, I could fix my schedule to where it allows me to have firmer boundaries. 
supporter: I think that that is an excellent idea and that you are being very mature about this. 
supporter: Are you in contact with your ex at all? 
seeker: No, I made a commitment not to contact him. 

supporter: That seems sensible. I had a problem with not contacting my ex when we split. I kept wanting to talk to him again even though I knew that I should not 

seeker: What made you stop?

supporter: A restraining order :D 
seeker: This actually made me laugh :D Thank you for elevating my mood 

supporter: In all seriousness though, with hindsight I realise that our separation was for the best. I think and hope that you will realise this in time too 
seeker: Thank you. Your analysis is extremely helpful.
supporter: You are most welcome. I really hope that things start to go well with you soon. 
supporter: Might I suggest taking up a new hobby and making some new friends? 

seeker: Yes, that crossed my mind. I think I should do both.
