supporter: Hi Anna, how have things been going for you lately?
seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough to be honest.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been happening?
seeker: Yeah, I had a fight with my boyfriend recently, and it's been weighing on me a lot.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. What was the fight about, if you don't mind sharing?
seeker: It was about our priorities and goals for the future. We seem to be on different pages, and I'm not sure how to handle it.
supporter: That can definitely be a hard topic to navigate. How are you feeling about the differences in your priorities?
seeker: I feel torn because I really care about him, but our visions for the future just aren't aligning right now.
supporter: It sounds like you're in a tough spot, wanting to find a balance between your feelings for him and your own future plans.
seeker: Exactly. I just don't want to lose him over this, but I also don't want to compromise too much on what I want for my future.
supporter: It's important to stay true to yourself while also considering the relationship. Have you talked to him about how you're feeling?
seeker: We did talk, but it didn't go well. We both ended up just getting more upset.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that it escalated. Sometimes it can be helpful to take a break and approach the conversation with a fresh perspective.
seeker: Yeah, we haven't spoken much since the fight. I'm hoping we can find a way to discuss things more calmly.
supporter: That's a good goal. It might also help to think about what aspects of your goals are most important to you, and where you might have some flexibility.
seeker: That's true. I know I'll probably have to make some compromises, I just need to figure out which ones I'm okay with.
supporter: It sounds like you're being very thoughtful about the situation. It's okay to take your time to figure these things out.
seeker: Thanks. I just want to find a way to make things work between us without giving up too much of myself.
supporter: Having that intention is important. You deserve to have a relationship where you feel respected and supported in pursuing your own dreams too.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard when someone you care about seems to be on a different path.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Relationships often require understanding and patience from both sides.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thanks for listening, it helps a lot to talk things through.
supporter: Anytime, Anna. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk. You're not alone in this.

supporter: Hello! How are you doing today?
seeker: It's a pretty day, but I'm sad.  How are you?

supporter: I'm doing well, thank you for asking! Do you mind me asking what's going on that's making you feel sad?
seeker: I don't like being blamed for something when I don't feel I did anything wrong.  A neighbor's dog attacked my dog and another dog within a week and I reported it to our apartment manager and animal control.  She was given the choice to get rid of her dog or move and she decided to move.  But my neighbors are mad at me, because they think I overreacted.  I guess they liked her more.

supporter: It sounds like you feel as though you are being personally attacked/mistreated for something that you feel you handled correctly. Does that summarize what you're feeling?
seeker: Absolutely!  You nailed it!
supporter: I feel as though you absolutely did the right thing! If I were in your shoes, I would have done the exact same thing.
seeker: Thank you!  That makes me feel better!  But, I don't know how to make my neighbors feel that way and I hate being the outcast.
 
supporter: I have neighbors who act in similar ways. They act as though they run the entire street, but they rent just like everyone else does here. Dealing with them can be very difficult at times.
seeker: Sounds like we live in the same neighborhood!  Ha!
supporter: Just based on what you're saying, I can completely understand why you feel the way that you do. In my opinion, you have every right to feel that way.
supporter: Haha! It's not fun at all to have neighbors who make you feel as though you're somehow less than them. I know exactly what that feels like.
seeker: Yep!  That's how I feel.  What should I do to get back in good graces with them?
supporter: I do know people who have gone through the exact same thing in the past. When another animal attacks one of your fur-babies, it's absolutely terrible. However, the fact that this woman was given the option to either get rid of her dog or move tells me that you are 100% correct in the way that you handled this situation. It's unfortunate for the woman, yes, but she should have had more control over her dog. It's bad enough when one animal is attacked, but when it's more than one, that's when you really know that it's a problem. Again, legally, she had to make a choice, and that's because she failed to properly secure her dog. I really don't feel as though you did anything wrong.
supporter: If I were you, I would ask to speak with the neighbors who have an issue with you face-to-face. I know it may be difficult, but I think that would be the best way to go about it. Are you on good terms with the other person whose dog was attacked?
seeker: I totally agree with you!  The woman is disabled and I think most of the neighbors feel sorry for her.  I've seen her loose control of the dog before, but she never attacked another dog(s).  I've even seem the dog pull her scooter over and the woman needed lots of help to get back into it.  I think everyone feels sorry for her.
 
supporter: That probably has a lot to do with it. I would feel sorry for her too, as it is very sad in general. However, it doesn't excuse the fact that her animal attacked two other dogs.
seeker: I've talked to the neighbors face-to-face and they just think that I overreacted.  The woman started getting her dog and private training and so they feel that she was trying.  My point was that my dog weighs 15 pounds and her dog weighs 45 pounds and, if it happens again, I may not have a dog anymore.  I don't want to wait until a dog is killed or badly injured.  I told them exactly what you just said, but they are being mean!

seeker: I guess I could try talking to them again.  Maybe they've cooled off some.

supporter: That is absolutely terrible. In that case, I would just tell them that you refuse to allow another dog to possible injure or kill your own dog, so you did what was necessary to protect your fur-baby. Had you not done anything, this could have happened again, and the outcome may have been much worse. At that point, if they still don't respond kindly, I'd tell them that you still feel as though you did what needed to be done, that you understand why they are upset, but that you will always do whatever it takes to protect your dog. Hopefully, they will stop being mean. Even if they just stop talking to you completely, it's better than them harassing you or something along those lines. If they do start escalating their nasty behavior, I'd let the manager of your complex know that you're being mistreated. I always try to keep things calm and quiet, but I refuse to be taken advantage of or treated poorly.
supporter: Personally, as I stated previously, I wholeheartedly believe that you did the right thing. If they're unable to see that, I'd try to just avoid contact with them unless it's necessary. I know it stinks and I'd be sad too, but unfortunately, some people just don't know how to let things go and seem to find joy in making other people upset. I'm so sorrry that you're dealing with all of this.
seeker: Thank you so much!  Those are really good suggestions.  I'll do that and, hopefully, they will calm down.  If not, I have other friends that live outside my neighborhood.  And I can talk to the manager like you said.

seeker: I appreciate your help today.  And your validation that I did nothing wrong.  I was beginning to second guess my actions.

supporter: I'm so glad that I was able to offer helpful suggestions! Hang in there. You sound like a strong person! I would definitely spend some time with your true friends who live outside of your neighborhood. I can assure you that if someone else's animal attacked one of mine, I would have done the exact same thing that you did.
seeker: THANK YOU!  Take care!

supporter: You're very welcome! You do the same. Have a wonderful day. Try to do things that make you smile! :)

supporter: You are welcome!

supporter: That's a great approach. I'm proud of you for tackling things one step at a time.
seeker: Thank you. I'll keep you posted on how everything goes.
supporter: Please do. Take care, Sarah. You've got this.

seeker: Going to the store gives me Panic Attacks! Driving also makes me highly anxious.

seeker: I am on medication but this only seems to help moderately.

supporter: Hello

seeker: Hi

supporter: So just to ensure that I understand you correctly, you are feeling anxious about going to the store during the pandemic

seeker: No. This has been going on before the pandemic

seeker: COVID didn't cause my anxiety

supporter: Okay, so just general anxiety about it then. 

seeker: Yessir

supporter: How long have you had this anxiety issue?

seeker: Only the past couple of years. It came on suddenly at a nail salon after I had an allergic reaction to a chemical in acrylic nails.

seeker: Originally the doctors thought it was brain inflammation.

seeker: What suggestions do you have for improving it?

seeker: Meditation?

seeker: Exercise? 

seeker: I do art. And never have anxiety when I'm painting, however, I cannot exactly do that at the store

supporter: Have you thought about looking for support groups with people who also have anxiety about being in public?

seeker: I have and I did

supporter: Have you thought about brining a friend with you to the store? Someone you are comfortable with? Having someone you are comfortable with may help to calm the anxiety while you are out. 

seeker: Support groups don't really help stop the Panic Attacks. They cause all sorts of sensations. Fast heart rate, chills, shakes, My brain feels foggy and impersonal.


seeker: I do go to the store often with my fiance :)

seeker: That has helped a lot

supporter: I have also had anxiety in the past when in public places, so I know how it feels to be anxious while out. 

seeker: Yeah, it's definitely annoying. But it isn't JUST at the store. I was diagnosed with Panic Attack Disorder and even have attacks at home where I freak out.

seeker: It's been better since I was on medication but I never feel completely....normal

supporter: Another thing that may help is having some headphones in attached to your phone or an MP3 player so you can have some calming music or something in your ear while you are out.

seeker: That's actually a really good idea. Distractions definitely seem to be the way to go for me.

seeker: That's probably why art helps so much

supporter: I found that distractions were great for me too! 

seeker: I wonder if it should be calming music or music that I generally feel like dancing too

seeker: I know that sometimes calming music kinda makes me more centered and aware of myself which can exacerbate the problems sometimes.

seeker: I usually listen to music loudly when Im in my car to help with the anxiety

seeker: Of course, I always think its working then I get to the store and my hands hurt from gripping my steering wheel so hard XD

supporter: Whatever music you think would be best would be a good idea. 

seeker: I think a lot of my anxiety doesnt stem from social stuff but from a fear of death tbh

seeker: What other distractions can you reccomend?

seeker: *recommend

supporter: Do you have a stress ball or something you can keep with you in your pocket while out? 

seeker: I don't!

supporter: I think picking up one of those and having it with you might also help!

seeker: That's a really good idea too. Thanks so much

supporter: You're very welcome!

seeker: <3 Have a good one!

supporter: Thank you, you too!

supporter: Hey, you need to remind yourself that things will not be this way forever. A vaccine will be developed soon, and things will be just like they used to!

supporter: okay 
seeker: No, I think that's all I needed,maybe just talking about it put things into perspective.
supporter: Great, it was nice talking to you.

supporter: Bye

supporter: Hello. How are you tonight?

seeker: I'm hanging in there. I'm in a funk.

supporter: I'm sorry to hear things aren't going to well. What's the problem in a nutshell?
seeker: I split with my girlfriend after 5 years together last month/

supporter: Breakups can be hard, I can understand your frustration. Five years is a long time to have a relationship and then end. 
seeker: I caught her cheating on me.

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. That's hard to forgive and move on from that. 
seeker: I'm trying to just move on but I feel so insulted. I'm mad then sad back and forth, over and over.

supporter: I find that when I have a very painful situation, I try to only thing about it for a certain amount of time. Then I make a list of things to do so I can be occupied to not think about it. 
seeker: Yes, but my whole life was upended. My living situation, my friend circle is broken up over this. I don't know how to move on. Any suggestions?

supporter: I've been using it myself over the past 3 months and it most definitely helps! But it's absolutely imperative to clear your mind and have complete quiet.

supporter: My final piece of advice would be to set aside time that is specified where nothing negative is discussed. No politics, no bills, nothing anxiety producing for you. It's probably best if this time is within an hour of your bedtime becuase anxiety is not conducive to a good night's sleep.
seeker: That's helpful. Thanks.
supporter: No problem. Take care. Wishing you well on your situation.
seeker: Thanks. You too

supporter: Hi, how are you?
seeker: I am not that good

seeker: I have tried everything but not able to find suitable job

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. What would you like to talk about today?
supporter: Would you like to discuss job-search strategies?
seeker: Yes

seeker: I actually created good profile on LinkedIn

supporter: We're in the middle of a pandemic, so it's been hard for everyone to conduct a job search. 
seeker: but so many people apply for same openings within few minutes.

supporter: That's a great start. The quality of your profile is important. Did you ask anyone to give you feedback on your profile?
seeker: Its highly competitive nowadays

seeker: Yes, I am taking feedback from my ex-colleagues

supporter: That's good. Have you benefited from their feedback? Do you think a profession resume writer might be of help? 
seeker: They have been very helpful but because of pandemic its pretty slow and lot of people are applying for same profiles

supporter: What sort of position and in what industry? 
seeker: I actually used to help people in the past in their profiles but now its not working
seeker: I have a software background with business intelligence

seeker: Looking for position as business analyst of BI Developer

supporter: That sounds like a competitive profile under normal circumstances. 
seeker: I have worked for several years in a dynamic startup enviornment

supporter: The demand for those positions has probably dropped because of the economic slowdown. is there any other sort of job that would interest you?
supporter: Is that the kind of job that you can do from home?
seeker: I was working on a senior position but I am looking for profiles like early starters

seeker: The senior positions are difficult to grasp because of economic slowdown

seeker: Yes, I was working from home for a while in my previous organization

supporter: If you are good with numbers and software, you are probably a good fit for other jobs.
seeker: Yes, I have atleast 5 different resumes with little tweaks. In a startup, you end up gaining knowledge of various fields.

supporter: So you're interested in going into the startup world?
seeker: No, I don't want to go back startup world again. That's not at all reliable

seeker: Its highly risky

supporter: Ok. So you want stability and a higher-level position. 
seeker: Stability is much more important, I don't need a higher-level position at this point of time. I am already looking for junior profiles to enter faster in the job market

supporter: Is it possible that you are overqualified for those positions?
seeker: Yes, but I have made customized resumes for different profiles. I tend to remove many things like MBA wherever its not required.

seeker: I generally try to apply with a balanced resume, its just that market is highly competitive.

supporter: That might work, but I wonder whether HR will want your credentials once you get a job.
seeker: I doubt HR will have any concerns about my credentials about being over-qualified after getting hired. The reporting manager may be anxious rather happy to know about my skillset

supporter: Ok. It's hard to know how companies play those things now. Sometimes they check your social media accounts for any inconsistency. 
seeker: Yes, they do check the social media accounts but I tried to keep generic profile over there to avoid concerns.
supporter: That's good thinking. Play it safe. 
seeker: Yes, thanks. I will keep trying I guess. Hopefully I get a job soon.
supporter: Is there anything else you would like chat about?
seeker: No, that will be all. Thanks

supporter: Ok. Have a good day. 
seeker: Thanks, you too.

supporter: Ok.

seeker: Hello
supporter: Hi, how are you feeling today? 
seeker: I am not feeling the best. I have been having some depression, because of not being able to see friends and family during this pandemic.
supporter: Oh, boy, do I know that feeling! How are you dealing with it? (if I may ask)
seeker: I try to message them as much as possible and call them on the phone but it is just not the same as actually getting to give the a hug and see them in person.
supporter: I know that. I use Zoom, just to see them...do you have a computer?
seeker: Yes. That works for some of my family but I have family in the nursing home that does not have access to computers. I haven't seen them in several months. It just breaks my heart.
supporter: Oh. I can feel it. I have someone who's sick as well. Do you have any one friend with whom you can share your feelings, your depression. I understand you're having issues with depression, right? It sometimes helps me to feel that we're all in this together. And, at the other end of this, we will be able to give the biggest hugs ever!
seeker: Yes. I have some very dear friends that have helped me a lot. I guess the depression is just worse because it is the holidays and this is the first year that I haven't got to spend it with my extended family members.
supporter: Oh....That's so tough...it being the first year!!!! Sometimes, I cry (I cry with my cat), and just to say the feelings out loud makes me feel a bit better. 
seeker: Yeah. I have a little dog that has been my cuddle buddy. I have had him for 13 years so he has seen me ugly cry many times. What are some things you do to deal with depression?
supporter: I try to read, watch programs or podcasts that take away my negativity. Anything that will give me a lift, so that my own depression won't get so bad that I can't remember what it felt like to be a bit happy. 
seeker: That sounds like some good advice. I think I will try to find a good podcast or a good comedy series that I like and spend time doing that. It's hard to be sad when you are watching something funny or listening to something funny. Thank you for the good advice and the listening ear.

supporter: I wish that I could listen to more....this thing is so slow. Remember, we
're all in this together, and we will come out the other end. Isn't it OK to be happy a bit, even though this takes such a toll on so many people? 
seeker: That is so true. I guess we tend to feel guilty if we feel happy since there is so much sadness in the world right now. But you are so right about the fact that we will come out on the other side. It helps to remember that bad things don't last forever.
supporter: Yes, and are you somewhere where you can walk or exercise a bit? I always feel better if I can move around...dance...something active. What I find helps me the most is to remember that we need to stay safe and be OK, so that we will be here to celebrate when this is over. 
seeker: Yes. I live in the country so I can go for nice walks when the weather is nice. Staying safe is definitely important right now.
supporter: Oh...it's fortunate that you live in the country. Can you take some deep breathes and watch the trees, the animals, and nature....they are all here for us???
seeker: Yes that is exactly what I do. Thank you so much for your help today. You have made me feel better just having someone to vent to.
supporter: Keep venting, if it makes you feel better. I know I do when I can talk to someone I don't know. Is it nice where you are today, so that you can look at something bigger than the indoors?? That often helps me feel better.
seeker: Yes. It the weather is very pretty here today. As a matter of fact, I think I am fixing to go for a nice walk. I hope you have a wonderful day and thank you for listening.

supporter: You bet, I hope you feel so much better and can take that with you tomorrow--that you had a good day on the day after Christmas!!!!

supporter: Half your neighbors died?

supporter: So do you think you can identify the most difficult problem you have? Maybe we can look at that and possible find better ways to cope?
seeker: I am feeling depression right now
supporter: I can understand feeling depressed. I think that can be debilitating at times, however there are ways to cope and help you get out of it. 
supporter: I used to struggle a lot with depression, but not much anymore. I learned a lot of coping strategies. I can share a few of those with you if you want. 
supporter: One of the best ways is to take a walk. Get outside, get fresh air. Look at the sky and the clouds and the trees and the grass. This will not only physically refresh you but help your health as well.

seeker: I am really afraid here I don't know what to do
supporter: As for the pandemic, if you know no one who has died, I wouldn't worry about it. The CDC has no reported deaths of anyone healthy. People who are unhealthy die, not the healthy, and people who are sick ALREADY are the ones who die. If you are relatively healthy, then you are good to go. Do things to protect your health. What are you eating? What are you drinking? Are you talking to friends and getting social life? Are you getting fresh air? Thinking good thoughts?  Or are you living in fear when you are not going to a lot of funerals. 
supporter: It is well documented that our immune system is affected by our mental state, so it is important that you care for your health. Focusing on the negativity of the pandemic will bring you down. Focusing on being healthy and taking care of your mind, soul, spirit and body will help build up your immunity and make you strong.
seeker: I don't like the noise of ambulance at all any time I see one I don't feel happy
supporter: I can understand an ambulance sound is hard to hear, but even that can be turned around. You can pray for the person, then switch your mind off. supporter: One thing I did to help with depression is keep a checklist of things to do when I felt down:  call a friend, call a loved one to encourage THEM, go for a walk, eat fruits and veggies, read a book, go for a bike ride, etc.  Things like that, then I chose to do those things despite how I felt. Doing those things helped my mood TREMENDOUSLY> 
supporter: Feelings follow thoughts. If you think negative thoughts, you will feel negative. If you think positive thoughts, you will feel positive. Sometimes this takes time, but it works.  Just because you feel sad doesn't mean you should just do nothing, a person can TALK their way out of sadness and choose to do something different.

source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I used to struggle a lot with depression, but not much anymore. I learned a lot of coping strategies. I can share a few of those with you if you want.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: One of the best ways is to take a walk. Get outside, get fresh air. Look at the sky and the clouds and the trees and the grass. This will not only physically refresh you but help your health as well.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I am really afraid here I don't know what to do
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I don't like the noise of ambulance at all any time I see one I don't feel happy
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: One thing I did to help with depression is keep a checklist of things to do when I felt down:  call a friend, call a loved one to encourage THEM, go for a walk, eat fruits and veggies, read a book, go for a bike ride, etc.  Things like that, then I chose to do those things despite how I felt. source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: Feelings follow thoughts. If you think negative thoughts, you will feel negative. If you think positive thoughts, you will feel positive. source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: Thanks your words of encouraging help me a lot
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I am glad you were able to talk about how this is affecting you. I think many people are affected. source_refs.exact_quote: You are very correct I like you a lot
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: Thank you, how very sweet!  I do thank you for sharing your life with me. I'm an older person and this has affected me too.  Life is full of ups and downs, so I've been through some rough times. You can do this! :D

source_refs.exact_quote: Lovely I love meeting people like you who has words of wisdom
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I had one more thought about when the ambulance comes by and you get upset. Pray for the person, pray for the workers. source_refs.exact_quote: I cannot worry about what is not my job. I have a home and family to care for and pets and neighbors. source_refs.exact_quote: If that is all, then you simply finish the hit. I am sure you will do just fine!

source_refs.exact_quote: Thanks for everything you are too good

supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I'm sad and angry because I no longer talk to my best friend
supporter: Do you know what might have happened to cause your and your best friend to not talk anymore?
seeker: Well she was staying at my house for a month and we were constantly fighting so she just stopped talking to me
supporter: That sounds really stressful and I can see how troubling that is for you.
seeker: Yes it is and then she began avoiding me while we were in the same house, so we started arguing again and I found out she's been lying to me since I've known her and I'm very upset.
supporter: That's definitely very upsetting. I know how it feels to have that sense of betrayal from a friend I was close to for many years. However, I was able to discuss the issue I had with my parents and other friends. Do you have anyone else close to you that you can talk to?
seeker: I don't think so, my parents think I was too harsh by deciding to end the friendship, it as if my own family doesn't understand. 
supporter: That can definitely add to frustration. What about your other friends? Do you have anyone who either shares the same opinion as you or does not know your friend that you can talk to?
seeker: My other friend believed that it wasn't too harsh to end the friendship as they know I value honesty but it makes me feel angry that I was being used for so long and constantly lied to.
supporter: You have every right to be angry, but the most important thing you can do is find a good support system with your other friend. It will take some time to heal, but I'll tell you a paraphrased version of one of my favorite quotes: "Resentment is like swallowing poison and expecting the other person to die." It's important to find support in your other friends and heal properly.
seeker: I really love that quote, it's absolutely true; I think I will talk to my friend about the situation some more so I can fully get over it.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: Yes, I also realized that I wasn't angry with my friend but rather myself 
supporter: Can you elaborate more? Earlier you said you and your friend were arguing while she was living in your house, then she stopped talking to you. Why might you be angry with yourself?
seeker: Because I basically allowed her to use me for seven years and kept lying to me or gave her space because I thought I was being a good friend.
seeker: I feel like I was stupid to do that and soft
supporter: If I may, I would argue that your actions don't make you soft and they certainly don't make you stupid. They are certainly not any reason to be angry with yourself. If I may bring up another cliché: "Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me." I would say you're in the "fool me once" stage and it is your friend's actions that have brought you pain. I think you're unlikely to trust her again.

supporter: Also, hindsight is 20/20. What you might see now in ways that your friend might have used you are things that you might not have seen then. We want to think the best of our friends until they prove us wrong. I think you were being the best friend you could be.
seeker: Thank you very much, I'll continue to talk about the issue with my other friend, I really appreciate your wisdom.  
supporter: Of course. I think you'll be alright and remember the healing process can take a long time after betrayal. Remember to be kind to yourself and keep that support system of your other friend by you. 
supporter: Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: No thank you, enjoy the rest of your day
supporter: You too!

supporter: Your are most welcome. Is there anything else that I can help you with? 
seeker: No Thank you Bye Bye
supporter: Goodbye and good luck!

seeker: I am feeling very sad right now, my boyfriend just broke up with me out of the blue
supporter: I am so sorry that happened to you. It can be very difficult to cope with situations that seem they come out of nowhere. Did your boyfriend give you any reason for ending the relationship?

seeker: He said he has been struggling with depression and needed to be alone

supporter: Sometimes having depression can make a person feel that they need to seclude themselves. Were you aware that he felt this way?
seeker: He has been distant recently.

supporter: Unfortunately that can be a sign of depression or that something is going on. Have you been able to communicate with him previously about becoming distant?
seeker: Every time I would bring it up he would dismiss it. I just don't know what to do. How can I get him back?

supporter: Maybe you could try to talk to him about seeking help for depression? Talking to someone close to him or even a professional would help him immensely. Talking to a counselor would help him learn ways to cope with his feelings.
seeker: That is a good idea. I want him to get back to being himself. He is like a different person right now. It's scary.

supporter: I understand completely. Depression runs in my family and if it goes untreated, can scare anyone that is involved. You can try suggesting that he talks to a close friend, family member, or counselor to talk about how he is feeling and ways to cope with it. Sometimes medication could be a good way to fix the chemical imbalance that can cause depression.
seeker: I will try to help him, he just doesn't want to seem to talk to my anymore. Do you have any suggestions on how to approach it with him?
supporter: You could start a conversation by saying that you just want to check on him and see if he is okay and how he is doing. You don't want to start the conversation by immediately telling him to get help, as he might just get defensive.
seeker: That is a good approach. And you don't think I will further upset him?

supporter: I don't believe it will upset him if you ease into suggesting that he should talk to someone he is close to or seeing a professional. Your main goal is to check on him and make sure that he is okay since he seems to want to be alone and not talk to anyone. Once he tells you how he is doing you could mention that even talking to someone about his thoughts and feelings could lift a weight off his shoulders. If he seems that he doesn't really know why he feels the way does, you could suggest that medically speaking, sometimes our brains don't produce the chemicals that we need them to and it could make us feel bad. Seeing a professional to get their opinion would also help greatly.
seeker: I agree, I hope he is agreeable to all of this. I just miss him so much and want him back.


supporter: It's very hard to see someone we care about go through this.
supporter: Communication is one of the best medicines there is to help someone feel better.
seeker: I just hope he opens up to me, and if not me, someone who can help him.

supporter: Even just trying to talk to him to see how he is doing will show him that care about him. I'm sure that once he is talking to someone about his thoughts and feelings, he will start to get back to his old self.
seeker: I hope so. I also don't feel like myself anymore without him and it has been getting me down. Thank you for the advice, I am hopeful things will work out for us

seeker: Hi

supporter: Hello! How can I encourage you tonight?
seeker: I'm really anxious and I javen

seeker: haven't been sleeping lately

supporter: So you have a lot on your mind and you are losing sleep over it?
seeker: Yeah my company laid off 10% of the workforce last Friday and furloughed another 10%. I'm afraid I'm next

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It can be a bit stressful to think you may lose your job. 
seeker: yeah my mind is racing and I can't stay calm.

supporter: I have found there are ways to calm myself down when things in my life seem very uncertain. 
seeker: Really? What seems to work? I'm willing to try anything right now

supporter: I make a list of the things I can do - And the things I can't. Then you can have goals. And if you can work on a goal, for example, if you need to write a resume, you start working on that a little bit every day until it's done. But if there is nothing you CAN do about the situation, you have to pray to God to help you then LET IT GO. If you can NOT fix it now, you will only make yourself sick thinking about it. 
seeker: I know. I can't seem to shut my mind down.

seeker: And not getting sleep doesn't help

supporter: It is much more difficult for me to remain focused and positive when I lose sleep. I have had to focus on self care, finding a friend to talk about my problems with, not someone who will TELL me what to do, but support me. So you need a good support system. And I find things like prayer, Bible reading, nice soft sheets to sleep on and some herbal tea like Sleepy Time help me relax before bedtime.  
seeker: Those are some helpful points. I didn't think about herbal tea

supporter: And be kind to yourself, no one likes to lose a job, it's unsettling. Do try to tell yourself things that are true to encourage yourself, like you will find another job, it might be uncomfortable and hard, but it actually might work out for your good in the long term.  I always found better jobs, but at the time I lost my job, I felt as if the world was ending.

seeker: Yeah I am really concerned because my wife lost her job this summer so I'm the only breadwinner at the moment

supporter: You aren't in an easy place, but this can actually work out for your good.  I think if you focus on the GOOD that can happen, that might help your more. I would be concerned too, but if you even start looking for a job now, that might help you become more confident. I do encourage you to set goals. 
supporter: I have found that the hard times are often stepping stones to better things, however at the time, all it feels like is hard times! lol
supporter: I'm an older lady - I'm almost 60. So I've had a lot of jobs, retired now, but I remember when my husband kept getting threatened with job layoffs. It was really disheartening for him.
seeker: oh wow

seeker: yeah, I'm so stressed it's not funny

supporter: If I had to do it over again, I would have encouraged him more to get that resume out and look for another job. The threat of losing his job was always hanging over his head. Yeah, it's not worth it my friend. Be pro active.
seeker: I've been trying to look on job boards and company websites but it's hard to find something that is close to the same level of pay. So far the ones I qualify for I will have to take a 25% pay cut or more

supporter: I would also encourage you to get outside and run, or walk or play with the kids or do exercise everyday, because if you are tired physically, that helps reduce stress and helps you sleep.
seeker: Yeah I'll try that. 

seeker: Thanks for all the tips. They're very helpful.

supporter: Sometimes a pay cut in the right company is a stepping stone IN the door, My husband lost a lucrative job one time, he started at a company washing dishes in his 40s, I kid you not, but he wound up moving up and retired early. 
supporter: He wanted to provide for our family, so he was willing to humble himself, Looking back, I'm amazed. But he moved up. Once in that organization, he had lots of open doors, so you never know what God has in store for you. 
seeker: Yeah but with my wife out of a job we can't afford for me to take a pay cut. We're already dipping into savings now.

supporter: I can understand that. Perhaps get together with her and look for ways to cut out spending. These are tough times. Even one car, or chicken instead of steak or canceling netflix or something like that. A few steps back is NOT failure, it can be prioritizing things in a difficult time. 
seeker: ok thanks

supporter: I do want to assure you that even though I don't know you, you sound intelligent and caring and obviously wanting to provide for your family. That's honorable. These are difficult times, I do encourage you to write things down because sometimes stress clouds our eyes and if you set goals and brainstorm, you will be amazed at what you can come up with.

supporter: Hi there, how are you?
seeker: I am doing ok.  How are you?

supporter: I'm doing well, thanks for asking. What are you seeking support for today?
seeker: I have been struggling for motivation to do anything the past couple weeks.  This is a really hard time of year for me.  I lost my cousin in a car accident at the age of 14 in a car accident coming up on 20 years this year.  We were very close.  I was 17 at the time.  Her was an alcoholic and my parents raised her a majority of her life.  Then 3 years ago 5 days after her death anniversary I lost my boyfriend at the age of 32 in a car accident.  I dread the holidays.  
supporter: Thank you for sharing that. It sounds like you are describing a strong association between the holiday season and loss of loved ones. This leads to less of a desire to engage in typical holiday events. Does that sound right?
seeker: You are exactly right.  The year my cousin got killed her mom was hungover so I went and picked up my cousin and her little brother to take them to our grandparents house for Christmas dinner.  She died 4 days later on Dec 29th.  And my boyfriend it was his first day back to work after the New Year.  He died on Jan 3rd. 
seeker: I usually go all out for the holidays to try to hide my depression every year.  This year I just can't bring myself to enjoy them.  I have even bought one christmas present.

supporter: I can see why this time of year is difficult for you. Trying to hide depression can be a challenge. Rather than hiding the sadness or grieving feelings, some people find relief in acknowledging and sharing these feelings with family members who may relate. Do you ever share these feelings with your cousin or grandparents that you mentioned?
seeker: My cousin doesn't live around here and we have never been real close.  He is alot younger than me.  We just never had the connection like his sister and I did.  And both my grandparents have passed away.  Grandpa has been gone for 12 years and Grandma has been gone for 4 now.
seeker: My family has always been really good about talking about our loses. Things just will never be the same.  
supporter: I understand. When losses are experienced it is a great change in many aspects of our lives. 
supporter: Are there any aspects of the holidays that bring you joy? Maybe holiday music, movies, bright snow (if there is snow where you live), or seeing joy on someone's face when you give them a great gift?
seeker: They say it gets easier. And I agree it does.  Things just have changed so much.  I miss how life was before I lost them.
supporter: I understand - and it is normal to feel that way. When we lose someone who brought us happiness, it is only natural to miss them and their company. 
seeker: I love giving gifts.  And I always put lots of thought into the gifts I give.  My nieces and nephews can't wait every year to see what I got them.  
supporter: That's great! You must have a special talent for personalizing your gift selections. Perhaps focus on that reaction from you nieces and nephews to support your motivation for giving gifts this year. 
seeker: This year I am tie dying hooded sweatshirts.  I make tshirts for a hobby.  And to tell you the truth thats the only gifts I have gotten so far.  My oldest daughter turned 18 this year and lives with her boyfriend so its just me and my 15 year old daughter.  She struggles with depression/anxiety as well.  Her dad has been in jail for some stupid actions since August.  She has had to deal with him being an addict pretty much her whole life.  I think we are both missing how the holidays were with her sister still living at home.  Too much change in our lives in such a little time frame.
supporter: Wow, what a great gift idea! That is a solid start on your gifts for the season, and something to be proud of. 
seeker: They will love them.  A couple years ago I put their names on fleece blankets when I worked at an embroidery shop.  They absolutly loved them!
supporter: And I see, it sounds like the changes in your life are potentially impacting your daughter as well. However, I'm glad you have each other for support this season. This year has been crazy for many reasons, and many people tend to find comfort in routines or traditions. Do you and your daughters have any holiday traditions you typically complete?
supporter: Awesome gift idea! Personalized gifts are always so heartfelt and appreciated. Good thinking!
seeker: Just the normal traditions.  My oldest daughter will be here for Christmas morming.  Then we go to my parents.  
seeker: Thank you for chatting with me tonight!  I hope you have a good rest of your night.

supporter: Great minds think alike! Is there anything else you wanted to bring up with me today?

supporter: you are right about others looking for work too. Are you signed up with many job seeking apps?

supporter: You mentioned feeling down in the beginning of the conversation, would you like to talk about that?

supporter: When I am feeling especially low or tense, I find that helping others significantly helps my disposition.

seeker: Hello
supporter: hi my name is Lisa, how are you?




seeker: I'm struggling to make it through the day. My daughter was hit by a car in September and the traumatic experience is weighing heavy on my brain.
supporter: it sounds like you are feeling troubled after your daughter's car accident am I right?
seeker: Troubled would not be the word I would use, but it wasn't a car accident. She was hit by a car in the street outside of my house.

seeker: She was coming home from school. She is only 5.

supporter: that sounds like it would be a very traumatic experience, it's no wonder this is hard for you, it would be hard for anyone in this situation
seeker: I have a hard time getting out of bed in the morning.

supporter: How  would you use to describe your feelings about this accident?

seeker: I would say that I am anxious all the time. She survived, but she had some serious injuries after. I feel like a part of me died that day, the part that thought I could protect her no matter what. I would say that I'm also feeling ashamed because it was out of my control.

supporter: It sounds like you are dealing with a lot...it is normal to feel anxious about it
seeker: Is that how you would feel?

supporter: and it's hard not to blame ourselves, but please remember this was outside your control
seeker: thank you for saying that. I quit my job to focus on her healing, and i don't want to go back to work now.

supporter: I have not experienced anything like this to be honest....the closest I can recall is encouraging my daughter to do something, and then she got hurt, and I blamed myself and felt like a bad mother
supporter: how is your daughter doing now?
seeker: She is healing well, she has a moderate TBI (traumatic brain injury) so there is still so much uncertainty. It sucks to blame ourselves for things that happen to our kids. 

supporter: the fact that you felt the need to quit your job shows how deeply this has affected you...do you miss your work?
seeker: No. And I'm completely dreading going back to work. I wish I could somehow get paid to exist so that I can just stay home with my daughter all day.

supporter: it sounds like you need to be with your daughter all day but also need the income that work would afford, am i right?
seeker: YES. And if you can figure out how to make that happen I'll give you 10% of the salary lol.

supporter: hehe...0% is all I'd ask for...
supporter: how about part time work would that be possible for you?
seeker: I've been looking for a remote part time job that has pay equivalent to a full time job. Apparently, that's not a thing.

supporter: i see...I would not know how to find such a job, i've often thought that would be a great thing to do..
supporter: i have a question

seeker: What's your question.

supporter: is there a friend or family member that can spend time with your daughter so it's easier to get back to maybe a part time job?
seeker: I don't have a family. Just my daughter, and my boyfriend who lives in Australia that can't come here due to Covid restrictions. She does see her Dad everyday, but the part time hours I would need would have to be flexible and no company is even really hiring part time at the moment from what I can tell.

supporter: I see. I wonder if you have spoken to a doctor about how you feel?  Struggling to get through the day must be so difficult.  I wonder if it might be helpful to get screened for depression
seeker: I have a psychiatrist and a therapist that I have been working with. Their solution is medication which I am extremely against.

seeker: hey

supporter: I'm sure it will take dedication and hard work, but I bet you can do it!
seeker: I think so. Im doing mturk for a second job right now. it helps some. i don't know about getting another job 

supporter: I've been in your shoes and also feel that's a good way to add a little extra income. It can really add up if left to built and used towards a specific goal.
seeker: I agree 100%. Been spending it on new clothes and toiletries lately to stock up for the covid shutdown. the extra money helps alot

supporter: It definitely can help. Perhaps you could have a separate way of using some of the money to go towards some of the other bills you would like to pay off? Maybe designate a certain percentage for what you are using it towards now, and the rest to other bill concerns.
seeker: i currently do that. it's hard to have the patience to pay it off. i hate having debt hanging over my head. i like to have nice things though and they cost money

supporter: Yes, and I have found this can be a good way to provide for the extra luxuries we like, without taking away from money that's used towards household bills.

seeker: oh wow, thank ya! I'll look into that 

seeker: MTS is a script? Which script should I use?

supporter: Of course, I hope it can be of use too you! One I use is Mechanical Turk Suite, which is an extension. I think you can look up as a search for extensions, scripts etc. Or Mturk forums and find out tons of help!

seeker: Thank ya! I'll check it out

supporter: You're welcome! Best of Luck!
seeker: Thank ya! Have a good night. Bye

supporter: I think you have it. You too.
seeker: Thank ya!. Bye

External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
seeker: My boyfriend broke up with me.
supporter: Hello there, how are you? 

seeker: I'm very upset.
seeker: He yelled and yelled at me.
supporter: Your relationship has ended? I am very sorry about that. And your boyfriend ended it? 
supporter: That was really wrong of him if you ask me. I think you might be better off without him. 
seeker: Yes, after seeing him act this way I agree
seeker: He said I was worthless.
supporter: I have been in this position myself and I know how painful it is but it turned out for the best for me - I now have a great relationship! 
seeker: Well that's good for you, but I'm so mad right now I can't see straight!
supporter: Noone has the right to put you down like that. You really are better off without him. 
seeker: I know. I do deserve better. But I was with him a very long time.
supporter: Can you think of something to do that will take your mind off him? 
supporter: How long were the two of you together? 
seeker: More than a year, but I've known him since childhood.
seeker: That's what makes me so mad!
supporter: He should not be treating you that way when you've known one another so long! 
seeker: All those years of friendship down the drain.
seeker: Should I call him?
supporter: I think that you should call one of your girlfriends and suggest you have a movie night. It would make you feel better 
seeker: But all of my friends are still friends with him!
seeker: And they took his side!
supporter: Oh that is rough. That happened to me too when I broke up with my ex. 
seeker: How did you get through it?
supporter: They all took his side? Not one took yours? 
seeker: Not one!
supporter: I tried to find some new interests. One thing I did was take a salsa class .. that was a great way to meet new people 
seeker: I'm not much of a dancer, but that might be a way to meet new people.
supporter: There are lots of other things you could do. Maybe you could take an evening class in something that interests you? 
seeker: He's a teacher, so taking a class might remind me of him.
supporter: I think also you need to think a bit more highly of yourself and not let idiots like this treat you so badly 
seeker: But maybe I deserved it.
supporter: he seems to have damaged your self esteem badly 
seeker: Yes, he did.
supporter: No you did not! Please don't think like that 
seeker: I'm just so angry that I could break something.
seeker: And maybe I will do that!
supporter: I think that that is a normal reaction to feeling ill treated. I hope that it will pass soon and am sure that it will. 
supporter: There are a lot of therapy groups available that might be able to help you through this 
seeker: But what if it doesn't pass?
seeker: And I cannot afford therapy.
supporter: I think you really need to take it one day at a time. Things are very raw for you right now 

supporter: There are some organisations that will offer a certain number of sessions for free 
seeker: I don't know if I could do that. I don't like talking about my problems with strangers.
supporter: And yet here we are :P. Therapy can be surprisingly beneficial, I have found. 

supporter: I do realise that it can be hard to open up to how we are feeling though. I know that I was 
seeker: Do you have any suggestions about how to open up to people I don't know?
supporter: I think that is useful to remember that we are all human and that most people have been hurt in this way at some point. No-one will be judging you 

seeker: That's what I am afraid of. Being judged by people.
supporter: Do you think that this might partly because your ex has eroded your self esteem? 

seeker: Probably. He called me a lot of names.
supporter: The important thing is to gradually rebuild your self esteem. Do you have any things that you excel at? 

seeker: I'm good at bowling. And I like riding horses.
supporter: Animals are a wonderful source of comfort when we are feeling very low! Could you join a riding club to make some new friends? 
seeker: Maybe I will do that. Horses are so cool.
supporter: I can feel that you are starting to make progress already and are thinking of things that you can do post break up 

seeker: I sure am. Thanks for your help.
supporter: You are most welcome. Is there anything else you would like to talk to me about? 
seeker: I don't think so...
supporter: Well, I wish you all the very best for the future. I know that things seem terrible right now but please believe me they will get better 

seeker: Thanks! Have a good day.
supporter: And you have a lovely day too. I know that you are going to be just fine in a few weeks from now. Stay strong!

seeker: Hello

supporter: Hello. What seems to be the issue?

seeker: I don't have close friends because I don't trust people

supporter: You said you generally don't trust family or people in general?

seeker: people in general, I do trust certain family members

supporter: Just people who are close to you?

seeker: no, I have a hard time trusting people i don't know in order to make friends

supporter: I have had a hard time trusting strangers, but that is not a big problem.
supporter: I used to be the same way, but I learned about how to make and keep close friends.
seeker: i think it feels like a problem because I never let anyone too close in order to make friends and have an external support system

seeker: how did you do it

supporter: I joined volunteer groups to help others.  I made friends with like-minded people who volunteered to make a difference.
seeker: I actually think that is a great idea.  I have never thought of doing that for that specific purpose.

supporter: Groups like Habitat for Humanity or UNICEF will help you to build long-lasting friendships.
supporter: It just takes finding the right volunteer groups and being willing to be pro-active.
seeker: I guess it makes a lot of sense.  If you go to a party or a bar, you don't know what you will get, as it is a mixed bag of personalities.  Whereas if you go to something like what you suggested then you already know that the people you meet have the same kind of heart.

supporter: You can do it. I have faith that you can use volunteering as the right method.
seeker: Thank you for that suggestion, that is really helpful and something that I will take with me from now on.  

supporter: Exactly, volunteering is a great option. And there are many organizations to join.
supporter: Did you need help with anything else?
seeker: I feel ok being alone mostly, but other times I would like to have people I could relate with and hang out with.  Probably has a lot to do with ADHD and how I feel misunderstood or my anxiety gets the best of me in social situations

supporter: I understand the ADHD.  There are support groups that can help you make friends; especially with ADHD, etc.
seeker: do you know any specific groups?

supporter: Using tools to build houses helps to release endorphins, which can release anxiety.
seeker: is this something you have done?

supporter: There is a group called, "Harry House" that provides support to those with ADHD and anxiety.
seeker: oh ok! I will certainly look that up, thank you for that information.

supporter: Surely. Is there anything else you need help with?
seeker: Does one have to travel far to participate in building houses?

supporter: No, Habitat fir Humanity has car pools. 
seeker: do you know if it requires a person to be away from home a long time?

supporter: They are a good group to help you build meaningful relationships.
supporter: I used to do a hour at a time; maybe one or twice a week.
seeker: oh! so a person could just choose how often and how long they participate?

supporter: Would you be interested in something like HFH?
seeker: thank you for sharing with me, i might like to participate in it in the future

supporter: Yes, you can sign up online to join a project.
seeker: ok i will look that up, thank you for all your help

supporter: Yes, you can volunteer locally; HFH is nationwide.
seeker: ok thank you

supporter: Any other questions? I am glad to assist.
seeker: no other questions, you have been most helpful, thank you!
supporter: I have done volunteer work; people want to be friends with those who care and know how to use a nail and hammer. :)
seeker: LOL good to know!

seeker: Thanks for the chat and I hope you have good holidays!

supporter: It may also help to contribute some money to keep the organization going. 
supporter: I felt great after making friends and building homes for low income people.

seeker: The only thing I can think of was that California was getting too expensive and the homeless were taking over LA; that may have spooked her to leave the state.
supporter: Wow, that's horrible. It seems you should have some kind of legal authority in that aspect.
supporter: Is that a big problem out there?

supporter: That's mid-boggling..
seeker: I am D-I-S-G-U-S-T-E-D to the Nth degree.
supporter: Do you have any hobbies?
seeker: Any help to get her to come back would help.
seeker: My hobbies are on hold.....I need to get "un-disgusted" first.
supporter: Well, I can't make her come back, but I can provide you with some information on how to get through these tough times.
seeker: ok.
seeker: I am all ears.....
supporter: I understand, it can be good to help get some stress out in other ways. Do you excercise?
supporter: What kind of hobbies do you have?
seeker: I have a gym membership....if they are even open with the COVID-19.
seeker: Maybe I can just jog or speed walk every day.  Perhaps pushups can help?
supporter: I like to run every morning, and it seems to help make alot of stress evaporate.
seeker: Oh, that may just help me relax and think about other things besides my wifey and twin kiddos.
seeker: Well, your input has helped.
supporter: I have found for me anyway, that running is an amazing stress reliever.
seeker: I will mull your insights over.  Good bye.

supporter: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.
supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?
seeker: I'd just like to find some peace with it, I guess. Maybe closure or even a chance to talk about it calmly.
supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.
supporter: You're definitely not alone, Taylor. I'm always here to listen whenever you need.

seeker: Hi there

supporter: Hello, how are you today?
seeker: I'm not feeling great. I applied for a job recently which took a lot of time. I now have an interview and it's in 3 days. I'm getting really nervous about this because I think I need longer to prepare. 

supporter: I know how you feel, I have often felt anxiety before a job interview. 
supporter: What makes you feel that you are unprepared?
seeker: The thing is I'm really good at interviews but usually it takes time to prepare. It's a corporate interview so I need to prepare behavioural answers to certain scenarios. In the past this has taken me a week to learn and record to memory

supporter: Is it possible that you could get a friend or family member to work with you on your responses? That could possibly speed up your preparation time.
seeker: Yes perhaps. I need to draw on previous experience so I think I'll need to prepare. I'm just so busy at work these days I just don;t think I'll have the time.
 
supporter: I can see that you are feeling a large amount of stress about the situation.
supporter: Would it be possible to take one or more days off from work to give yourself more time?
seeker: Yes this is very stressful. Have you ever had a similar experience and if so how did you handle it?

seeker: Potentially but this is very short notice, usually I have to provide more notice for leave from work.

supporter: Yes, I have had to deal with time pressures quite a few times. I am sure most people have in the modern era where everything moves so fast. I have usually gotten help from friends, or done my best to delay or remove other commitments from my life. As a last resort, I have sometimes had to accept that I would be getting less sleep than usual for a few days. 
supporter: Are there any other commitments that you can possibly delay or remove from your life while you prepare for your job interview?
seeker: Perhaps I can ask if I can finish early from work for the next couple of days and get some time that way. I do think however I'll be more nervous due to less time to prepare. The thing is I'd delay the interview but this might affect my chances.

seeker: I suppose I could ask my partner to look after the childcare for the next couple of days.

supporter: That seems like a good idea, unless that will be likely to cause you other problems. You seem like a hard working, diligent type of person that can make this work if you make the effort.
seeker: Tanks , I think I need to stay positive about this. Not sure how to handle my interview nerves however?

supporter: Well, everyone handles stressful situations differently, but there are some things you can do or try that might help. If you prepare as much as possible in the time that you have, you can be confident that you have done your best, and that is all that matters. You can decide that while you would like to get this new job, the world will not end if you don't get it, and you will worry less and have less stress. Also there is the classic technique of picturing your interviewer in their underwear. It makes them seem less imposing, and you can feel more confident.
supporter: Do you think any of these ideas might help?
seeker: There are actually some great suggestions there. The naked idea is a classic and it did make me smile. I think I am aiming for perfection when I think I should try and relax and just give it my best shot. That does help actually!

supporter: Be confident in your abilities. You are the right person for the job, and if the interviewer does not see that, it is their failing, not yours. You will do great.
seeker: Thanks for that. I think the key to this is confidence so I'll go with it. Feeling more relaxed about it all now,

supporter: Excellent. I am very happy to hear that. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
seeker: No that's great. Thanks from your help

supporter: You are quite welcome. It was a pleasure speaking with you. Have a great day.

seeker: it was good talking to you.

supporter: Hello, How are you feeling today?
seeker: sad and lonely

supporter: I see you are feeling sad and lonely, is there anything going on right now to enhance those feelings?

seeker: The election and COVID are making it worse.

supporter: There is a lot going on right now, but i see you said its making it worse. What may be the root cause?

seeker: I have no one to share my deepest feelings with at this moment. 
supporter: I understand having it seem like there is no one to talk to. I am here and there are others. I believe you can find an outlet to share.

seeker: Where do you suggest I look? 
supporter: I would first start to try and feel connected. There are many online forums, that perhaps you can join in on things that interest you

seeker: How about local groups? How do I find someone with like minds?
supporter: Local, and safe, meetings are a good start as well. Have you tried looking for any online local spots? Or in a local news paper? Its great you are coming up with ideas already.

seeker: I really like to play tennis. That may be a good spot. Have you tried Tinder or Match?

supporter: Those are more for a quicker deeper connection. I would try to cast a broad net. Maybe with Meetup or Nextdoor. 
seeker: What is Nextdoor?
supporter: It is an app to get you connected to your local community and neighbors.
seeker: That sounds great. Does it have special sections for specific groups?

supporter: I believe it does have subsections but it is more of a general hang out for neighbors to keep up with each other.
seeker: That's cool. I should check it out. I feel like a book club would help. Do you like books?

supporter: I do love books. They are a great way to get connected with yourself and enhance your creative side! I bet you could find a local book club on one of those apps.
seeker: For sure. Books are great. You have been very helpful. What's you first name so I can thank you properly?

supporter: Rachel, and no need to thank me! Being able to help is the greatest reward!
seeker: Thank you Rachel. Best of luck to you. I'm going to end it now.
supporter: I wish you the best as well!

reading_text:
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hi, how are you? What would you like to talk about today?
seeker: Hi - I'm sorry. I stepped away from the computer for a moment while waiting... 
supporter: That's quite all right. The wait times can be a bit long. How are you?
seeker: Well, my manager has decided that everyone in the office will continue to work from after the pandemic is under control. But I've found myself depressed from working from home all the time.

supporter: Working from home is not what people expected. Many have found themselves isolated. They miss the interaction of the office. How long have you bee working from home?
seeker: For a full year--since March 2020, when the pandemic first started. I was working from home just 1 day per week prior to that, which I liked. But I've found that 5 days per week is much too much. I miss people. :( 
supporter: Have you and your co-workers talked to your boss about a hybrid schedule, maybe a couple days a week in the office? That might work. 
seeker: That's where it gets awkward. It seems like everyone besides me are super happy that we'll continue working from home. I hesitate to share my feelings because maybe my manager will change her mind, which would be a big bummer for everyone else on the team (seemingly).
supporter: I see. That's a concern. So you feel that if one person goes in to the office, then everyone else will have to? There won't be any flexibility?
seeker: Well, it's possible that my manager will say we can be flexible. But if so, I think I'd end up being the only one in my office working... which would be just as lonely as working from home while throwing away the few perks of working from home, like saving on gas. Plus, I think my company will probably want to repurpose our office space eventually.

seeker: lol, sorry, that was an ugly run-on sentence. :\

supporter: Hm. A bit of a dilemma. Can this situation go on forever though? Maybe the boss will extend the stay-at-home for a while, but when other companies go back to the office, the expectation will be there for all companies.
supporter: Other employees might change their minds bit by bit as well. 
seeker: That is indeed a possibility. But my office is in a city that has a whole lot of high-tech companies, which were moving towards doing more work from home even BEFORE the pandemic. So it kind of feels like this might be a "cultural shift" in my area in general. Although there has GOT to be a whole lot of other people who feel like I do. Maybe we should start our own company, lol.
 
supporter: True. I don't think you are alone. Is there something that you can do to make working at home better for you? More frequent breaks? Better work space?
seeker: That's a good question. My state is still one of the ones that's mostly shut-down. Part of my depression surely stems from the fact that all evening/weekend activities ended a year ago as well.
supporter: True. It might be easier to work at home when you have a chance to get out of the house during your free time. 
seeker: That's true. And your suggestion of improving my work space is a good one. I've been working in a modified walk-in closet. I've tried to make it inviting, but there are no windows/etc.... it's kind of a dark cave.

supporter: Most people didn't plan for the long term because nobody thought that this was a sustainable way to work. By the way, if your company wants you to stay home, then it might help buy the equipment you need to be productive. 
seeker: That's a good thought. My computer is set-up on a folding card table. (I tried finding a desk a while back, but there was a huge shortage since everyone suddenly had to buy them for themselves, kids, etc.). I hadn't thought of asking my company to buy me one. Plus a more comfy chair could improve my attitude.

supporter: I think if you talk to your co-workers, they'll have ideas for upgrading your workspace. 
seeker: That's a great idea. Maybe I should set-up a "virtual happy hour" where we can exchanged the tips/tricks we've learned to make working from home more enjoyable this past year.

supporter: I think that's a great idea! People probably want to connect without having to talk about work. Later on, they might want to do the same thing but face-to-face. 
seeker: You're right! Well, thank you so much for your help.... and you TRULY did help me put this all into perspective. Sincerely, thanks! :)

supporter: Sure! My pleasure. Best of luck with all that! Have a great weekend!
seeker: Thanks! You too! Bye

supporter: Is there a quit/finish button on your end?

seeker: Hello

supporter: Hi! How are you today?
seeker: I have been better 

supporter: It sounds like you might be upset. Can you tell me what’s going on?
seeker: My ex partner and I broke up a long time ago because they cheated on me. Now they will not stop contacting my friends and family and posting about me on social media

supporter: That sounds difficult and stressful. What do you do when you see it happening?
seeker: I usually just document it and try to not go online for a while. It is hard to ignore

supporter: It sounds like you are avoiding things you enjoy because of their actions. I think documenting it is a good idea! Have you tried reporting them for harassing you?
seeker: I have tried but everyone just tells me there is nothing they can do because they don't think it is dangerous or criminal at this point 
supporter: That must be very frustrating. Can you tell me if you’ve tried other things to get them to stop? 
seeker: I have confronted them in person but it was dramatic to say the least. They basically had a meltdown that they don't want to lose me 
supporter: You tried to do the right thing and they are having a difficult time letting go. The ongoing comments through social media sounds like they are wanting your attention. That can be exhausting for you. In my past, I had to block someone who did something similar to me. If my friends mentioned seeing something from my ex about me, I asked them to keep it to themselves or consider blocking them,too. The people who were closest to me understood what was going on and I realized that people who didn’t know me, didn’t matter. Would you be willing to suggest this to friends or family if it would help to remove the ex from your interactions?

supporter: I see. How long has this been going on and is this a daily occurrence or does it happen at certain times?
seeker: It has been happening for at least 6 months now and it usually happens every weekend

supporter: I can sense your frustration. It must be overwhelming at times and make you dread the weekends. It sounds like it has become a habit for your ex. It might help if you write a letter to them explaining that you are ready to move on and are asking them to do the same. Explain that you are giving them the opportunity to stop harassing you in the following ways [list some of the details you have documented]. Inform them that if they do not stop, you are considering taking it further regarding harassing communications and that this letter serves as your intention to no longer tolerate their actions. Send it via certified mail and keep a copy. This will give them no way to immediately respond and would be the first step of official documentation should they decide to continue.  Do you think that might help?
seeker: I think that is an excellent idea! That is a good way to end this once and for all. 

supporter: I sincerely hope it is a step toward you regaining your control  over how you are able to interact with people. I wish you the best in dealing with this and hope you begin to feel better about it soon, especially entering into a new year! 
seeker: Thank you very much!

supporter: That sounds perfect. Remember, small steps add up. With everything you're juggling, make sure to celebrate these wins, no matter how small.
