supporter: Hi! How are you tonight?
seeker: I've been better. I just buried my dog yesterday
seeker: She was going to turn 15 next month
supporter: Ouch! I'm so sorry to hear that. I never lost a dog, but I've lost cats. 
supporter: Is 14 a good age for a dog?
supporter: I have my first dog so I don't know much, he is 9 years old and came with our house. 
seeker: Actually, yes. She was old and had dementia.
seeker: The oldest dog I evet had was 15
supporter: I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us. 
seeker: How did your dog come with the house?
supporter: Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? We moved from FL to KY and the little dog just hung out here, he really belonged to the neighbor's son who didn't want him, so he just ran around wild and wouldn't leave. I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.
supporter: I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.
seeker: I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2
seeker: Thank you. that means a lot
seeker: We both had dogs when we met.
supporter: So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol
supporter: I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it! 
seeker: They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes
supporter: I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.
supporter: I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.
seeker: Thanks. Another person who has pets helps
seeker: They understand
supporter: I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.
supporter: I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog. 
seeker: Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.
supporter: Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed. 
seeker: That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.
supporter: I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D
seeker: You too. Thanks so much. bye
supporter: I have one more thing to say - wise words from this 92 year old lady at church named Sue. She told me this after my brother died. When you get older, everyone you know is practically dead.  She said "Life is for the living, if you get caught up to much in all the death, you won't life."  True words. God bless, have a good night.

seeker: Oh that's a good idea - in public and not making a big deal about it - and before she moves teams and rumors get worse. 
supporter: That is exactly right. Each person handles and avoids conflict differently and you have the important roll as leader in all of this.  of any stress this has caused.

supporter: Hello.
seeker: Hello

supporter: How are you today?

seeker: Really bad. My 10 year marriage is failing. Things have not gotten better.

supporter: What happened?

seeker: That's the thing. Nothing really happened. No cheating, drugs, or abuse. I suppose the euphoria has worn off, and she just doesn't find me interesting anymore.
supporter: I understand how you feel. Have you guys tried spending more time with each other? Maybe going out on dates?
seeker: Maybe we haven't done this enough in the past. We both had busy careers. I tried initiating this last year, but without success. Maybe, I was too late. 
supporter: Its never too late to put spice back into the relationship.

seeker: I hope you're right. Do you have other suggestions about how to do so?
supporter: Show her that your still love because by being spontaneous. Surprise her with gifts. Maybe take her on a random vacation somewhere. Have a deep conversation about how you are feeling and that you still love her and want her in your life.
supporter: It might take a little bit but its better to try than not to try at all.

seeker: I think your suggestions are very helpful. A vacation is currently out of the picture due to COVID. I want to try having deep conversations, but I don't know where to start.
supporter: Start by talking about whats going on. Tell her how you think you guys should spend more time with her. Or that you dont want to lose her. Ask her if there is anything she might want to discuss. She maybe having issues shes afraid to talk about.

seeker: I think you hit upon something. She is quite hesitant in talking about issues. Do you have any thoughts about marriage counselling? We've never tried that.
supporter: I think that would be a good idea. Having the chance to get things out and getting more advice is always helpful. Make sure you leave any issues at common ground.
seeker: If my wife is the one having issues with conversations, do you think a male or female therapist/counsellor would be better? I want her to feel comfortable expressing herself.
supporter: Most likely a female therapist would be better. Nobody understands a woman more than a woman.
seeker: I think that sounds like a safer choice. I was also hoping if you have suggestions for me personally. I am quite depressed and I am having problems getting through the day.
supporter: I suggest taking one step at a time. I wouldn't rush through things. I would suggest sitting down and talking through some things that are going on. Maybe taking some time away from work. Going out and spending time with each other as much as you can. 
supporter: If you guys think you may need a marriage counselor, I highly recommend it. I think it would be a great start.

seeker: Thank you very much for your response. You have been very helpful. Perhaps, one last question - my wife and I have been hiding our problems away from our teen-age son. Do you agree that we should continue to keep it from him?
supporter: Depending on the nature, I think you should let him know whats going on. He may already know.
seeker: Ok, thanks for all your help again. I feel much better now, and hopefully I will get through this.
supporter: I know its really hard, but I think you guys with work things out. Have hope. Times are stressful, especially in this day and age.
seeker: Take care, friend, good-bye
supporter: goodbye

seeker: Hello there.

supporter: Good evening . How can I help you
seeker: I'm having a problem with one of my friends.

supporter: So you are having issues with your friend? That is upsetting . What is the issue?
seeker: She has been having a problem with a different friend for years. I have been listening to these problems for all of that time. And even though it's so frustrating, because it's the same problem over and over again, I keep listening because she's my friend. But lately I have been going through a lot, and I haven't had as much time to sit and listen to these same problems, and she gets so angry telling me I don't care about her. The problems I've been going through are very serious, and I just don't have time to sit on the phone listening to the same stuff I've been dealing with for years.

supporter: I can understand how angry unappreciated and burnt out you must be feeling.  I would feel that way too
seeker: It's been really rough. I've tried so hard to be there for her, and I feel like she just doesn't even appreciate it.

supporter: I don't think she is a place to be able to see anyone but herself. She is self centereed self asbored and self pity party and doesn't care about anyone but herself right now . Is that accurate?
seeker: Yes, that's exactly accurate. And she is 50 years old, and the issues have all been high school type problems that I've been listening to. Stuff about how she didn't post on social media about her birthday, and little petty things like that. Not something an adult should be concerned with. And I still sat and listened to her all that time.

supporter: I completely understand how unappreciated and stressed this would make you or any person. Especially when our plate is full and its the same old same old and nothing is changing. Its like thinking doing same thing over and over you will get a different result when 2+2 equals 4
seeker: Yes, exactly.

supporter: You are an extremely good and loyal friend and I am so proud of you. Most people would have left her.  
seeker: Thank you. That's really important to me. She was starting to convince me that I wasn't a good friend because I wasn't there for her right now when I had problems of my own. Real problems - like my daughter's engagement breaking up.

supporter: However, it is time to take the hard road. YOu are going to have to say with LOVE because its not always what you say but how you say it.  Give me a minute to please type it
seeker: Okay, thank you.

supporter: You are going to have to sit her down and say  I need to be honest with you.  I have always been there for you but you are not willing to take my advice or others advice and quite frankly I just can't do it anymore. IF you want to remain friends I need you to grow up and realize the world doesn't revolve around you or even me.  Right now I could really use a good friend. seeker: I'm feeling rather sad. I used to have a very close-knit group of friends, basically my best friends. We would talk all the time, hang out together, and basically just do everything together. Because of Covid, I've had to stay in my house and basically not associate with anyone else. My friends don't even try to talk to me anymore. I understand that life goes on without me, but they could at least try. 

seeker: They never even offered to wear a mask around me. They would make fun of me when I wore a mask. They didn't support my decisions when I was trying to still be a part of the group while also protecting my family (since they are all high risk)

supporter: So what I hear you saying is that since COVID your friends won't talk to you and that they make fun of you for wanting to wear a mask and protect yourself?


seeker: Yes. Sure they've tried to stay in touch but it's always me starting the conversation. Or if they start it, it only involves "hi how're you, good how're you," and then the conversation ends.

supporter: I am sorry to hear that your friends have been so distant lately.  Have you tried to ask them why they have been this way?
seeker: Yes. They say that because I'm not hanging out with them physically, it's hard. They also say that I don't put effort into conversations when I feel like I am the only one putting in effort (which I have stated and they have said I don't).

supporter: So what I hear you saying is that they have backed away from you because you have chosen to take precautions due to COVID and they are choosing to not? Is that correct?
seeker: Yes this is correct. 
supporter: Well you are being smart by doing the right thing and protecting yourself and others during this time.  You should not feel bad about what you are doing.
seeker: Thank you. I just don't know what to do in this situation. I don't want to keep reaching out when I don't feel like they actually want to keep in contact with me. I know we could still get along well, but it's hard when I'm the only one to make the effort. 

supporter: Do you have any other friends besides this group?  Do you have other people that you could reach out to that are social distancing that you could relate to more during this time that you would have more in common with right now?
seeker: I have very few that have similar thoughts as me that I have tried to reach out to. But most of them have their own lives, boyfriends/girlfriends, and things they do. Mostly everyone seems to be hanging out with people which leaves me physically left out. 
supporter: What hobbies or activities do you like to do?
seeker: I play field hockey so I train a lot in my basement (because I'm scared to go out to the gym), I listen to music, read, watch Christmas movies, and I love talking to people.

supporter: I understand that you feel that you would look desperate but you said you like reading book so there may be some online book clubs that you could join.  I know that I have been involved in those and I didn't feel like I was seen as desperate since there are so many people that want to be social but don't want to put themselves at risk.

supporter: Hi there! I'm great, what about you? How can I help today?

supporter: That's tough... so you're saying that you grew apart a little? Or do you think it was more one-sided?

supporter: I completely understand, and I don't think you should beat yourself up over it!

supporter: Why are you freaking out?
seeker: I think that'll help, yeah

supporter: Sometimes just a friend to hear you out and encourage you can really make a difference. Life has its ups and down. 
seeker: I decided to leave my husband, he keeps snapping at me and won't listen to me or let me do anything
supporter: That's a difficult decision you have made. 
seeker: I'm worried how it'll go though because we have kids
supporter: Have you tried to talk to him about the problem? Or a counselor?

supporter: I have worked at a domestic violence shelter before, the most dangerous time to leave a situation like this is when you leave.  Do you have a plan in place?
seeker: I have some leads on apartments and some savings I'm putting aside, and a friend I plan on living with
supporter: My husband used to be very controlling as well, I dragged him to counseling. He changed. He bucked at first, but eventually he went. We have gone a few times off and on over 20 years. We both came from broken homes.  

seeker: I haven't got 100% of the details worked out yet, but I'm trying
supporter: Has he hurt you physically? or is he mainly emotionally abusive? 

seeker: He hasn't hurt me physically
seeker: I often feel like he would but I'm also a child abuse survivor so it's hard to tell if that's true or just a memory
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. I can understand that you would be really stressed at this time, however, I do encourage you to get a good plan in place, and definitely get counseling. 
seeker: I think that's the best idea
supporter: Yes, I had child abuse in my life too, I really think counseling saved our marriage, 3 times. But like, I said, he didn't want to go. However, the first time, I did leave and stay with a friend, and that convinced him I was serious. 
seeker: that's a good thought, I wonder what he'd do if I stayed with a friend
supporter: I wish I could fix this, but I can't. The road will be rocky and I don't know how I would have made it without people to encourage and support me, so I'm glad a friend is willing to have you stay with them until you can get on your feet.

seeker: me too, that's making all the difference

seeker: definitely that makes sense
supporter: He feared I would die or leave him or something, but once he saw that, and realized what he was doing was hurting me and making me want to leave, he changed. supporter: Ouch! That sounds painful to look at.

seeker: eight years, together for 11
supporter: That's a long time. I will say a prayer for your safety and for you to get some help, hopefully he will join you. Marriage is a lot of work, but it can't be one person, it has to be two. 
supporter: Don't leave anything in writing around until after you leave. 
seeker: absolutely!
seeker: definitely no paper trail, for sure
supporter: I believe in the power of prayer too. The Serenity prayer is a good one to help me let go of my fears and do what I can, leaving the rest to God.

supporter: If I worry and get upset, then I waste energy, I have had to learn to get distracted if I find myself on that worry train, call a friend, go for a walk, just not obsess, it goes nowhere.

source_refs.exact_quote: I have some leads on apartments and some savings I'm putting aside, and a friend I plan on living with
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: My husband used to be very controlling as well, I dragged him to counseling. He changed. He bucked at first, but eventually he went. We have gone a few times off and on over 20 years. We both came from broken homes.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I haven't got 100% of the details worked out yet, but I'm trying
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: Has he hurt you physically? or is he mainly emotionally abusive?
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: He hasn't hurt me physically
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I often feel like he would but I'm also a child abuse survivor so it's hard to tell if that's true or just a memory
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I'm glad to hear that. I can understand that you would be really stressed at this time, however, I do encourage you to get a good plan in place, and definitely get counseling.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I think that's the best idea
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: Yes, I had child abuse in my life too, I really think counseling saved our marriage, 3 times. But like, I said, he didn't want to go. However, the first time, I did leave and stay with a friend, and that convinced him I was serious.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: that's a good thought, I wonder what he'd do if I stayed with a friend
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I wish I could fix this, but I can't. The road will be rocky and I don't know how I would have made it without people to encourage and support me, so I'm glad a friend is willing to have you stay with them until you can get on your feet.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: hey may not realize I'd leave at all
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: me too, that's making all the difference
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: My husband really loved me, but coming from a broken home, he lost his mom when he was 12, so he thought controlling me was the solution, very messed up, but he had to learn to see that.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: definitely that makes sense
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: He feared I would die or leave him or something, but once he saw that, and realized what he was doing was hurting me and making me want to leave, he changed. But honestly, I have never understood men and why they dont' see life the way we do. Sometimes it takes that objective person to help them see it.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I'm not convinced mine loves me, looking back it's beginning to seem like he was draining me for my income and labor
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: Ouch! That sounds painful to look at.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: it is, I think I was super wrong about him and overlooked red flags
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: People who truly love others become willing to change. Sometimes it takes a DRASTIC measure to wake them up, like leaving. He has not heard you, so many he will "hear" it when you leave. But please be careful and have a plan.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: How long have you been married?
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: eight years, together for 11
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: That's a long time. I will say a prayer for your safety and for you to get some help, hopefully he will join you. Marriage is a lot of work, but it can't be one person, it has to be two.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: Don't leave anything in writing around until after you leave.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: absolutely!
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: definitely no paper trail, for sure
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I believe in the power of prayer too. The Serenity prayer is a good one to help me let go of my fears and do what I can, leaving the rest to God.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: I know that one, it's helping me a lot too
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: If I worry and get upset, then I waste energy, I have had to learn to get distracted if I find myself on that worry train, call a friend, go for a walk, just not obsess, it goes nowhere.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: And I urge you to get a counselor.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: that's good advice!
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I will
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: Thank you
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: You are welcome. Watch your thinking, when it goes off track, take charge, change your thinking, get up and move about and do something else because it's not healthy for you to worry. As you said, you freak out, and that is not good for you or your children.
source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: definitely, I think I can do that! I feel a lot better!
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.exact_quote: Thank you! I'm feeling a lot more confident!
source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.exact_quote: I'm glad to hear it. Keep the faith, all will be well in due time! Sometimes rough roads really work out, but it never FEELS that way!  You have a good night! :D

seeker: Hello

supporter: Hi there, how are you today?

seeker: I'm a bit bad honestly.

supporter: Can you tell me what's going on to cause you to feel this way?
seeker: I've been struggling with depression for a while. It's hard to deal with. I feel hopeless. 

supporter: I see. I definitely understand how long bouts of depression can make you feel more hopeless. Have you discussed your depression with anyone else before?
seeker: I've spoken to a therapist but it didn't help. I tried a help hotline online but they thought I was suicidal so they called the cops to check on me .. never doing that again lol. 

seeker: I don't know what to do

supporter: Yeah, it sounds like you aren't suicidal. Though I do have to check; have you had any thoughts or tendencies of suicide or self-harm?
seeker: I have in the past. Recently, no. 

seeker: I just feel like I'll never be happy.

supporter: I understand. Can you provide any more information about your meeting with the therapist? You said talking to one didn't help, do you know why?
seeker: I think it didn't help because I'm a bit shy. Or because I didn't know where to start. It's hard to know what to talk about.

seeker: I guess it also didn't help because she seemed like she was just reading a script. She wasn't the greatest at making me feel cared about

seeker: You're doing pretty good though haha

supporter: That makes sense and is completely natural. It's difficult sometimes to open up to a stranger that you don't completely know or might not trust. It definitely sounds frustrating that she seemed like she was reading from a script. 
supporter: And I'm glad to hear you think I'm doing alright lol
seeker: I think therapy could work. Actually something happened with my therapist (maybe fired lol) and she's no longer my therapist.. so I need a new one.

supporter: That's interesting. I know from experience that finding a good therapist is all about trial and error, unfortunately. It's important to find the right fit and I would definitely suggest looking for a new one. Do you know of anyone in your life, maybe a friend or family member, that has been to therapy that you would be comfortable getting a recommendation from?
seeker: I think my closest friend has been to therapy. I could always ask her for a recommendation.

supporter: That sounds like a great idea! Remember to keep your friends close too. I know it can be tough when you feel as low as this, but it's important to have a good support system in addition to any therapy you might be receiving.
seeker: My friends and I look out for eachother. I think they're a good help :)

supporter: That's great to hear! It really sounds like you can go to them for support and often being there for someone else can make us feel better too.
seeker: This was a nice little chat! You should actually volunteer for a helpline haha

supporter: Aww that's so good of you to say!! I do want to confirm that you have a game-plan now, though. Remember to keep your friends close and to start looking for a new therapist if you haven't already. If you find one that's not the right fit it doesn't hurt to start over or maybe even ask for a recommendation from that therapist. If they're any good they should understand how important it is for you to find a good fit. Also remember to be kind to yourself. It can be difficult, but I know you can do it.
seeker: I'm ok! I got my friends and family. I made an appointment with my psychiatrist to get different medication so I could ask him for a therapist recommen
dation as well.

supporter: That's absolutely wonderful to hear! Is there anything else you would like to discuss today?
seeker: I think I'm good. Thank you though! This was nice :)

supporter: Awesome. You've got this! Have a good rest of your day
seeker: You too! :)

supporter: before you take any action, i'd ask myself what are your options?
supporter: you know that his actions have very little to do with you and more to do with him, right?
seeker: Well, I could move out but I can't afford to rent a flat on my own. I'd have to move in with my parents, realistically. 
seeker: I keep telling myself that but I feel really betrayed. I keep wondering what she is like and whether she is prettier and more successful than me. 
supporter: are your parents supportive of that idea?

supporter: it's not about her or you. it's about him.

supporter: they will understand. opening up to them will be the hardest part. it's a shame cocktail, but it's not one you made

supporter: it's in our nature as women to ask "what did I do?" but it is never about us or anything we did. 
seeker: Thank you, I am really glad that you understand. I don't feel that I will ever be able to trust any man again! 
supporter: trust and vunerability is huge in a relationship. i'd look for professional help if you wan tot try and work on it

supporter: do you have a friend who has been through a similar situation? sometime that helps.

supporter: my guess is he felt the same way you are feeling right now

supporter: i'm totally into the podcasts "a slob comes clean" basically it's about getting your poop in a group

supporter: that's so hard. imagine how much energy he had to use to keep his lives from colliding. he couldn't find a better use for that energy?!

supporter: NO!! she's not going to be able to help you unless you need a witness for divorce court
seeker: It would be less of a betrayal, I think, if she did not know about me. I would never do that to another woman! 
supporter: she likely knew, othewise how would he explain all the time he spent with you to her?
seeker: I suppose that's a good point too. I think maybe I do just need to make a total break and not look back.

supporter: glad i could help. please stay safe and no matter what you decide to do, you will be fine.

supporter: hello there, how are you? 

seeker: I am ok.  Kinda having a rough day today.
supporter: I am sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it? 
seeker: Sure.  It's coming up on 3 years next month that I lost my boyfriend in a car accident.  Its just really rough this time of year.

supporter: Oh I am so sorry to hear that. I cannot imagine how hard that must have been for you. 
seeker: Extremely hard.  I remember that morning like it was yesterday.  He got killed within an hour after leaving the house on his way to work.

supporter: He was killed so soon after you last saw him? 
seeker: Very soon.  And the worst thing is I was upset with him that morning.  He had an addiction to xanax.  I was not ok with it.  He had went and got some that morning and he would always give them to me so I could give them to him so he didn't take them all.  I was so upset that he went and got them.  He was packing up his truck with things to take to the new shop that day.  He was a tattoo artist and just started a new job.  I didn't even get out of bed to help him and he knew I was upset with him.

supporter: Have you considered any sort of bereavement counselling? Addiction in a partner is a very hard thing to have to deal with. It is not your fault! 
seeker: I had decided that I was gonna wait to hear from him that day instead of texting or calling him.  I wanted him to realize how upset his addiction made me. Instead the phone call I got was that he had been killed.
supporter: Do you feel any sort of guilt about it? You should not, of course, but do you wonder if things would have been different if you had talked to him first? 

seeker: I haven't done any counseling.  I know I should and it would probably help me.  I don't know why I have not.  
supporter: I have previously had counselling and found it very useful but there is a long waiting list for a free counsellor 

seeker: I don't feel guilt about it.  Now at least.  I was pretty hard on myself at first.  But I know that he knows why I was upset that morning.  It was something we dealt with a lot.  
supporter: Are you still in touch with his family and friends? 

seeker: I went and talked to a therapist once right after and never went back.  And I don't know why.  He was amazing to talk too.  But I just never went back.
supporter: I think you should do things in your own time but I would recommend doing it again one day. 
seeker: I don't have any contact with his family.  I actually had to block them on all social media.  They are extremely religous.  Which there is nothing wrong with that.  But he didn't have the best relationship with any of them.  They couldn't accept him for who he was.  His biological father didn't have anything to do with him.  His mom was remarried and had two more kids and they didn't treat my boyfriend very good growing up.  He ended up living with his grandparents.  He finally had acceptance in my family.  He actually talked to my mom more than I did lol.
supporter: Sounds like a very complicated set up. It is sad when family members become partially estranged from one another. 
seeker: His family has been pretty horrible to me and my girls.  And I know it's because they have guilt for the way things were with their relationship.  They didn't even invite me and my girls to the burial of his ashes.  
supporter: That is extremely offensive and I think you would have had the right to contest that. 
seeker: It's very sad.  Not what I wanted at all.  But they were really horrible to me and my girls.  I know he would not be happy that they have treated us so poorly.
supporter: I hope that you are able to come to terms with things in the near future. Please try and focus on your girls and not worry so much! 

seeker: His sisters went and cleaned out and took everything he had from the shop the day after the funeral.  Which really hurt.  The stuff he had there meant alot to me. 

supporter: I think you should talk to someone about this. Maybe a lawyer? There must be something people can do to help.

supporter: Hello, how can I help you today?
seeker: I'm having a hard time each day, but today especially. I keep having anxiety attacks that come on suddenly and intensely. 

supporter: I understand you keep experiencing anxiety attacks.
supporter: Is there any common cause for the attacks?
seeker: None that I have figured out yet, they just seem to come on out of nowhere

supporter: Is there any specific stimuli that takes place just before or within an hour prior to the attacks?
seeker: Any stimulation triggers me really, a lot of noise, lights, but mostly my thoughts are very loud

supporter: You are not alone, a lot of people experience anxiety attacks due to physical stimuli.
supporter: Have you looked into mindfulness exercises or meditation?
seeker: I feel so alone though, it doesn't bring me any comfort to know that other people have them

seeker: yes, and they do help, but there are days that it doesn't matter what I do, and today is one of them

supporter: I have experienced Anxiety myself and meditation helped me for the most part, I also found that I wasn't sleeping enough and being tired made my attacks longer.
supporter: Are you sleeping okay at night?
seeker: I'm getting plenty of sleep, and I do practice meditation, maybe not as often as I should, I meditate five minutes per day


supporter: I would suggest trying Mindfulness exercises for at least 15 minutes every day and see if that helps.
seeker: I'll see if that helps, I'm really low on energy right now because it just takes so much out of me

supporter: I understand, Sometimes the Mindfulness exercises help me get more productive sleep.
seeker: I try to do mindfulness before bed, but I'm always too tired. I think it would be better if I did them in the afternoon at some point, did you use guided meditation?

supporter: I did, ASMR guidance seems to help me most, but I happen to be ASMR sensative, perhaps you are as well? They seem to help with my anxiety as well.
seeker: Are those the videos on youtube where the sound is enhanced? Those are soothing

supporter: Yes, Kind of like whispers, almost like Bob Ross on those old painting videos.
seeker: Just talking about my anxiety has helped a lot actually, and I do enjoy bob ross, hadn't thought of that as therapeutic but it makes sense

supporter: I am glad I could be helpful.
seeker: Yes, thank you for your help

seeker: Take care now!

supporter: Be Well!

seeker: Hi
supporter: Hello there, how is your day going? 
seeker: It's going okay. I'm just having a hard time.
supporter: Is there something that you'd like to talk about? 
seeker: It's mainly my husband. His spending habits are out of control. He thinks he need to reward himself for living. We can't survive if he keeps gifting himself.
supporter: Wow that sounds like a big problem. Is he aware of how much distress this is causing you? 
seeker: I've tried talking to him about it, but he claims that he needs to reward himself or he wouldn't do anything. Like, if he gets up and goes to work then he needs to eat out to reward himself.
supporter: So you feel that he is misunderstanding life? That he feels that he deserves things just for existing? 
seeker: Exactly. And if I push further, he compares himself to other people: "Well, at least I don't hit you." or "At least I'm not an alcoholic" Like I should thank him for existing.
supporter: It sounds like a really toxic relationship - I hear you! I have been in that position also. In the end I felt that I had no choice but to leave. I cannot tell you what to do, though. 
seeker: It's hard because we have children. When we were just dating, he was a different person. He didn't start to act this way until after our eldest was born.
supporter: Ah, unfortunately a lot of men are like that - before you become seriously committed they seem totally different. Have you considered seeking professional help? 
seeker: The problem all boils down to money. If I had enough for therapy I wouldn't be worried about his spending habits! lol. But, you're right, that's probably what we both need!
supporter: I believe that there are some organisations that will offer free therapy sessions for people in need. Have you considered asking your doctor? 
seeker: Really? I'd definitely be interested in that. Do they have online therapy like that?
supporter: I am not totally sure what is available but I think that there might be such things 
seeker: Thanks for your help. You said you've been in similar relationships. Is this behavior common for men? 
supporter: Well no, I don't think that all men are like this by any stretch of the imagination. Unfortunately, however, there are some bad apples who give all men a bad name. I am sure that the same applies to women too though! 
seeker: Haha, true. I just wondered. I had previous relationships, but they were very short.  My dad was always the opposite: he was a penny-pincher. Sometimes I worry that maybe I'm just to stingy with the money, but then I remember that we have none, so Idk how to be more generous lol
supporter: You sound to me as though you are being realistic and sensible about your financial situation and are being neither too stingy nor too lavish. 
seeker: Thank you for your help and feedback. I appreciate it. I'm going to select Finish & Quit

supporter: I hope that I have been able to be of some help to you! 
supporter: Have a lovely rest of day

supporter: Exactly! there is nothing at all wrong with not being a straight A student.

seeker: A bit, but she uses the "I pay for your education" card.
seeker: Which makes sense, but still, I know I am doing well so it's just a lot at times.
supporter: Absolutely not. There is nothing wrong with not being perfect. And she has no right to emotionally manipulate you by mentioning money. 
seeker: I agree, but she does have money over my head, which sucks.
seeker: Don't get me wrong, I am very grateful for her financial support, but she uses it to manipulate me at times.
supporter: Are there any scholarships or hardship funds that you could potentially look into applying for? 
seeker: Yes, I have received multiple scholarships, but nothing that will make a dent in the tuition. 
seeker: College is too expensive.

seeker: That's what I keep telling myself, but I have this overarching fear that I will be in debt forever then.
supporter: Debt is a very scary thing to experience, I know. I do worry a lot about it sometimes too so you are not alone. 
seeker: That makes me feel better.
supporter: The main thing is, do you enjoy your studies and consider them worthwhile? 
seeker: yes, somewhat, but who loves school?

seeker:

supporter: Are you able to confide in your friends about your situation and your worries? 
seeker: Yes at times, which makes things a little better in the moment.
supporter: Do you feel that your friends are able to empathise with your situation? Are any of them going through the same thing? 
seeker: they all have more independence and pay for their own things, so they can't really relate to me. That is where I feel behind in life than everyone else.
supporter: Would it be possible for you to get a part time job of some description? Maybe bar tending or working in a restaurant? 
seeker: That gives me social anxiety, which is something I also struggle with greatly. 
supporter: Ah I suffer from terrible social anxiety myself so I hear you 
supporter: I hope I have been able to provide you with some useful advice!

supporter: Hi Jane, it's great to hear from you again. How have you been holding up?
seeker: Hi, it's been a bit rough lately. My car broke down and the repair costs are just... more than I can handle right now.
supporter: Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that, Jane. That must be incredibly stressful, especially with everything else you've had to deal with recently.
seeker: It really is. I've been trying to manage, but the financial stress keeps piling up. I still haven't resolved the money issue with my friend, and now this... It's overwhelming.
supporter: I can only imagine how difficult that must be. You've been doing your best under such challenging circumstances. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
seeker: Thank you. Sometimes it feels like I'm just not able to catch a break. I've been trying to keep track of everything with my journal, but it feels like every day brings something new.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool, and it's a good step that you're using it to process your thoughts and feelings. It shows how you're trying to find ways to cope.
seeker: Yeah, I thought it might help calm my anxieties. But with my job performance not being where it's supposed to be, and money problems, I just feel stuck.
supporter: Feeling stuck is definitely tough. It's important to remember that it's not a reflection of your abilities or worth. You're dealing with a lot, and your efforts are meaningful.
seeker: Thanks. Sometimes I just worry that I'm not living up to expectations, especially at work. The fear of being seen as incompetent is always there.
supporter: I understand. Work pressure can be intense, and when combined with personal challenges, it's a lot to balance. Have you been able to talk to anyone at work about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not yet. I'm hesitant because I don't want it to seem like I'm making excuses. I really want to prove myself and get back on track.
supporter: That makes sense. It might help to reach out for support when you're ready, even just to get some feedback. Sometimes, opening up can bring understanding and solutions you couldn't see before.
seeker: You're right. I'll think about that. Maybe just having a conversation could help put things into perspective.
supporter: Absolutely, even small steps can lead to positive changes. Remember, you're doing the best you can, and it's okay to seek help when you need it.
seeker: I will try to remember that. It's helpful to talk about it and just get it off my chest a bit.
supporter: I'm glad you reached out, Jane. It's important to have a space where you feel heard. If you ever need to talk or get things off your mind, I'm here.
seeker: Thank you so much. It really means a lot to have someone who listens and understands.
supporter: You're welcome. Remember, one step at a time, and be gentle with yourself. You're not alone in this, and there are brighter days ahead.
seeker: I'll keep that in mind. Thanks again for your support.

supporter: Hello!
seeker: Hello.

supporter: How has your day been?
seeker: Okay I guess.

supporter: Has there been anything that has been bothering you?
seeker: I have been very depressed lately.

supporter: What do you think has been causing your depression?
seeker: I was raped when I was a teenager by my boyfriend and as you can see its still haunting me to this day.
supporter: That definitely is a very impactful event, but you've already been so strong for reaching out.
seeker: Thank you. I feel as if I lost who I am after that happened.
supporter: I think it would be okay to allow yourself grieve because in a sense the person you were has now changed due to this event.
seeker: It is very hard to be in another sexual relationship after that has happened. Im not sure I will every be the same again.

supporter: I understand, I had a similar event where I was taken advantage of with similar feelings.  I personally decided to share all my feelings with my new partner and we went very slow only doing things I was comfortable with.
supporter: That may be a strategy you could use to help move back into having a sexual relationship with someone.
seeker: That seems like a good idea. But, what if my partner doesn't have empathy for those sort of things. Im worried he will not care.
supporter: In good relationships both partners have mutual respect for each which extends into their sexual relationship.  Remember you haven't lost your self worth, and you deserve someone who respects you.
seeker: I suppose. I just dont want to burden my new relationship with my past issues.
supporter: Your past is definitely not a burden, it's part of you, even if it's not a positive experience.  By sharing your past, it would bring you closer as a couple.
seeker: I guess you are right.

supporter: Another thing that could help you navigate new relationships is counseling.  I've had counseling sessions that have greatly helped me in the past.
seeker: I will look into that tomorrow. Thank you for your advice and time. I truly appreciate it. 

supporter: Of course!  I think we must support each other in our times of need.

seeker: Hello

supporter: Good afternoon!  What can I help you with today?
seeker: I've been feeling a lot of pressure and stress lately due to school

supporter: Oof, yes, school can be a tough situation.   Are you close to the end of the semester?  
supporter: That can be both a relief and stressful, because a break is near, but all the exams and projects are due.
seeker: Yes, I am a little more than halfway done with the semester
seeker: The thing is that I am in a doctoral program, so even though the semester is close to the end, I always need to continue working 

supporter: Ahh, I see.  That is a great deal of time and work.  What are you studying?  
seeker: It is... I am in psychology

seeker: I have to work on my thesis on the side even with all of my classes and I have a hard time managing my time and keeping track 

supporter: Time management can be very difficult with a normal class load, that sounds exhausting.  
seeker: It is!
supporter: Do calendars help you at all?  I am a super visual person, so calendars and planners are invaluable to me, as well as different colors of ink and labels so I can visually divide my attention
supporter: Getting a million different colors of pens and highlighters changed my organization for the better.  
seeker: I do keep a physical and electronic agenda, but I feel like even if I write down my tasks, I find a way to procrastinate which is what I am having trouble with

supporter: Also, setting clear boundaries for your study/work and relax times may help.  I like to set a timer for, say, 45 minutes, and work/write/read/study for that long, then, I get a 10 minute break.  I'll go outside, refresh my coffee, grab a snack, dance to some music, stretch, then set another timer for 45 minutes, then another break for 10 minutes.  That allows my brain to take a second and refresh from the work.
seeker: That is actually very helpful, I'll take note of it

seeker: I think it would help to fix break times so I can actually focus on working 

supporter: Or, like, today, I woke up and spent half an hour allowing myself to drink my coffee and scroll through Reddit.  Then it was time to work on my group project for 45 minutes, then a break, then I worked again, took a break, went to a class, etc.  Scheduling your breaks can be helpful too so your lizard brain doesn't freak out and go "WE ARE GOING TO BE WORKING FOREVERRRR"
seeker: I agree!!! That really is helpful, thank you

supporter: which, for me at least, is where the fatigue sets in.  You're very welcome!  I hope I was helpful.  You seem positive and willing to try new things, and I think you will be successful even if you are tired. 
seeker: The pandemic hasn't really helped either

seeker: I'm always locked in my apartment and staying sitting down in front of my computer all day

supporter: Definitely not.  Everyone's Maslow hierarchy getting knocked out from under them is extremely disconcerting.  
seeker: Hahaha, Maslow, i like it.

supporter: Like how is a person supposed to study, self-actualize, when we literally don't know what will happen next?  
seeker: I agree! I've also been turning to drugs a lot lately due to the situation. Procrastinating makes me feel guilty, and I end my day too early to smoke and focus my mind on something other than studying....

supporter: Are there aspects of your study that you dislike, or are you just ready to be done with school?  Little of column A + column b?
seeker: Hm, I think it has less to do with liking or disliking, and more with starting a very hard and lengthy degree online without any social contact

supporter: Ah, yes, that makes sense.  And working from home is infamously hard, again, for lack of boundaries, so in addition to just not seeing people and getting the casual affirmation and confirmation messages on a daily basis of like "hey Jim you did a great job on that spreadsheet" or "Haha Jessica you're so funny", we also are writing papers in our pajamas and bedclothes, which makes it seem interminable.
seeker: Ugh exactly

supporter: Listening to lectures while the doorbell is ringing and it's just so strange and we aren't set up to do it.  That's why I'm a big fan of specific spaces in my house since March.  I tried to sit in bed with my laptop and do things but 1. I'm old and it hurts my wrists and 2. my headspace is so completely different from being my computer chair and at my desk.  I try to be really strict about where I do my work., maybe trying to structure that a bit could help you feel a little more in control of the work load and your day's schedule.  
seeker: I agree, that makes a lot of sense! Thank you 

seeker: You have been a big help today and I really feel listened and understood. I really appreciate it

supporter: I am very glad to hear that!  You sound motivated to succeed and I think that you deserve to take care of yourself and stay healthy to complete your studies.  It will be hard but it will also be worth it, and you should be proud.  Good luck with everything!  
seeker: Wow, thank you! 

seeker: Have a great day 

supporter: Thank you!  You too!

supporter: Why would they judge you on that? Do they know your nephew as well?
seeker: Yes, she is very close friends with my nephew's mother as well. She is the kind of person who will go into deep debt and overdraw her bank account to buy someone a gift, I am not. I could not afford the gift, I am disabled and on a very minimal income.

supporter: Then would you say its a little odd for her to be acting in this manner towards you?

source_refs.speaker: supporter

source_refs.speaker: seeker

source_refs.speaker: supporter

seeker: That's all I can do. Idk. They started visitation with their daddy this weekend and i feel anxious to let them go because their father is not the most attentive person.
supporter: Neither was my ex husband. I know what your going through just take some time for yourself while they are with their dad.

seeker: Haha cute! No worries i will.

supporter: How are you today?

seeker: Feeling down.

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, what's got you down?

seeker: I live in a more rural area that has moved into our highest risk tier for Covid. 
They just seem to be making all the wrong choices amongst our local schools and other agencies.
supporter: I can relate to being in a rural area being hit right now. What are the wrong choices that they're making?

seeker: The middle school is still in person 100% of the time. There have been >30 cases, most in the last 3 weeks, and they keep sending letters home stating that they don't believe the kids are getting sick in school. It's infuriating.
seeker: So, I get mad, then I get anxious, then I get down...

supporter: It's such a hard time right now, knowing what is the right thing to do. Does your district offer any virtual options?
seeker: They do. It's a pretty poor one though. I'm looking at charter options right now. They only offer ELA, Math, Science, and SS through the public virtual option. 
seeker: The kid I'm concerned about is taking math 3 grades ahead and high school spanish. I do not think their program is in her best interest, so I'm focusing on the charter option, but it takes time :(

supporter: That's frustrating, obviously you want what's best for your kid and it's going to take time. 

seeker: It does. Like you said, crazy time for everyone.
supporter: I think the important thing to remember is that we're all going through similar things. Which probably increases our anxiety because we don't have any good way to express our frustrations since everyone else is in the same or worse position.
seeker: True, true. It does help to focus on how you can help, especially if you find people in worse positions.
supporter: While we're busy worrying about things like education and jobs, I like to look for the little messages of hope and empathy that we'[re seeing through all of this as well. It's a good teaching moment for our kids and showing how to collectively work to take care of one another.
seeker: I like that. I especially like the idea of involving the kids.
supporter: Just think of all of the ways our kids are learning to adapt to different life situations as well. That's worth just as much as their formal education. Your concerns are valid, and hopefully finding another safer school works out and this whole thing is over soon.
seeker: I have been trying to do projects at home I normally wouldn't to try to help everyone fill time. Things like creating websites, art projects, and such. Those skills will help tremendously.
supporter: That's a great idea, helping fill time with things to distract is a good way to relieve stress as well.
seeker: So, I guess I'll just keep doing what I can and try to stay away from media and the state's tracking site. I had been doing this, but the announcement for the new tier came from the school!
supporter: What region are you in? We're midwest and watching the news is not the best way to lighten the day.
seeker: Midwest. Not the worst place to be, although we supposedly hit some statistic that no other state has yet, so we may be heading that direction.
supporter: Well my suggestion is to turn off the news.
seeker: Consider it done, lol! I'm gonna log out now, but you did give me a couple points to consider that would be better than dwelling on the hopelessness.
seeker: Stay safe where you are.
supporter: You too, thanks for chatting!

seeker: Hi.  I am worried about my exams.
supporter: Exams are a stressful time. What seems to be the problem?

supporter: Exams are a stressful time. What seems to be the problem?

seeker: I do not feel like I am properly prepared, even though I have studied.  
supporter: I can assure you that countless students including myself have gone through the trials of studying for exams and do feel overwhelmed but it passes.

supporter: Have you studied?

seeker: I have studied.  However, I still feel like I am not prepared.  One big problem is that I have no quiet place to study.  
supporter: I get it, distractions can be challenging to overcome at times. Have you thought about going to a library, or a book store?
seeker: I have not.  Both of those are great suggestions.  I wonder if I should take the time to walk to the library (30 minutes), or just continue to study?  Maybe, I know as much as I can know.  The anxiety is too much.
supporter: If it helps you study then the library may be worth the time and effort. Sometimes we can stress out over worrying about not having enough time to study. But trust the work you have done and you will know if it is enough.
seeker: This is very good advice.  Have you completed college?
supporter: Yes, and it wasn't easy but with hard work, it is completely doable. And you have the power within yourself.
seeker: What do you think will happen if I fail this test?

supporter: Sometimes it is not about the amount of studying, but the way you study. I like reading my textbooks and highlighting the important parts and then rewriting them so they become ingrained in me. But let us not jump the gun, you haven't failed anything.

seeker: Very true.  Thanks for reminding me.  I think I worry more about the outcome than I need too.

supporter: Don't forget to breathe. Exams are stressful but I would suggest don't cram everything to the last minute. Usually the hour before the exam, I do something else.
seeker: Very good advice.  Any suggestions on what I can do?

supporter: Stay calm, believe in yourself, start your studying early so you are not cramming everything in the last few days.
seeker: Great Advice.  

seeker: But, in the one hour prior to the exam, do you have any advice on something I can do to calm my nerves?

supporter: Walk outside, away from the students waiting for their tests.
seeker: Wonderful suggestion

seeker: Thank you for your help.  I think I will go walk now.  Best regards. 
supporter: Is there anything else I can help you with?


seeker: No.  Thank you.
supporter: Goodnight and good luck.

seeker: I need some advice I have been feeling anxious lately.
supporter: Im sorry to hear you have been feeling anxious. Lets work to find things that maybe help you feel better when your feeling this way. 

seeker: Do you have any ideas?
supporter: Based on studies generally walking away for a moment from a stressor can help to relieve that stressor momentarily enough to maybe make you feel alittle better. 
seeker: I have been going for walks alone and that is nice to have a break. Any other ideas?
supporter: Thats a good idea and sometimes when ive been stressed walking or any physical activity can help to promote more of a positive feeling based on the release of endorphines.
supporter: How long have you been experiencing anxiety?
seeker: I have been working out more. How do you relax? I have had anxiety for a month now.
seeker: I think I need a vacation.
supporter: Do you think maybe it has to do with covid going on right now? Or did anythign specifically happen that has brought on more anxiety? more work? family? money? .....
seeker: Covid is bad enough but my husband has been battling an illness for weeks.
supporter: Generally to relax i as well enjoy some forms of exercise, sometimes a cup of warm tea or even just listening to music can help distract your mind for a moment. 
seeker: Those are good ideas. Do you think a good diet helps too?
supporter: Im so sorry to hear that. I completely understand why you may be feeling the way you do. 
seeker: Any other advice?
supporter: I do think a good diet can help with many aspects of things, after all food is the energy and nutrients for your body. So if you eat bad quality food you dont reap all the benefits and nutrition that comes from a good nutrient rich diet. 
seeker: Do you think calling friends helps?
supporter: The best advice i can give is to remember to be positive , focus on also your own sanity and take one day at a time. 
seeker: That is sound advice. 
supporter: i think having a good support system is a wonderful idea. That can include friends, family or any other professional you may use to communicate with.
seeker: I think as he feels better I will too.
supporter: I think that may be so. Its tough to not worry when it comes to anyone you care about or love especially if they arent doing well. 
supporter: Is there anything else i can help you with or do you have any other questions?
seeker: Exactly and I think he finally has some medicine that is starting to help.
seeker: Thanks for your help.
supporter: Im glad to hear that. And your welcome. I hope i could help and hope the best for you and your family. 
seeker: To you too.

supporter: Hello. How are you? What would you like to talk about?
seeker: Got any advice for a lonely single fellow in his mid thirties? I miss my friends, and virtual meetings on Zoom don't feel the same as meeting in person!
supporter: The pandemic has been hard on many people, those in relationships and those looking for new ones! Have you tried to develop a new hobby or interest that you can do with others once the pandemic is over?
seeker: Well, I've been writing enough poetry to publish a book, so I'll certainly do that. I know the pandemic has been rough for everyone. Hopefully my doctor will say I qualify for the vaccine soon. 
seeker: Getting my stimulus check in the next week or so would certainly make me a bit happier, too. 
supporter: That's great! Poetry is something you can share in person or over video link. What about physical activities? I think that yoga might be something that you can do by yourself and with others. There are a bunch of videos on sites like YouTube. 
supporter: A stimulus check! Yes, we can all use money during these trying times.
seeker: Oh, I took advantage of virtual yoga and zumba early on during the pandemic. Friends had virtual classes. Eventually they were able to go back to work. Being disabled is a poverty trap for a lot of people, not just me. I really want to find a girlfriend once I get vaccinated. 
supporter: I have tried yoga myself, but it wasn't really my thing. I prefer walking and riding a bike. 
supporter: Do you have to wait until you get vaccinated to start working on getting a girlfriend?
seeker: Well, certain things don't work for every person. 
supporter: True. I like trying new things, but I am happy to give them up if they just don't fit my style. 
supporter: Is there a way you could start looking for a girlfriend online now, before the pandemic is over?
supporter: Maybe there is a way to make a connection using your poetry.
seeker: Technically, no, I don't HAVE to wait to get vaccinated, but then again, maybe I don't want a girlfriend. The only one I had ten years ago in college wanted to marry me and have a child and I wasn't ready for commitment. I fear marriage, actually. 
supporter: Marriage is a big step, and any prudent person would think carefully before making the commitment. 
seeker: That's a good point, I'm sure if my poetry is entertaining or full of truth about my experiences in a wheelchair, perhaps a woman will find that attractive 
supporter: Are you concerned that things will move too quickly to that level of commitment (marriage)? You could make it clear from the outset that you want to take it slow. 
seeker: Or I could just get an adult entertainer to be my companion for a day. I've done that before with women in that industry. It costs a bit, but it's worth it for companionship 

seeker: No, I just hate the idea of waking up to one woman for 20 or 30 years

seeker: But it's better than being alone

supporter: Robin Williams talked about that situation.
supporter: He said that he didn't fear being alone as much as being with people that he didn't like.
seeker: Did he really? Well, it's sad how he ended up, I'm too scared to commit suicide like he did! I enjoy living life, even when I have months at a time without human connection


supporter: Adult entertainers provide one kind of companionship, but it is not complete. It feels like a stopgap to me. Is it fulfilling enough for you?
seeker: You're right, I just lack self confidence in my poetry....hopefully I'll figure out a way to spit it out on a blog or something

supporter: You could trade poems with other budding poets. "I'll show you mine if you show me yours."
supporter: Do you find yourself to be more an introvert or an extrovert?
seeker: Oh it's been very fulfilling for me when I've had the opportunity to use it. Most of them are genuine women. Only a handful have tried to take advantage of me. 
seeker: I'm definitely an extrovert
seeker: That was a clever pun by the way 
seeker: It's ironic and strange how many people struggle with that stupid voice in their head that tells them they're not good enough to accomplish anything. 
supporter: Thanks. Ok. The pandemic is particularly hard on extroverts. People look down on sex workers, but I think that the world is a big complex place and people are trying to make their way in it. If everyone is consenting, I see no problem. 
supporter: Have you tried psilocybin? Some people swear that it changes the inner monologue for the better. I am not a physician, but for long-term adjustment, it might be beneficial. 
seeker: Well of course it's consentual. I would never NOT ask for permission to do things with a sex worker, or any person. 
seeker: I'll have to Google that, I've never heard of that, but thanks for the advice!

supporter: Sure! I'm glad we had a chance to chat. Best of luck with making friends/girlfriends after the pandemic!
supporter: BTW, is there a quit button on your end?
seeker: Yes there is, and I am pressing it right now. Thanks so much, I'll be fine. Have a good night!

supporter: Good night!

supporter: I can understand how that can become a source of frustration after a while.
supporter: Would you like to share what pushed it beyond the normal point today?
seeker: It's just been an ongoing thing that has escalated recently because she's so afraid and timid and doesn't believe anyone could really love or care for her. I get sick of having to say that of course I love her. 
supporter: I can relate because I also have a close friend that seeks constant reaffirmations. 
supporter: Have you spoken with her about this?

seeker: I have. I address it every time it comes up. She always sells herself short. Recently I suggested she could babysit my kids, she agreed, then almost immediately said it was ok if I had someone better in mind, and didn't want her, even though I had asked her!
seeker: do you talk to your friend about it?
supporter: Sometimes it is very difficult to see yourself through someone elses eyes when you undervalue yourself.
supporter: I know it may be difficult to remain patient when your friend repeatedly does this, but maybe you could explain to her that it makes you feel like she is mistrustful of your opinion when she second guesses your taste in friends.

supporter: I did in fact speak with my friend and it helped our relationship quite a bit. We continue to be very close 20 years later.
seeker: It's frustrating to me and gives me anxiety because I wish I could change her to see herself the way I, and others, do. But I know I can't make her see her self worth. That's something she has to find for herself. 
seeker: That's good to hear about you and your friend.

supporter: Sometimes you have to take a step back and fill your own cup.

supporter: It has been my pleasure! I trust you will make the right choice! Best of wishes!

seeker: I just can't make myself get started. There are so many dishes.

supporter: Sometimes even every day tasks can seem overwhelming. Do you have an idea of what makes you put off the dishes?

seeker: I feel like I just don't know where to start.

supporter: How long have you been hesitant to start?

seeker: I guess it has been a few days now.

supporter: I get it. Sometimes I find dishes so overwhelming that I will let them pile up. Maybe together we can figure out a way to break it into smaller tasks.
seeker: Ok, I suppose I can try that. But I don't quite know where to start.

supporter: It is so hard to figure out where to start sometimes. Ok, I'll help with a plan. Maybe you can glance at the dishes and pull out the largest one that is dirty. Let's start there.

seeker: Ok. That makes sense. There is a large pot. I think if I was that, maybe it would get me started.
supporter: yes, starting with the large pot would be a great place to start! Good thinking!
seeker: Ok, but then what?

supporter: Well, washing the pot will make the overall task look smaller. Then, let's pick a second type of dish to focus on. After you wash the large pot, try to focus on larger bowls, then plates and cups. You could leave the silverware for last.
seeker: Oh, thank you so much! It helps my anxiety to talk through a plan. Sometimes I get so anxious, it is hard to figure out how to break a large task down to something manageable on my own.
supporter: I am always happy to help. I find it difficult sometimes too.

supporter: I really think you are figure out how to get through this and help your anxiety.
seeker: Wow do you think so?
seeker: Have you every had anxiety like this?
supporter: Yes, I have. I often look at work assignments as larger than they are and can only get started when I break them down.
supporter: I really think you have done great job figuring out how to tackle the task that is causing you anxiety.
seeker: I think so too. I hope I can apply this to other things.
seeker: So, it's easy to figure out with things like dishes because there is a size. How do you do it when it is a task that isn't physical like this. Like work?
supporter: So, I see that you get how to do this with this task, but it is still hard to figure out how to conquer tasks that aren't physical like dishes.

supporter: Hello, how are you feeling?
seeker: Tired, very tired!! 

supporter: Oh?  How come so tired?
seeker: Because I can't sleep... I don't know what's wrong with me I just lay there awake for hours!

supporter: Oh I have had trouble sleeping before!   Would you like to know what helped me?
seeker: Yes please, I'm desperate, I'll try anything!

supporter: First of all, fixed sleep and wake times.   If you toss and turn for hours, still get up at the same time.   Eventually your body will tire and sleeping will naturally become easier.
seeker: I have to always get up for work so I am sticking to the same routines, I just lie in bed with so many thoughts racing around my head and I just can't get off to sleep

supporter: Second thing I do is I have a wind down routine.   No work past a certain time, no matter what.   Only soft music, pleasant movie, some light reading, and dim the lights.   It slows your body down before sleep.  It will help slow that racing thoughts you are having.
seeker: I did try reading a book last night, but I don't really have lights that I can dim, it's just the one bright light in our room.

supporter: I have had racing thoughts and it used to drive me up the wall!
supporter: Can you buy a lamp?  Even a second hand one if your budget is tight?
seeker: Yeah, it's just so annoying and then I'm so tired and irritable the next day, I find myself snapping at everyone.

supporter: The bright light will keep your mind stimulated.
seeker: I could buy a lamp I suppose, to see if it helps? But when I am awake all night it's in the dark so I'm not sure if the light is the problem>

supporter: Aw so you are so exhausted from racing thoughts and not enough sleep the night before that you end up taking it out on others, but not meaning to.  Am I understanding correctly?
supporter: Do you get any exercise?  I sleep better on days I go for walks, and my sedentary days I sleep worse, it's quite clear to me.
seeker: I have been trying to do lots of walks, I need to lose weight as well so they kind of go hand in hand!


seeker: I do also have back pain so that's another thing that doesn't help!

supporter: Good effort, keep it up!
supporter: Back pain, I know all about that too unfortunately.  How is your mattress?
seeker: Yeah it's a pretty good mattress, but it is a few years old now, I'm not sure how often you're supposed to replace them?
supporter: Hmm I can't recall, I can't afford to replace mine regularly enough lol.  Maybe google it?
seeker: Yeah maybe, at this point it's worth looking into anything that could help!

supporter: Do you have someone to talk to about the thoughts that are racing? 
supporter: If they are worries, maybe a counsellor would help.
seeker: Not really, I don't really have any friends and my boyfriends a bit weird about stuff like this, I can't really talk to him about things like this.

seeker: Yeah maybe, I have been considering a counsellor myself.

supporter: Hmm that's a challenge not having friends.   Have been there too!   
seeker: And I don't know how to go about finding new ones! I don't think I'm someone people like to be friends with, I try to make friends but they always move on.

supporter: I don't want to give you a huge barrage of suggestions but another thing that helps me is a podcast called Tracks to Relax.
seeker: Sounds interesting, I'll have to look it up!

supporter: Well maybe you just haven't met the right people yet.  It takes time finding someone we click with
seeker: That's true, maybe they weren't meant to be my friends. Anyway, thank you so much for your help but I have to shoot off.

supporter: It's probably not you!   When people drift away from me I always say to myself "Oh well, their loss!"

supporter: you're welcome bye and i hope things improve soon.  You WILL get through this!
seeker: Thank you for your support :-) 
supporter: My pleasure, I've enjoyed talking with you.

supporter: There is a hard line between helping a friend who is addicted and actually enabling them. Have you ever heard of this?
seeker: Sadly my friend has been arrested a few times, spent time in prison, and is fully locked in his lifestyle. He's such a great person, very funny, nice, but he is lost

seeker: He has alienated all of his friends, including me. I was the last one holding on
supporter: My husband and I actually have worked with recovering drug addicts and alcoholics. We are retired now, but still volunteer. seeker: I agree, I'm afraid that's what I have to do. Another one of our mutual friends passed away recently to an overdose. I don't want to lose another friend.
supporter: Have you seen the serenity prayer? Knowing what to do, what not to do and accepting life really is a great thing to ask God for. We can't change others. Yet you have to find a way to have peace. 
seeker: Yes. I know I have to let go. I've punished myself trying to stay in his life. 
supporter: It's very hard to lose friends to addictions. It's epidemic in our society now. However, you can pray for them and look for ways to keep your life on track so you don't get lost focusing on them and not where you want to go. 
seeker: all drugs are bad, but meth is a truly evil drug.
seeker: It's just rotting his soul and body.  He believes he can't stop and you're right, letting go and just sending prayers is all i can really do now

That way you open up yourself to make new friends. 
supporter: I have had to walk away from many unhealthy relationships over the years, it isn't easy, but it's part of maturing in life.

supporter: I've learned the hard way, if a person doesn't want to change, I'm just beating my head against a wall. I can pray, then leave the rest to God. It seems like a lesson I learn over and over again! Hahah.
