supporter: Hi Charlotte, how are you holding up today?
seeker: Hey, I could be better. I just received a performance review at work, and it wasn't great.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Getting negative feedback can be really tough. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling pretty down, actually. It's made me question my abilities and what I'm really contributing at work.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. You've been handling a lot, and criticism can feel overwhelming. Do you remember anything in particular from the review that hit especially hard?
seeker: There was a comment about my consistency. It feels like everything's been piling up, and I'm struggling to keep up with expectations.
supporter: It's hard when everything seems like it's accumulating. You've had a lot on your plate, especially since the conflict with a coworker and the added pressures. Do you think the feedback was fair, or does it feel more like an overwhelming time for you?
seeker: Honestly, part of it might be fair, but I also can't help feeling like I'm being judged more harshly because of past incidents, like that project last year with the errors.
supporter: I remember you talking about how challenging that was. It sounds like some of the stress from then might still be lingering. Have you talked to anyone about how you're feeling, perhaps your therapist?
seeker: Yeah, I've been trying to keep up with therapy. It's helpful, but days like today make it hard to remember the positives.
supporter: I'm glad you're staying connected with therapy. Remember, you're making progress, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. What small things can you do today to take care of yourself?
seeker: Maybe I'll go for a walk or do something creative. I haven't drawn in a while, and that used to help me relax.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking time for yourself is important, especially when you're dealing with so much stress. How about some light exercises like yoga? I remember you mentioning it helped in the past.
seeker: Yeah, yoga could be good. I should get back to it. Thanks for reminding me.
supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You've worked hard and deserve to be gentle with yourself right now. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to talk about?
seeker: Just trying not to let this affect my job too much. I still enjoy some parts of it, like those moments when I really connect with a project.
supporter: That's a great mindset. Focusing on the parts you enjoy can be very grounding. You've had recognition for projects before, like the one you were acknowledged on recently. It shows your capability.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me of that. It helps to remember those moments, especially now.
supporter: I'm glad to be here for you. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need someone to talk to.
seeker: I will. I appreciate your support. Thanks for listening and helping me process all this.

head: RS
reading_text:
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hello, I am here to listen. How are things going?
seeker: Bad. Almost had a good day and then got treated bad in the end so I don't know why I try.

supporter: I understand how you feel. It seems as if you are being treated badly for no genuine reason. Is this correct?
seeker: That is correct.

supporter: Who is treating you badly? Do you believe there are any causes behind the actions of those hurting you?
seeker: My husband mainly. He just doesn't want me to enjoy life I guess.

supporter: That must be really difficult to go through, I know when my partner treats me badly, I am hurt and upset with them. 
seeker: Yeah, just become part of life I guess. Doesn't make it any better.

supporter: Are there any steps you can think of taking to express your frustrations with your husband? 
seeker: I have tried many times. It always ends up my fault in the end so I don't bother anymore and just take it.

supporter: It is easy to lose patience when the blame is always directed towards you. I am sorry that is occurring, but applaud you for your efforts in trying to express your frustration.
seeker: Thank you. It gets trying at times. Tonight, I just sit in the dark alone because it isn't worth the hassle.

supporter: I can tell from chatting with you that you are struggling and fed up with this situation because you are trying very hard in your marriage but get nothing but disrespect in return.
seeker: That is for sure. Most of the time it is just the way life is but there are days I get fed up and it irritates me. It has been this way for a while.

supporter: From what I have seen, if a situation like this continues, not only will you be consumed with anger towards your husband which will all come out at once, but it may also lead to divorce based on research I have read about.
seeker: I won't divorce...even if I am miserable, that isn't an option.
supporter: I understand. I would prefer to work out a situation rather than use divorce as an option as well, but I am concerned with how miserable you have become. 
seeker: I have gotten used to it. It is the way I am supposed to live my life I guess.

supporter: Some people respond to different strategies. You have tried communication through words to tell your husband your feelings, but have you shown him the consequences of his actions? Does he see how miserable you are? I suppose I wonder if you are interested in utilizing different strategies to find a solution to your issues with your husband and any others who may treat you badly. 
seeker: He knows I am miserable. He knows I am upset. He is the living room watching tv and I am in the bedroom. It doesn't bother him that I am upset. It is getting late where I am and I should probably go to bed soon.
supporter: Alright. I have enjoyed talking to you, and hope that things will work out for you. My last suggestion is possibly to try to talk your husband into couple's therapy and see how he responds. Even if he responds negatively, at least you have tried to dissolve the issue once again. In situations like this, remember even when you feel completely alone, that someone is looking out for you even if you do not realize it. Take a few calming deep breaths and engage in self-care, you deserve it. 
seeker: Thank you, good night.

supporter: You're welcome. Goodnight.

reading_text:
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hello! How are you doing today?
seeker: Hello, I'm having a very rough day, how are you?

supporter: I'm doing well, thank you! I'm sorry to hear that you're having a rough day. Do you mind me asking what happened to make you feel that way?
seeker: My mother passed away about a month ago due to alcoholism, it has been rough attempting to cope with the many different emotions.
supporter: I am so sorry to hear that. My brother suffers from alcoholism as well. I know how worrisome and difficult it can be. I still have a hard time dealing with my emotions. What different types of emotions are you feeling?
seeker: I'm so sorry that it's a situation that you can relate to, its such a hard situation watching someone drink their life away no matter what you do until they eventually pass away from it. I can say my anxiety has increased immensely as well as depression. It seems that quite a bit of pressure has been placed on me because of the family business she ran and my dad who is now trying to live without her.
supporter: Wow, that really is a lot to deal with. It seems as though you have a good understanding of what you're feeling but that you are trying to figure out how to move forward from here. It seems like you are trying to figure out how to work through your feelings as well as how to manage and deal with the pressure that has been put on you as a result. Does that sound accurate to you?
seeker: It definitely does, I know it feels like quite a bit now but will gradually become easier to deal with. 
supporter: That is a great attitude to have. I'm very proud of you for trying to stay positive and for reassuring yourself that it will become easier for you to deal with over time. You sound like an incredibly strong person!
seeker: Thank you so much! That means a lot just to hear and I think it is incredibly refreshing talking to someone that has a fresh mind about all of it rather than another family member that is attempting to cope with the same situation.
supporter: You're very welcome! I know from experience that it is usually best and much easier to talk to someone on the outside who doesn't know all of the ins and outs of what you are experiencing.
supporter: Have you considered any ways in which you could start to work through what you're feeling?
seeker: Very true, especially someone who is willing to listen and provide advice or positive conversation.
seeker: Yes, I have begun a new medication that will hopefully help soon, I have also begun focusing on different hobbies that I enjoy so that I can keep my mind busy.
supporter: It's great to hear that you are on a medication that will hopefully help you. Have you also considered speaking to an outpatient therapist or someone along those lines? That way, you could return to the same person as often as you feel necessary to continue to work through your feelings with someone who isn't directly involved with your situation.
supporter: I think that focusing on different hobbies that you enjoy is an incredible way to take your mind off of everything and to keep yourself busy! What types of hobbies are you into?
seeker: I haven't thought too much about it, but I do think it might be a great time and something that will be necessary in order for self healing and really to just express the up and down emotions that occur. 
seeker: I have recently fallen in love with wood working and different crafting. I enjoy being able to use my hands and become proud once i finish an accomplishment. 
supporter: I completely agree. I used to see a therapist. It was very difficult for me to do in the beginning, but once I got to know them, they provided me with coping strategies that otherwise, I never would have thought of. One of my favorites that he introduced me to was guided meditation. Have you ever heard of it?
seeker: I have not, I think if i feel that I can open up quickly, it would be extremely beneficial.
supporter: That sounds awesome! You should look into a relatively new craft called diamond painting. I started doing them back in 2018 and it completely turns my brain off from the outside world.
seeker: I have been looking at them recently and think I might just order one! Thank you for the advice!
supporter: You are very welcome! In my opinion, the best place to get one from to start with is Amazon. That way, you can get them in a few days as opposed to having to wait for weeks or months for them to arrive from other countries.

supporter: Hi. What brings you here today?

seeker: I am having a hard time with the realization that my once strong friendships are no longer as strong. I feel disconnected with them. The limitations the pandemic has set for all of us have been great. I am unsure if I will ever regain those friendships 

supporter: I understand that.  The pandemic has been very hard to keep connected with everyone. Have you tried talking to your friends about how you are feeling?
seeker: Yes, I have tried to message them daily, but the responses have always been clipped and or the response comes after couple days. I do feel other friendships have formed within each community, feeling a bit left out. I feel silly, like a teenage girl, who wants to be included. Just want to feel as though I am still part of their lives. 

supporter: It's completely normal to feel like that. I have been in your exact shoes.  I would suggest inviting one of them out for lunch or dinner and express face to face how you are feeling right now.
seeker: I was thinking the same thing, but I am unsure I feel awkward now, I feel like I do not them as I thought I did. I am unsure why I feel this way. one of them is my daughters god mother and the text are there but they are not like they use.. I am unsure if I should ask why she has time for others and not us... just saying it makes me feel weird

seeker: anyone there?

supporter: She may be going through something at home or having family issues.  We truly never know what the other person is going through unless we have that uncomfortable situation. My suggestion would be to rephrase that question slightly to her.  

seeker: I agree with you, just seems really strange since we were inseparable before the pandemic. I am also aware many are going through this situation just thought my friendships were stronger and distant would not be an issue. 

seeker: I will, never did I think I would hesitate whats going on.. 

supporter: It's completely natural.  Instead of texting her, have you tried calling?
seeker: Yes, I have. The conversation have been superficial, like small talk. There is nothing to share, I am guessing. My daughter has had lots of dance functions despite the pandemic and yet I have not felt supported. Perhaps shes not okay with venturing out during the pandemic.. though I do see on social media shes meeting other friends in social settings. 

seeker: Perhaps I need to be more open and not be so distant? Maybe its me and I am not seeing it?

supporter: How long have you been friends?

seeker: we are both 35 and we met in pre K. we are lifetime friends. shes a sister to me. At some point our parents use to live in the same apartment complex, our parents are great friends as well. 

seeker: I was there for her babies birth, when she found out what she was having. We have shared grand moments together. 

supporter: You both have been friends for such a long time.  I'm so jealous of friendships like that. I would definitely ask her for lunch.  You all have been through so much together. This conversation with her would be a weight off your shoulders.

I am an only child, and perhaps that makes me feel extremely unconfident. I am sure if asked, she would respond I am just being needy. eh, I will ask, since the pandemic ive only seen her once. 

supporter: I do not think she would respond that way at all. Once she sees that this has you concerned about your friendship, she will take it serious and open up to you.
seeker: You are right! thank you for the reinsurance. I hate that I am this way. 

seeker: you have helped me so much today, thank you for helping see things differently. 

supporter: I'm an only child as well so I understand how you are feeling :)

supporter: you are welcome! Glad I could help!
seeker: AWESOME! then you know the overwhelming need (sometimes) of being included. 

seeker: I think I have a plan, lunch and talk to her about how I am feeling, shes always been so understanding, I miss her babies so much.

supporter: Yes! It can be frustrating at times. But it sounds like you have a plan in order. You just need to execute it.
seeker: Yes, I do , thank you! have a wonderful weekend. 

supporter: You as well!

seeker: Hello... I am feeling quite anxious

supporter: Hi, I am very sorry to hear that.

supporter: What it is you are feeling anxious about?

seeker: CoVid and my job leave me worried every day


supporter: So you are feeling anxious about losing your job due to COVID, just to clarify.

seeker: Yes, I have been forced to work from home and I am unsure if my job will still be around in a month

seeker: I am worried I will lose my house if my job is eliminated

supporter: Just from the few messages we have exchanged I can tell this is making you very anxious. 

supporter: Have there been any lay off's at your job due to COVID?

seeker: It is making me anxious. There have been some layoffs in other departments.

seeker: And, some people who decided to go in the office a few days have gotten CoVid.

supporter: I completely understand that feeling, as I was also very worried about my job when the pandemic started, 

supporter: Have you spoken with your manager about this? It might help to get some clarification from your manager about your job security?

seeker: That is a good suggestion. I have actually been worried about the answer I would get or that I would get no real answer at all. 

seeker: the truth right now is scary

supporter: I understand being worried about that, but I definitely think getting some clarity would help you out in the long run. 

seeker: I may try that this week. I feel a bit better, but how long can this go on? So many people have lost jobs and are sick or dying. Two people in my building have died.

seeker: I think about lying in the hospital alone, no job, dying.

supporter: From the news I have seen the vaccine is coming soon and that is supposed to be very helpful to help get back to normal.

seeker: I hope that is true. I miss my workmates. They are good friends. We all want to see each other again and have our jobs.

supporter: I know it is a super tough time, but I know you can make it through it!

seeker: The worst days are when I keep the anxiety inside and don't talk much about how I feel. 

supporter: I have struggled with anxiety in the past as well and it definitely helps to talk to people about it. 

seeker: I really appreciate your assistance today. I feel better and will take some action this week. Thank you!

supporter: You're very welcome! Feel free to chat if you need anything else!

supporter: Hi, how are you doing today?

supporter: Good thank you. Why only ok? What is bothering you? 
seeker: Well 2020 is bothering me, like everyone else.. earlier this year my job was terminated, then for 3 months I was not bringing in income. Now that COVID is still out there, I fear that my current job will be terminated
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. 2020 has been tough for many, so you are not alone. 
supporter: I have been through a similar situation in the beginning of the year where I have lost my job. I was fearful but I kept thinking positive thoughts and it helped me get through tough times. 
seeker: True, I have been trying to think of other things I can do, like start a business
seeker: But I have been working for 20 years, that I feel like I am supposed to work for someone else and not for myself.
supporter: That is a great idea. The government has great support programs for new business owners like you. 
supporter: I think working for yourself is great. You can set your own hours, chart your own path. It would help with your employment situation for sure. 
seeker: I feel that I have not ideas.  I feel like i have been thinking about a business idea for myself and family for some time now.  I wonder how others decide on what to do
seeker: Like how to get that motivation in their head to start something really new 
supporter: My suggestion would be to think what your local neighborhood needs - maybe it is lacking a cafe or a grocery store?  
seeker: I know, i really want a niche company.. Something that no one has thought of, or is not yet in my community. 
supporter: Yes, I can identify with that. Motivation is hard - but think about your future job situation and your family. 
seeker: I would love to do a zero waste company or store, since that is what I am really into. 
seeker: Do you think it is hard to set up a business plan?
supporter: That's a great idea! Green is the new way to go! I believe in you.
seeker: Oh Thank You!

supporter: hello, how are you feeling today?

seeker: I am feeling really sad and lonely right now. My boyfriend and I broke up and it was me who wanted it but now I regret breaking up and he doesn't want me back.
supporter: I am sorry to hear that, I can understand when we think we want something and then we change our mind but it's too late.
seeker: That is exactly it. I broke up with him because I liked another person but then quickly realized that I made a mistake and it's too late. I want him back should I start calling and going to his house to beg?
supporter: nobody knows him better than you do, right now I do not think he is in a good place either since it wasn't his choice to end it, how do you think he would react if you started pressuring him?
 
seeker: I haven't really thought of that yet. He has a pretty short temper actually. I know he is really mad at me so I think he might want to yell at me and get his anger out before he could start being nice to me again. 
supporter: frustration and anger are common responses in situations like this, perhaps you can try a softer approach and let him know how you feel, without pressuring him into a response
seeker: Yeah, that's true. I have been secretly watching his social media and he has girls asking him out and I don't want to let them get to him before I can get him back. I want to make it up to him somehow and do whatever he wants to get back together.
supporter: you can always ask him calmly if he would like to talk, so you both have a chance to express your feelings in a safe way, with no yelling or arguing, do you think that's something he would do?
seeker: I can try that, I think he might be responsive at first if I dont set him off. All of his friends hate me so I have nobody on my side right now. Should I try to get his friends to like me again? Is that an way  I could use to get him to want me again?
supporter: nobody likes to see that one's friend is sad because of someone else, I think this is an issue that only the two of you can resolve, if he takes you back then his friends will take you back as well, but you need to make sure you want him back
seeker: I can understand what you mean. I need to think this through.
supporter: what made you like someone else in the first place?
seeker: Well, we are in a small town and he was popular and the cutest guy in our town. I liked being with someone so popular. He wasn't always nice to me and is why I wanted to be with someone else for a short time. He used to leave me at parties and go off with his friends sometimes.
supporter: was it a common thing that he didn't give you the attention you wanted?
seeker: My friends always said that I could do better and that he didn't deserve me. He gave me statis in our town and everyone wanted to be his girlfriend so I think I liked the attention, yes.
supporter: were you happy with him or were you happy that you were with the popular guy?
seeker: I really liked being with the popular guy who everyone looked up to. My parents don't like him at all and have wanted us to break up the whole time we were together.
supporter: it sounds to me like you liked the title more than the feeling of being with him, reflecting on your time together, would you do that again? 
seeker: I have never thought of it this way. You are making a lot of good points that I never thought of before. When I think about him I miss the way I felt in terms of being popular. I don't really miss him as a person.
supporter: popularity in my opinion, it's just an opinion (I hope I make sense) but think about how you'd like to be treated and how you want to feel when you are with someone, because at the end of the day it's your feelings and your happiness, I wish you the best of luck.

supporter: Hello there how can I help?
seeker: I'm feeling so worried about the COVID-19 crisis.

supporter: So you feel anxiety about this whole COVID-19 epidemic?
seeker: Yes, I'm particularly worried about my parents. One is on oxygen at night, but he still doesn't want to listen about not going in crowds.

supporter: Oh well I understand your concern then.  As a son or daughter it is certainly reasonable to be concerned about your parents especially as they grow older.  I have a similar situation with my own mother.
seeker: I just don't know what more to do.
supporter: Well first of all, you have to take care of yourself because if you don't you can't help them.  So just take a moment to close your eyes and take some deep breaths and realize you stressing is probably going to make them stress.
seeker: That is helpful information.  What can I tell them?
supporter: Well if you can get some concrete info such as from the CDC and John Hopkins showing case counts in your area.  Show them graphs so they can visually see the impact.  Also if you can get a hold of their doctor yourself, see if you can convince them to give your parents a call, say to check on them and give them some advice.
seeker: That sounds like a good plan.  Is there anything else I can do to decrease the anxiety for me?

supporter: Don't get absorbed in the numbers, it can drive you crazy.  Also if you are using social media like twitter and getting inundated with info, remember a lot of it is fake.  I would suggest limiting exposure for a little while just to get you fixed a little bit, if that makes sense. 
seeker: Do you think there are some good social media sites that could help?

supporter: Not particularly social media because it open to everyone, just pick and choose where you choose to get info from.  The CDC is a great resource as well as the John Hopkins site which has been tracking since the beginning.   Everybody has a couple of news outlets they trust, use those.
seeker: How can I cope with limiting my visits with my parents because I am afraid to spread COVID?

supporter: First of all you are not alone.  but don't let them see you anxious for sure.  You can also show them if they can how to do video visits.  You can do that all the time, even phone calls every day.  It means a lot.
seeker: That makes sense.  I appreciate the suggestions.  How can I show them the kids care too?

supporter: Nothing will make grandparents smile more than seeing their grandkids on a video call.  If you don't want to bring them when you physically visit have them record themselves on your phone as an example.
seeker: Maybe I can send them some pictures too.  Nothing like a great big hug, but for now some video chats and pictures or recordings may help.  I'm starting to feel a little more relief.

supporter: Of course.  I don't know if they dressed up for Halloween, but see if they want to dress up and take some pictures for grandma.  Pictures and voice and video are wonderful in these times.
seeker: Thank you so much for helping.  I think I can use your advice.  Take care and have a great day!  
supporter: You too, I hope I helped.  Take care!

supporter: Of course, Charlotte. I'm here for you. What's been happening?

seeker: Yeah, it seems like things have piled up since last fall, like the panic attack at work and the extended hours.
supporter: Those were significant challenges. And I remember your workload and social conflicts taking a toll on you. How are you managing those feeling now?

supporter: Recovery has its ups and downs. It's very brave of you to acknowledge where you're at. Maybe focusing on your victories, like forming new friendships, can help you move forward.
seeker: That's true. This new friend has been understanding. We both need a fresh start this year, and it's comforting to know I'm not alone in this.
supporter: It's wonderful to have someone who comprehends what you're going through. Have you considered if they might be open to sharing support with each other?
seeker: We have talked a lot, and it seems like we're both open to supportive friendship. It's nice to feel connected like that.
supporter: That's so key—to have someone to lean on. Think of them as a partner in your journey. It's also important to continue prioritizing your mental well-being.
seeker: You're right. I need to keep working through this with therapy and allow myself to enjoy new experiences.
supporter: Absolutely. Celebrate the steps you've taken already. It’s okay to lean on friends for support, and accepting help doesn’t mean you’re not strong.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter after talking with you.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself, Charlotte.

seeker: Hey there, is it okay to talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed with emotions right now.
supporter: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on lately?
seeker: It's Nate, my ex. He reached out to apologize recently, and it's stirred up a lot of old memories and feelings.
supporter: I can imagine that must be really tough. How did it feel when he reached out to you?
seeker: Confusing, honestly. Part of me was glad he apologized, but another part isn't sure if I can trust his intentions.
supporter: That's completely valid. Trust can be hard to rebuild, especially after everything you've been through.
seeker: Exactly. I keep thinking about our past arguments and how they made me feel. It's all just resurfacing now.
supporter: It sounds like those memories are really triggering some deep emotions. How are you handling them right now?
seeker: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Between the pressure from studies and your relationship history, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot.

seeker: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.
supporter: Imposter syndrome is really tough to deal with. Just remember, your voice is unique and valuable in its own right.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me. I often forget that when I'm deep in self-doubt. It means a lot to have your support.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Taylor. Make sure to be kind to yourself and take things one day at a time. You're doing your best.
seeker: Thanks. I really needed to hear that. I’ll try to focus on what's within my control and take small steps forward.
supporter: That's a great approach. You're stronger than you realize, and I'm proud of you for reaching out and talking this through.
seeker: I appreciate it. It feels good to get everything off my chest and know I'm not facing this alone.

supporter: It is OK to ask for help. Many people do it every day. You deserve to be heard.

supporter: You have a wonderful dedication to your children, I can tell.

supporter: I found a lot of chat boards and information from a google search. You are not alone and it is OK to feel and to be going through this. 
seeker: I think you are provided me with valuable help and advice..I appreciate it..Thank you..I think I can exit the chat?what do you say?
supporter: Your are welcome and I wish you the best in life. You can exit if you wish. 
seeker: sure.bye.
supporter: bye

seeker: HI, I need help, I have been feeling very down lately.
supporter: Okay, how can I help you?

seeker: I just wanted to talk to someone.
supporter: Is there anything particular that has got you feeling down lately?
seeker: I feel like I am in a rut.  
supporter: Its always good to have someone to talk to, I am happy to help. I have felt stuck many times, so i can understand that.
seeker: What did you do to get out of the rut.
supporter: Well I had to sit down and think about why I was stuck and tried to come up with as many options as I could to be unstuck, then i put them in order based on which I thought would work best. It took quite a few of them, but I did finally get unstuck.

seeker: I can try doing that.
supporter: Every one is different, but it is worth a shot, might help the rut your having, might also give you new ideas that will help you decide on how to not feel like your in a rut anymore. Sometimes just talking to someone can help too, bouncing ideas off of each other can help in some cases.
seeker: True,  I have been avoiding most people. 
supporter: Its hard to talk about certain problems, so I can't blame you, however you can get some good ideas from others. You might have just needed some space to evaluate your situation, nothing wrong with taking a break from things or people if it helps you.
seeker: I will try reaching out to my sister tomorrow.  maybe she can help.
seeker: I also feel embarrassed that I feel so unhappy. 
supporter: From chatting with you I can tell you might be ready to start talking and maybe get some help or advice, family is a great start they are typically a great support system. It is okay to feel embarrassed but being unhappy will eat at you, sometimes its good to set our pride aside so that we can figure things out. In my situation of feeling stuck I was ashamed that I sat and let people treat me so badly but it wasn't until I seen it as a problem that I started making my lists and getting advice. Some things we do on our own and some its good to have people to help. I think reaching out to your sister would be worth a try, she might also have different ideas and suggestions you haven'
t thought of yet.
seeker: Thanks, you have been a lot of help.
supporter: Thank you for chatting with me, I am glad to help. I hope you have a great day! Stay positive!
seeker: I will try and you have a nice day too.
seeker: Bye
supporter: If you need to chat again I would be glad to talk to you, I think you will do great at fixing your rut. Thank you. 
supporter: Bye.

supporter: Hello there, how are you today?
seeker: Hi, Thanks for talking to me today. I've been so upset about my boyfriend breaking up with me.  It was so unexpected.

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. When did he break up with you?
seeker: He texted me yesterday!  Can you believe that?  We've been together a year and he broke up with me by texting me!!!  He couldn't even do it face to face!

supporter: That seems very cowardly to break up with you over text after being together for a year. 
seeker: Yes, I thought so too!  He knew I'd be upset and he didn't want to deal with me I guess.  He knew I wanted to get married some day from the very start.  He knew it didn't have to be soon.  I'm still in college.  I just want to know that he wants marriage some day but he decided that marriage is an institution he doesn't believe in.

supporter: That is a shame. I can understand his perspective if marriage is not something he wanted but it seems hurtful to string you along in  a relationship if your life goals were very different. Was your differing opinions on marriage the only reason he gave?
seeker: Yes, It was completely unexpected because things with us were going great.  I was completely blindsided.  We hadn't even talked about marriage lately.  He just knew that it was something that I wanted in the future.

supporter: That sounds very difficult. How have you been coping with the break up?
seeker: I've just been crying and laying in bed.  I called off work today.  I don't want to see anyone right now.

supporter: I think this is to be expected from a very fresh break-up. I know that when I broke up with my partner, I spent at least a few days crying and trying to figure out what my life would be now.
seeker: How 'd you get over it?

supporter: I tried to focus on other areas of my life and to critically reflect on my relationship. Largely, I threw myself into my work and tried to better that aspect of my life, and hung out with people that I knew cared about me. Both of those are very good distractions which you might be able to use.
seeker: Maybe calling off work was a bad idea...  all I'm going to do is think about this instead of doing something to take my mind off of it...

supporter: I think one day off to get the crying out of your system is a good emotional cleanse. We all need time to self care and look after our emotions. Maybe going for a walk or doing some yoga, to place your focus on something rather than being boxed into a room may help to shift your focus.
seeker: I think I'm going to get out of bed and do something to take my mind off of this .  Thanks for chatting with me today!

seeker: I think I'm going to do that!  There is a park by my house that I'm going to go for a walk in!  Some fresh air might be good for me!

supporter: You are more than welcome. I hope that you feel better by being outside. 
seeker: Thanks!  I hope so too!

supporter: I'm glad you feel open to discussing it. Remember, I'm here if you ever need to talk or vent. You're not alone in this.

supporter: Times are very tough right now. It's pretty crazy how covid has impacted everything.

supporter: It doesn't have to be much but even just a little conversation can go a long way

seeker: Thanks for your help. I appreciate you.

supporter: No problem. I hope you feel better.

supporter: Hello, my name is Sharon, how are you today?
seeker: Hello. I am sad because my job is not rewarding. It is a dead-end job and I feel shameful anymore. I don't like talking about my job with anyone since it is so pointless.
seeker: Hi Sharon. I'm Larry.

supporter: Hi Larry.  What sort of job do you do?
seeker: I am a maintenance supervisor in a manufacturing facility.
supporter: I have had jobs that seemed pointless as well.   I was a sales assistant in a store constantly waiting for customers, it was boring!  Just a paycheque with no fulfillment.  I found it depressing as well.
supporter: So it sounds like you are finding no point to going in to work, and it's making you feel sad, am I correct?
seeker: Yes that is a very good summary of what is going on. And I am glad to see you can relate. While I am lucky to not work in sales since I know those jobs are extremely tough but the lack of reward is all the same.
supporter: Are there other jobs available in your area that you could apply for that are more up your alley?
seeker: I have not seen anything worth jumping ship for. I am afraid of the old adage of the grass always looks greener from the other side of the fence. Meaning I leave this job and only find a worse job.
supporter: I see., yes that could be a risk for sure.have you spoken to your manager to see if there may be other opportunities in the manufacturing facility for you?   I bet they would rather retrain you for a different position than lose you.
seeker: Unfortunately there are no other positions at the place I work. Yes my boss is very well aware of how unhappy I am. He is also unhappy and has been looking for jobs too. It isn't that great of a place to work at. I have had 3 different friends leave my place of employment, I've just been to lazy to leave too. It's a catch 22, too lazy to leave but due to feeling sad from being here I don't have the energy to try to leave.
supporter: Yes I can understand that.  Sadness and depresion can lead one to feel depleted and lacking motivation to make change.  
supporter: I have been depressed and lacking motivation in the past, I remember how it felt.
seeker: Yes, I see a psychologist and she does her best to help me but ultimately it is up to me to make the changes I need to in life.
supporter: Is there anything about your position that you could suggest improving to your boss, to make your job more interesting?   Maybe some ideas you may have for streamlining the work or somethings?
supporter: I'm glad to hear you have someone to talk to about it.   Over time as you keep working on it I hope things will improve for you.
seeker: I've spoke things over with my boss, he has tried a few things. Currently we are in a holding pattern due to some upper management changes and we are awaiting to see how the new manager would like to run things.
supporter: oh I see.  Do you have hobbies outside of work that you find fulfilling?
seeker: I have been slacking on that too. Just don't find pleasure in anything anymore. Now that it is spring time though hopefully that changes. 
supporter: Lets hope the new manager improves things for you, it sounds like there is a ray of hope there!
supporter: Yes it's hard to get started on anything when we are down.  I remember writing lists with very small goals on them.  Small goals feel like mountains when we are down!   Then I would work my way through that very short list and check things off if I could do them, which gave me a small lift of accomplishment.
seeker: I should start writing lists. I know that is a great tool for helping.
supporter: Lets hope the new manager can improve things.   And your work with the psychologist is very positive, it's great you reached out for help, that is a strength.   You've spoken with your boss.   You are doing all the right things.
seeker: Thank you for the encouragement .
supporter: you're very welcome, it's been a pleasure talking with you Larry.

seeker: Thank you for your help Sharon. Have a good day.
supporter: you too!  take good care of yourself, bye

supporter: Hi there, how are we doing today?
seeker: Okay how are you?
supporter: Im doing great thanks. Anything on your mind today?
seeker: Just pondering microcheating and wondering why someone who I do not like that way would be considered microcheating
supporter: And what do you mean by microcheating?
seeker: It is a new thing like having a man you like that you check up on on social media even though you are in a relationship, or eating lunch with the same woman or man that you like but you don't act on because you are married. 
supporter: Oh i see, well i think overthinking things like that can lead to unwanted emotions. Or putting yourself in a situation with another person when you are in a relationship might mean there are other issues going on.
seeker: Yes i see that. No nothing else going on just thinking that the definition maybe shouldn't be as exact for the type of person that I do not talk to because of his reservations about it.
supporter: Well, if you are not talking to them then i see no harm. If you are talking to them with some sort of intention to for a relationship beyond friendship then i see issues arising.
seeker: That is what I feel. I am not talking to him. I had to the other day to get in contact with someone(medical emergency) but do not call just to chat and catch up. I even unfriended him. I just want to comfort him over it but I think it is best just to never speak of him again. 
seeker: Comfort my fiance 
supporter: To never speak to your fiance?
supporter: If you want to continue your relationship and you do not feel you can continue a platonic relationship with this other person then that might be best.
seeker: No I am ending my friendship with him. That is what is best.
supporter: I think it might be as well if you cannot control it. I do have to ask though, are you happy with your Fiance?
seeker: Yes very.
supporter: Then i 100% back you on your decision. Id take this time to focus on you too. Strengthen the bond a bit.
seeker: Yes, I think that would be best. I thank you for your time. 
supporter: I thank you for opening up!
seeker: It is okay see talking about this is actually microcheating. So now I am worried about that.
supporter: I really wouldnt even consider it cheating to have feelings. Acting on them or trying to strengthen them may be though.
seeker: Yes that is true. My fiance is over seas for work for the next 13 mos so I am here in the states alone. We get to talk but he isnt here with me so having no one to talk to is lonely. 
seeker: That is why I brought it up.
supporter: I see that, have you tried to talk to your friends about this issue? Or even try a therapist? Maybe you and your Fiance can figure out more times to talk with facetime or zoom. Do a virtual date night.
seeker: Yes I don't have any friend that arent men so I think therapy is going to help. I don't talk to anyone anymore. But I thank you for your time. I just wanted to clarify why I brought it up. I hope you have a good day.
supporter: I hope you do as well!
seeker: thank you

seeker: Hi. 

seeker: I'm anxious and depressed.

seeker: Is anyone there?

supporter: im here
seeker: Hi. I'm anxious and a bit depressed.

supporter: what made you feel this way?
seeker: The pressures of Covid and taking care of my disabled sister are just getting to me. 

supporter: i see how that could make you a bit anxious. I get the same way also.
seeker: Thanks. I'm just tired of the Covid restrictions. I can't wait for things to get back to normal. 

supporter: i feel the same. being on lockdown could make anyone a little crazy
supporter: do you have family or friends that you could reach out to over the phone?
seeker: I do. My other sister is always a big help. Maybe I should text her more often?

supporter: yes! that would always be a good idea. its always comforting to hear from a loved one.
supporter: i myself yearn for a good call from family or even hearing someone close voice. always makes me smile.
seeker: That's true. I tend to stew on my thoughts. 

supporter: hows the weather where you are?
seeker: It's not too bad. Cloudy and 40 which is pretty good for this time of year. How's your weather?

supporter: i live in the south . not cold yet. but your weather sounds like it would be nice for a lovely walk.

seeker: Exercise does always help. I walk/jog five miles every day. I generally feel my best right after that. Don't you find that true too?

supporter: yes! although i probably couldnt walk nor run 5 miles a day. i love getting out to enjoy nature. it always helps to keep mind off things. does that usually work for you?
seeker: Yes, I love nature but I live in a congested suburb. It would take me awhile to get out to the country. That's why Covid is so tough - I can't travel which is my main form of relaxation. What do you do to relax?

supporter: i see, for me to relax. i find sitting back in my recliner reading a nice book always relaxes me. i also love yoga. its a refreshing relaxtion
seeker: I should try yoga. I sometimes do breathing exercises when I get really stressed. Maybe I should go back to it. What do you think?
supporter: actually that would be a good idea. i find yoga and breathing deep help relieve stress & let go of the negative.
seeker: I think I'll try it. Thanks! It was good talking to you. I think we completed the requirements. Have a good Thanksgiving and stay safe out there. Bye!
supporter: you too always :-)
seeker: Thanks!

supporter: Hey Sarah, how are you doing today?
seeker: Hi, I'm feeling pretty anxious after a tense meeting with my new boss.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. What about the meeting made you feel anxious?
seeker: Well, it was really intense. The new boss seemed very critical, and it brought back a lot of anxiety about leadership at work after my previous boss resigned. I'm worried about the changes.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. It's understandable that you'd feel uneasy, especially after everything that happened with your last boss. Do you feel like this new boss might have a similar impact on your work environment?
seeker: I hope not. But it's hard not to worry, especially since I'm still trying to process everything that happened before, including the harassment issues.
supporter: It's upsetting when past events continue to affect you. It sounds like you're still carrying a lot from before. How has your therapy been helping with those feelings?
seeker: Therapy has been helpful, but sometimes it feels like progress is slow. My therapist says I need to be patient, but it's tough when these feelings keep resurfacing.
supporter: I understand how frustrating that can be. It sounds like you're doing your best and are committed to your growth. Have you been able to talk to your new boss about any of your concerns?
seeker: Not really, I'm afraid of confrontation. Every time I think about bringing it up, I worry it might make things worse or be misunderstood.
supporter: It's normal to feel hesitant about that. Maybe starting with small, non-confrontational conversations could help build some rapport first?
seeker: That's a good idea. I think finding common ground could make it easier to approach issues later. I just need to overcome my initial discomfort.
supporter: It sounds like a wise approach. Taking things step by step at work can make it seem less overwhelming. Remember, you're not alone in feeling this way.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. It helps to hear I'm not alone. I'll try working on small conversations and see how it goes from there.
supporter: I'm glad to hear you're feeling a bit better about it. In the meantime, how's everything else going in your life, like things with your partner or your friend?
seeker: Things with my partner, Jack, have been a mix. We're still working on giving each other space, which is challenging. With my friend, it's been hard because I worry about her a lot.
supporter: Navigating space in a relationship is definitely tricky. It's great that you both are trying to work it out. And it's natural to worry about a friend in crisis—just remember to take care of yourself too.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement. I'm trying to find balance in all these areas. It's just that some days are harder than others.
supporter: You're showing a lot of resilience, Sarah. I believe in your ability to manage these challenges. Please reach out anytime you need to talk more.

supporter: Hi Linda, how are you feeling today?
seeker: Hey, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed at the moment.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to share what's been going on?
seeker: It's been a lot at work. The pressure has really been getting to me lately, and I actually had a panic attack a few days ago.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Panic attacks can be so frightening. Have you been able to talk to anyone about it?
seeker: I mentioned it to David. He's been there for me, but sometimes I feel like it's unfair to burden him with my issues.
supporter: It's great that David is supportive, but remember, your feelings and experiences are valid, and it's okay to lean on him during tough times.
seeker: Thank you. I just wish I could manage my stress better. I thought adopting Buddy would help, but I still find myself feeling anxious.
supporter: Pets can be comforting, but it's understandable to still feel anxious, especially with work pressures piling up. Have you had a chance to take any breaks or do something relaxing lately?
seeker: Not really. The deadlines are so tight, and I'm constantly worried about falling behind.
supporter: I can imagine that makes it hard to decompress. Perhaps finding small moments in the day for yourself could help, even if it's just a few minutes.
seeker: That might be worth trying. Maybe a short walk with Buddy could help clear my head.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Buddy would probably love that too!
seeker: Yeah, he probably would. I also think I need to re-evaluate how I'm handling work stress. This panic attack was a wake-up call.
supporter: It's impressive that you're reflecting on this and considering changes. Recognizing the need for balance is such a big step.
seeker: Thank you. I really appreciate the encouragement. I also need to find a way to mend things with Lily. Our argument has been weighing on me too.
supporter: Family dynamics can be challenging, especially after a disagreement. It's understandable you're feeling down about it.
seeker: Yeah, I hope I can find a way to apologize and move forward. I've been hesitant to reach out.
supporter: Taking the first step can be daunting, but it could lead to healing for both of you. Maybe just starting with a message to say you miss her could open the door.
seeker: That's a good idea. I'll try to write her something sincere. I really hope we can patch things up.
supporter: Your willingness to reconcile shows just how much you value your relationship with her. I'm hopeful for you both.
seeker: Thanks. It means a lot to have someone to talk to about all this. I'm feeling a bit more hopeful now.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that, Linda. Remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk. You've got this!

supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I just need help deciding what to do.
supporter: What are you contemplating for?
seeker: I was doing okay in school, but when we had go virtual, I lost all my friends. 
seeker: I want to quit school and just go home. But my parents would not be happy. 
supporter: why do you think so?
seeker: I don't see anyone but my roommate and she has a boyfriend. I'm so lonely!
supporter: How about joining a club at school to know more people?
seeker: We are in a lockdown because of COVID. So the clubs are not doing anything. 
seeker: I know I'm not the only one feeling this way.

supporter: So you're stuck with your roommate but she doesn't care about you?
seeker: She's just busy with her boyfriend. They go out on hikes and stuff, but they just want to go by themselves. I'm just on my own all the time.

supporter: Everyone feels that, and it's totally normal. Don't be too harsh on yourself
seeker: Do you think I should quit school and start again next fall?

supporter: Why don't you do something on your own? Read a book, do some crafts?
supporter: I don't think you should do that. Who knows how next year's gonna look like? It might be even worse
seeker: I have. I've worked on my schoolwork, but it has been very easy. I also paint. But I need people. 
seeker: At home, I had all my friends around. Of course, we weren't in a pandemic then.

seeker: This pandemic is making everyone feel lonely I think.

supporter: How about doing video call with your friends at home?
seeker: I hadn't thought about that!  They are all at different schools, but maybe I can do a Zoom meeting for all of us.

supporter: I totally feel you, I feel stressed out and very uncertain throughout this pandemic. You are not alone
seeker: I guess my friends may be feeling stressed too. Maybe I'll try and start a Zoom party!  We could plan a time and wear pajamas and just sit and talk. 
supporter: Exactly, I do virtual happy hour with my friends every month
seeker: That sounds like fun!  

seeker: Why don't you do a virtual happy hour every week?

supporter: Not only that, when you feel lonely, text your friends and share it with them or your family
supporter: Oh I am too busy to do that once a week. All of us are actually
seeker: I have been afraid to tell my parents how I'm feeling. I don't want them to worry about me.

seeker: I want them to know I'm lonely, but not freak out about it :-)

supporter: I don't think so. Maybe they are waiting for you to say first and give you advice, they have more experience after all
seeker: That's true. And I do know my mom is working from home now and she's a really social person. It's probably getting to her too.

supporter: if that's the case, you can use this chance to be there for her. I think talking to your mom will help you both
seeker: Yes, I'll probably call her and my dad tonight. I'll let them know I'm a bit sad and lonely, but not so much that they worry. And then I'll start planning my virtual party with my friends!

supporter: Sounds like a great plan. I believe you can overcome this together
seeker: At least the party will give me something to look forward to!

supporter: Yes, right now I'm trying to teach myself one day at a time mindset
seeker: That seems like a smart thing to do. None of us can really do anything to make the pandemic go away. We just have to get through it one day at a time.  

seeker: Thank you for helping me come up with a plan!

supporter: That's the right mindset. I 'm glad I could be some help
seeker: Enjoy the rest of your night!

supporter: you too

seeker: Can you help me?
supporter: sure, what seems to be the problem
seeker: I can't figure out why my friends don't understand why I want to keep a bit distant during COVID

supporter: I had the same issue with my friends as well
seeker: Really?  What happened?
supporter: We stopped getting together and going out places cause they were all closed
seeker: Yes, that happened here.  But they still wanted to come over despite government orders limiting gatherings.
supporter: We now have weekly video call meetings instead, it helps us stay connected
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Is it hard to do?

supporter: Not at all, we use a program called Skype, that's free. You can use it on your phone or PC
seeker: My friends want to go out all the time.  How can we connect during a Skype?
supporter: Pick a time you'll both be available, and you'll both need the program. It's quite easy to use and there will be youtube videos that'll help you set it up, should you need it
seeker: Do you do any activities together over Skype?
supporter: We usually just chat about our week or get advice on normal things, sometimes we'll play a drinking game and be goofy together. 
seeker: Are there other games people can play together on Skype because I don't drink?
supporter: Drinking isn't a requirement, usually we'll just chat if we don't feel like drinking
seeker: I just want to connect and please my friends but it is hard to not have any physical contact and only be online.
supporter: I can understand that and it's definitely frustrating. But it'll be so much better once you can see other other again, cause absence makes the heart grow fonder
seeker: Wow, I didn't think of it that way.  That puts a positive twist on it.
supporter: Yes, I always like to look for the positive in any given situation
seeker: Thanks for your help.  I feel a lot better.

seeker: Hi

supporter: hello. How are you?
seeker: I'm honestly having a rough time

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me about it?
seeker: Sure. I just lost my job and school is out so I feel like I have lost purpose

supporter: Thank you for telling me. I'm sorry to hear that. What did you do for your job?
seeker: I was a manager of a retail store that closed. 

supporter: I see.  That's a very important role for any business. I bet there are numerous other retailers out there looking for a good manager to hire.
seeker: That is true, I am just not sure if that is what I want to do anymore

supporter: I see. Well then, if this helps.  The store closing might have been a positive thing, so you could find your next passion. 
seeker: That is a good point. 

supporter: I will also add, that being a Manager means you have some very important skills that would translate well to your next job, or anything you decide to do.
seeker: That's true. I know the experience will help me but I still miss it 

supporter: Also, let's say you decided to work for another company, something new, outside of retail. Because you were a manager, you could also be promoted more quickly because of your management experience. 
seeker: That is also true. I guess I just need to decide what I want to do now. That is probably the most difficult part. 

supporter: Yes, it sounds like a part of you still misses the retail environment. I see that too. My best advice, is take a few days to think about what you really want to do.  Think about what you are skilled at. Then decide which route you want to go.  I know there will be numerous options out there for you in retail management, but if you wanted to do something different, there will be opportunities there too. Because you have options, you will likely pick the choice that will be most fulfilling for you, in something you will be passionate about - so this will likely be very positive for you. 
seeker: That is really nice to say. I guess I am also just scared to go for something and have it not be as fulfilling as I thought

supporter: that's possible. but you will have plenty of options either way. Could be a different retail store, or something new. 
seeker: Yeah. It is a big decision, though. Thanks for talking it out with me

supporter: Yes, of course. Take some time to think it through. Weigh your options, and the pros and cons of each. Then pick the option that will be the most rewarding for you. 
seeker: Sounds like a great plan. Thanks again!

supporter: Thank you for talking with me. 
seeker: Bye
